BURBANK, CA — Today, August 31, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) celebrated the official phase out of paraquat in California after every manufacturer of products containing the toxic ingredient voluntarily agreed to pull them from the market. The phase-out is the direct result of legislation Friedman authored in the California Assembly which forced state regulators to fast-track a scientific review the pesticide industry had fought for years to delay.

“Today, California reasserts itself as a leader in protecting the health of its residents by eliminating the highly toxic chemical paraquat,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “I will continue to do everything I can to protect Americans from harmful chemicals, especially in our air, water, and soil.”

HOW FRIEDMAN'S BILL FORCED THE PHASE-OUT:

AB 1963, signed into law in September 2024, required the California Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) to complete a formal scientific reevaluation of paraquat by January 1, 2029 — dramatically faster than the department's typical pace, with some reviews dragging on for more than two decades.

DPR opened the reevaluation in November 2024 and released two preliminary scientific assessments that identified harms to the thyroid system, links to birth defects, and significant risks to wildlife.

Because of AB 1963, DPR’s reevaluation gave it the authority to require manufacturers to submit new studies. They set a deadline of June 5, 2026 for pesticide manufacturers(?) to fill newly-identified gaps in the agency’s human health toxicology database.

Instead of submitting the data, manufacturers began cancelling their California registrations in April 2026. The last registrant cancelled on August 6, 2026 — triggering the statewide phase-out of DPR announced on August 10.

Paraquat is one of the most widely-used herbicides in the United States and is applied to almonds, pistachios, grapes, pomegranates, cotton, and other crops. It is so dangerous that only licensed applicators may use it. Scientific research has linked paraquat exposure to Parkinson's disease, childhood leukemia, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, thyroid disease, and birth defects.

Friedman has a track record of protecting Californians from exposure to harmful chemicals. In the California Assembly, she authored legislation to ban PFAS (known as “Forever Chemicals”) in cosmetic, personal care, and juvenile products like cribs and car seats sold in California. In Congress, Friedman is a co-lead of the bipartisan No PFAS in Cosmetics Act with Representatives Debbie Dingell (MI-6) and Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-1). The legislation bans the use of PFAS in cosmetic products sold nationwide.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representatives James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), a Member of the Committee on Homeland Security, and Bennie G. Thompson (D-MS), Ranking Member of the Committee on Homeland Security, led Committee Democrats in sending a letter to Acting Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Director David Venturella demanding answers after ICE awarded a $16.7 million sole-source contract for 6,000 electric shock gloves despite warnings that such devices can lead to serious injury or death.

The Members raised concerns that ICE plans to use the gloves on individuals in custody and for crowd control despite the agency’s alarming record of violence and misuse of force.

“Incorrectly labeling migrants who largely have no criminal record as inmates and associating them with aggression shows that ICE does not intend to use the G.L.O.V.E. for de-escalation, but rather as nothing more than another weapon in ICE’s arsenal,” the Members wrote. “Furthermore, it is alarming that ICE also intends to use the G.L.O.V.E. for crowd control by ‘[a]ssisting crowd control units in moving groups or denying access to areas.’”

The Members are demanding ICE provide records related to the sole-source contract, communications with Compliant Technologies, plans for distributing the gloves, policies governing their use, training materials, and reporting requirements.

To read the full letter, click here.

WASHINGTON, DC (August 30, 2026) — Today, NASA, in partnership with SpaceX, successfully launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Named for NASA's first chief astronomer, the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, or “Roman,” is NASA’s newest flagship observatory. It is designed to explore the universe, addressing some of the most important science questions identified by the astronomy community. Roman was the top priority large mission of the 2010 Astronomy and Astrophysics Decadal Survey. One exposure from Roman’s primary instrument will capture over 100 times the area of the sky as an exposure from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope.

“Congratulations to NASA and its partners on this outstanding achievement,” said Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren. “The Nancy Grace Roman Telescope will give humanity a grand encompassing view of our galaxy and will shape the next generation of space exploration. It is because of sustained federal support that we are able to achieve missions of such magnitude. This launch would not have been possible without the thousands of employees supporting the Roman mission across NASA’s centers who have been working tirelessly to make this mission a success. I thank them for their dedication. Roman will allow scientists to explore never before seen galaxies, investigate dark matter and black holes, and catalogue new planets around stars outside of our own solar system. I look forward to closely following Roman’s journey to its final orbit and the commissioning of the observatory ahead of starting science operations.”
title: Ranking Members Lofgren, Foushee Congratulate NASA and Partners After Successful Nancy Grace Roman Telescope Launch

WASHINGTON — This week, Representative Lauren Underwood announced a new round of federal funding she has secured for nursing education, health care, child care, research, airport improvements, and quantum computing supply chain and manufacturing development in northern Illinois.

As a member of the Appropriations Committee, Underwood has made securing federal resources for our community a top priority. The following funds will support programs in the 14th District with federal resources:

Head Start, Joliet, Illinois – $1,946,280

Head Start in Joliet has been awarded $1,946,280 in federal funding through the Administration for Children and Families at the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).

This grant supports Early Head Start Child Care Partnerships, programs designed to enhance and support early learning settings to provide comprehensive and continuous services. These programs increase access to high-quality, full-day, full-year child care, including family child care, for low-income working families.

Family Service Agency of DeKalb County, Inc, DeKalb, Illinois – $582,504

The Family Service Agency of DeKalb County has been awarded $582,504 in federal funding through the Administration for Children and Families at the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).

This grant supports programming that provides homeless youth with supervised transitional housing, case management, independent service planning, counseling, and developing life skills.

Will County Community Health Center, Will County, Illinois – $1,153,424

The Will County Community Health Center has been awarded $1,153,424 in federal funding through the Health Resources and Services Administration’s (HRSA) Health Center Program (H80).

This grant supports health centers that treat medically underserved communities.

City of Mendota, Mendota, Illinois – $375,000

The City of Mendota has been awarded $375,000 in federal funding administered through the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration at the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).

This grant expands the availability of substance abuse treatment and recovery services available to Americans to improve the lives of those affected by alcohol and drug addictions, and to reduce the impact of alcohol and drug abuse on individuals, families, communities. The funding also addresses priority mental health needs of regional and national significance and assists children in dealing with violence and traumatic events through by funding grant and cooperative agreement projects.

University of St. Francis, Joliet, Illinois – $337,661

The University of St. Francis has been awarded $337,661 in federal funding through the Health Resources and Services Administration’s (HRSA) Advanced Nursing Education Workforce (ANEW) program.

This grant supports the training and graduation of advanced practice registered nursing (APRN) students/trainees in these disciplines. The grant provides awardees with funding for tuition and other eligible supports to build academic-clinical partnerships to facilitate clinical training, and continue to develop and sustain clinical faculty and preceptors as needed. The program seeks to increase the number of primary care nurse practitioners, clinical nurse specialists, and certified nurse midwives trained and prepared to provide primary care services, mental health and substance use disorder care, and/or maternal health care.

Lewis University, Romeoville, Illinois – $218,502

The University of St. Francis has been awarded $218,502 in federal funding through the National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Division of Undergraduate Education.

This project aims to serve the national interest of training the next generation of scientists by helping faculty access and implement evidence-based laboratory teaching practices. Chemistry laboratory training is a central component of all undergraduate degrees in STEM fields. These hands-on experiences will push students to apply theoretical ideas, deepen their understanding, and develop the skills necessary for success in future STEM careers.

Aurora University, Aurora, Illinois – $396,032

Aurora University has been awarded $396,032 in federal funding through the National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Division of Undergraduate Education.

This project seeks to serve the national interest by helping undergraduate students learn chemistry in ways that reflect how modern science is practiced. Computation, data analysis, modeling, and simulation are now central to chemistry research and many STEM careers. Yet chemistry courses often emphasize step-by-step procedures and calculations rather than computational problem solving. This gap is especially important in general chemistry, an introductory course that enrolls large numbers of students and influences persistence in STEM pathways.

Lewis University Airport, Romeoville, Illinois – $444,673

Lewis University Airport has been awarded $444,673 in federal funding through the Illinois State Block Grant Program at the Department of Transportation.

This project constructs a new 40,000 square foot non-exclusive use hangar for aircraft storage to assist the airport to be as self-sustaining as possible by generating revenue.

DeKalb Airport, DeKalb, Illinois – $287,640

DeKalb Airport has been awarded $287,640 in federal funding through the Illinois State Block Grant Program at the Department of Transportation.

This project rehabilitates 5,700 feet of existing paved Taxiway B to maintain the structural integrity of the pavement and to minimize foreign object debris to extend its useful life.

Block Quantum Tech Hub, Illinois – $30,000,000

Block Quantum Tech Hub has been awarded $30,000,000 in federal funding through the Economic Development Administration (EDA) at the U.S. Department of Commerce.

This grant supports the development of a quantum supply chain to position the Illinois-Indiana-Wisconsin region as a center for quantum manufacturing. The Block Quantum Tech Hub is working to scale manufacturing in the Midwest and grow and strengthen our nation’s base of quantum manufacturing and supply-chains. More information about the Block Quantum Tech Hub can be found here.

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El comisionado residente en Washington, Pablo José Hernández Rivera, presentó hoy una agenda de cinco puntos para atender las crisis de agua y energía en Puerto Rico, al marcar su regreso a la capital federal tras un mes de trabajo en la isla y el receso de agosto de la Cámara de Representantes.

"Regreso a Washington con una agenda clara: voy a priorizar lo básico, agua y energía," dijo Hernández Rivera. "Antes de hablar de desarrollo económico, de atraer inversión o de decir que Puerto Rico está abierto para hacer negocios, tenemos que priorizar lo básico."

Al regresar a Washington, Hernández Rivera indicó que se mantendrá enfocado en agua y energía a través de las siguientes cinco acciones:

Solicitará que el Congreso investigue formalmente el escándalo de Power Expectations.

Exigirá respuestas directas del zar de Energía federal y del presidente del 3PPO sobre el alegado encubrimiento de este escándalo.

Le dará seguimiento a la inclusión en el Senado de las prioridades de Puerto Rico en el Water Resources Development Act, que incluye hasta $75 millones para proyectos de agua en Puerto Rico y ya fue aprobado en la Cámara de Representantes.

Le dará seguimiento a la investigación de la Oficina de Rendición de Cuentas del Gobierno (GAO) sobre el uso de los miles de millones de dólares en fondos federales destinados a los sistemas de agua de Puerto Rico y por qué la isla aún no cuenta con servicio confiable.

Continuará el reclamo por una Declaración de Desastre Mayor y por que se expanda a más municipios la declaración de emergencia por sequía del Departamento de Agricultura federal (USDA).

El comisionado residente repasó además un mes de gestiones concretas en torno al agua:

7 de agosto — Presentó un paquete de cinco acciones federales y pidió, por primera vez, que la gobernadora solicite una Declaración Presidencial de Desastre.

11 de agosto — Se unió a un grupo de congresistas para exigirle al GAO una investigación exhaustiva sobre el manejo de $9,000 millones en fondos federales para el sistema de agua.

13 de agosto — Lideró una carta junto a 25 congresistas exhortando a la gobernadora Jenniffer González-Colón a solicitar formalmente la Declaración de Desastre Mayor.

17 de agosto — Su oficina exigió a la Autoridad de Acueductos y Alcantarillados (AAA) datos sobre las pérdidas de agua —cerca del 60% de lo que produce la agencia—, los retrasos en proyectos críticos y el uso de fondos federales disponibles.

21 de agosto — Encabezó una gestión junto a nueve miembros del Congreso exigiéndole al USDA la declaración de desastre por sequía.

“Nuestras gestiones han rendido resultados. El 26 de agosto, el USDA aprobó oficialmente la declaración de desastre por sequía para 26 municipios de Puerto Rico, abriendo acceso a préstamos de emergencia y ayudas para los agricultores afectados. Además, logramos incluir 11 prioridades de Puerto Rico —incluyendo $75 millones— en el Water Resources Development Act”, añadió.

El Comisionado Residente estuvo acompañado por el portavoz del PPD en el Senado, Luis Javier Hernández; el portavoz del PPD en la Cámara de Representantes, Héctor Ferrer; la alcaldesa de Naguabo, Miraidaliz Rosario Pagán; la alcaldesa de Loíza, Julia Nazario; y el alcalde de Juncos, Alfredo “Papo” Alejandro, quienes se unieron al reclamo por respuestas y mayor fiscalización ante los problemas que enfrentan sus comunidades.

Alcaldesas de Naguabo y Loíza respaldan gestiones del Comisionado Residente: “Es insólito que haya millones en fondos federales asignados para proyectos de infraestructura y que la burocracia frene su avance. Agradezco al Comisionado Residente por examinar en Naguabo esta realidad. Nos sumamos firmemente a su llamado para que el USDA extienda la declaración de emergencia por sequía a más municipios que están sufriendo esta crisis, así como a su exigencia de investigar a fondo el contrato de energía temporera. Nuestras familias no pueden seguir a la merced de la ineficiencia”, manifestó la alcaldesa de Naguabo Miraidaliz Rosario Pagán.

“Agradecemos las gestiones del Comisionado Residente y su presencia en nuestros municipios para constatar esta grave situación. La falta de agua y luz afecta el comercio, el turismo y la salud mental de nuestra gente, como vemos a diario en nuestro equipo comunitario. Apoyamos al cien por ciento su agenda desde Washington para lograr que la ayuda por la sequía llegue a más pueblos necesitados y para que se le rindan cuentas al país sobre las irregularidades en el contrato de generación temporera”, destacó la alcaldesa de Loíza Julia Nazario.

“Desde el inicio del cuatrienio hemos estado fiscalizando la crisis de agua y energía, denunciando la falta de uso de fondos para la AAA y las malas negociaciones con Genera, New Fortress y Power Expectations. Si el gobierno hubiera atendido nuestras investigaciones desde mayo de 2025, no estaríamos pasando por este bochorno. Nos hemos unido a cada petición del Comisionado Residente, pero han caído en oídos sordos. Reiteramos que el Senado debe convocar una Comisión Total para exigir cuentas sobre la generación temporera y los problemas de agua, donde la verdadera sequía ha sido la mala gerencia del gobierno”, manifestó el portavoz del PPD en el Senado, Luis Javier Hernández

Por su parte, el portavoz de la Cámara de Representantes Héctor Ferrer destacó el impacto al bolsillo de los puertorriqueños: “La sequía está golpeando el bolsillo del puertorriqueño. Lo responsable es solicitar, tal como lo recomendó nuestro Comisionado, al Presidente de los Estados Unidos una declaración de emergencia. La Gobernadora no puede continuar tratando esto como un asunto secundario”, subrayó Ferrer Santiago al tiempo en que insistió en la renuncia del director de la Autoridad de Acueductos y Alcantarillados Luis González Delgado.

Hernández Unveils Agenda in Congress to Tackle Puerto Rico’s Water and Energy Crises

Hernández will push to expand USDA’s drought disaster designation to additional municipalities and seek an investigation into Puerto Rico’s temporary power generation contract.

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — Puerto Rico’s Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández outlined a five-point agenda to address Puerto Rico’s water and energy crises as he returns to Washington following the congressional district work period.

“I’m returning to Washington with a clear agenda: I’m going to prioritize the basics: water and energy,” Hernández said. “Before we talk about economic development, attracting investment, or saying Puerto Rico is open for business, we have to prioritize the basics.”

As he returns to Washington, Hernández said he will remain focused on water and energy through the following five actions:

Seek a formal congressional investigation into the Power Expectations scandal involving a multibillion-dollar temporary power generation contract.

Demand direct answers from the federal energy czar and the president of the Third-Party Procurement Office (3PPO), the independent entity that oversaw the procurement process, regarding allegations of a cover-up surrounding the Power Expectations controversy.

Press the Senate to preserve Puerto Rico’s priorities in the Water Resources Development Act, including up to $75 million for water infrastructure projects, after securing those provisions in the House version of the bill.

Follow up on the Government Accountability Office (GAO) investigation into how billions of dollars in federal funding for Puerto Rico’s water systems have been used and why the island still lacks reliable water service.

Continue pressing for a Major Disaster Declaration and for USDA to expand its drought disaster designation to additional municipalities in Puerto Rico.

Hernández also highlighted the steps he has taken over the past month to address Puerto Rico’s water crisis:

August 7 — Unveiled a five-point federal action plan and, for the first time, called on the governor to request a Major Disaster Declaration.

August 11 — Joined members of Congress in calling on the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the management of $9 billion in federal funding for Puerto Rico’s water system.

August 13 — Led a letter with 25 members of Congress urging Gov. Jenniffer González-Colón to formally request a Major Disaster Declaration.

August 17 — His office demanded information from the Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority (PRASA) on water losses, which nearly 60% of the water the utility produces, delays in critical projects, and the use of available federal funds.

August 21 — Led an effort with nine members of Congress calling on USDA to issue a drought disaster designation for Puerto Rico.

“Our efforts are producing results. On August 26, USDA issued a drought disaster designation for 26 municipalities in Puerto Rico, making emergency loans and other assistance available to affected farmers. We also secured 11 Puerto Rico priorities in the House-passed Water Resources Development Act, including up to $75 million for water infrastructure projects,” Hernández added.

Hernández was joined by Puerto Rico Senate PPD Minority Leader Luis Javier Hernández; Puerto Rico House PPD Minority Leader Héctor Ferrer; Naguabo Mayor Miraidaliz Rosario Pagán; Loíza Mayor Julia Nazario; and Juncos Mayor Alfredo “Papo” Alejandro, who joined his call for answers and greater federal oversight of the water and energy crises affecting their communities.

The mayors of Naguabo and Loíza, two municipalities particularly affected by water shortages and unreliable service, also expressed support for Hernández’s efforts.

“It is unacceptable that millions of dollars in federal funding have been allocated for infrastructure projects while bureaucracy continues to delay their implementation. I thank the Resident Commissioner for coming to Naguabo to see this situation firsthand. We strongly support his call for USDA to extend its drought disaster designation to additional municipalities affected by this crisis, as well as his call for a thorough investigation into the temporary power generation contract. Our families cannot continue bearing the consequences of government inefficiency,”said Naguabo Mayor Miraidaliz Rosario Pagán.

“We appreciate the Resident Commissioner’s efforts and his presence in our municipalities to see the seriousness of this situation firsthand. The lack of reliable water and electricity affects businesses, tourism and the well-being of our residents, something our community team sees every day. We fully support his agenda in Washington to extend drought assistance to more municipalities in need and to ensure accountability over the concerns surrounding the temporary power generation contract,” said Loíza Mayor Julia Nazario.

The minority leaders of Puerto Rico’s Popular Democratic Party (PPD) in the island’s Senate and House of Representatives also backed Hernández’s push for greater oversight and federal action

“Since the beginning of this term, we have been conducting oversight of Puerto Rico’s water and energy crises, raising concerns about the use of federal funds for PRASA and the government’s agreements with Genera, New Fortress and Power Expectations. Had the government acted on the issues we began investigating in May 2025, Puerto Rico would not be facing this situation today. We have supported each of the Resident Commissioner’s requests, but they have gone unanswered. We again call on the Senate to convene a Committee of the Whole to demand answers on temporary power generation and the island’s water problems. The real drought has been a drought of effective government management,” said PPD Senate Minority Leader Luis Javier Hernández.

PPD House Minority Leader Héctor Ferrer, meanwhile, emphasized the financial impact on Puerto Rican families. “The drought is hitting Puerto Ricans in their pocketbooks. The responsible course of action is to request a presidential disaster declaration, as our Resident Commissioner has recommended. The governor cannot continue treating this as a secondary issue,” Ferrer Santiago said, while reiterating his call for the resignation of Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority Executive President Luis González Delgado.

###
title: Hernández Unveils Agenda in Congress to Tackle Puerto Rico’s Water and Energy Crises

Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on MS NOW’s PoliticsNation, on the show’s 15th anniversary, where he made clear that House Democrats are committed to lowering the high cost of living and ending the affordability crisis that extreme MAGA Republicans have visited on the American people.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Joining me now to kick off this special show, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries. Thanks for starting off this 15th anniversary edition of PoliticsNation. We have a lot to cover, but I want to start off with some of the day’s top headlines. Yesterday marked the six-month anniversary of President Trump’s war with Iran, a conflict the administration told us would be over in a matter of days. That’s still going half a year later. This week, the administration announced an ‘Economic D-Day’ against the Iran—against Iran. But have you seen any signs that we’re getting anywhere close to a resolution that would calm global markets and get our troops out of harm’s way?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, first of all, Rev., great to be with you. Congratulations on 15 amazing years. And so appreciative to be on this anniversary show. And congratulations on a very successful march to defend the vote yesterday. As you indicated, Donald Trump promised that this war of choice in the Middle East would be over in four to six weeks. It’s now raged on for more than six months with no end in sight. What we have seen is that Iran is actually stronger now than they were before this conflict was recklessly entered into, and the American people are economically weaker, particularly as it relates to skyrocketing gas prices and skyrocketing food prices. It’s clear that Donald Trump and Republicans entered into this conflict with no clear objectives, no plan and no exit strategy. And so, now we find ourselves in a mess where you’ve had 18 brave, patriotic service members lose their lives, hundreds have been seriously injured and, of course, tens of billions of taxpayer dollars have been wasted.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, staying with global affairs, last night the Trump administration announced what it claims is a deal to take control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuela’s oil reserves. This is eight months after the administration took out the regime of former President Nicolas Maduro. The consequences of this deal for global energy markets are potentially massive. But what do you make of it? Is there something Trump can actually do? Is there something within his purview? Would it lower prices at the pump, like he claims?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Very unlikely to lower prices. Nothing that they’ve done has actually driven down the high cost of living, notwithstanding the fact that Donald Trump and Republicans promised that they were going to lower costs on day one. Costs in the United States of America, of course, have not gone down. Costs have gone up as a result of direct actions being taken by Republicans, including the Trump tariffs, which have increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year. And, of course, this reckless war of choice that has resulted in costs, particularly gas prices and food prices, increasing. So this, to me, seems like another desperate attempt to pretend as though the problems that the American people want Donald Trump and Republicans to solve are going to be solved. The only way to actually move this country in a different direction is going to be to make sure that we take back control of the House as well as the Senate in November. We’re committed to actually fighting for an affordable America, to lower the cost of groceries and gas and housing and to make sure that healthcare is affordable for every single American.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, moving closer to home, President Trump this week massively escalated his trade war with Canada after talks between the two countries collapsed. The White House imposed a new 50% tariff on Canadian products that economists warn could increase costs for American consumers. Trump also signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America. In your opinion, is any of this doing anything to help make living expenses more affordable for Americans or to create jobs? And if not, what is it all about?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, again, I think what we’re seeing is Donald Trump throw a temper tantrum because Canada refuses to bend to his will, and I think he’s been so used to a Republican Congress that conducts itself like nothing more than a reckless rubber stamp for Donald Trump’s extreme agenda. He doesn’t like it when people push back against his failed, broken and extreme policies. Certainly this trade war with Canada is going to make life more expensive for the American people in an environment where far too many people are already working hard, they’re playing by the rules, but they can’t thrive and can barely survive. Life is too expensive in the United States of America. People are drowning in this failed economy, and we’re determined to do something about this affordability crisis. It’s not a hoax. It’s very real. I hear about it every day in the district that I’m privileged to represent in Brooklyn or as I travel the nation. It certainly is also the case, Rev., that pretending to rename Lake Ontario is going to do nothing to actually improve the situation that we’re in relative to this failed economy. And we need serious people to engage in serious behavior and that’s not what’s coming out of 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue, or the Republican-controlled Congress right now.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, we’re all counting down to the midterms, now just 66 days away. With polls showing approval ratings plummeting for President Trump and his Republican Party, many Democrats are worried this White House is looking for ways to mess with the vote. One area of growing concern is the post office. The administration says it’s moving ahead with restrictions to mail-in voting after the Supreme Court earlier in the week lifted an injunction on procedural grounds. However, there’s already been another partial injunction issued at the district court level and the legal fight is expected to continue. If the order is allowed to be enacted, states could potentially have to hand over their voter rolls, or the post office might not deliver their ballots. Can you talk about the significance of this situation and what Democrats are doing to push back?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We’re going to continue to do everything possible to make sure that this illegitimate, we believe, unlawful and ultimately unconstitutional order does not stand. The Framers of the Constitution were very clear in assigning responsibility to oversee elections to states and local authorities—that was done specifically to avoid some king-like figure from being able to try to parachute in and manipulate an election. And that’s why ultimately we believe that on substantive grounds, we will prevail in the courts, including ultimately if it goes back up to the courts, the United States Supreme Court, perhaps it doesn’t get there because the lower courts continue to do the right thing. Now we also have to be prepared for the reality that Republicans have adopted voter suppression as an electoral strategy. And that’s why, as Democrats, we’re committing to making sure that we stand up the largest voter protection effort in the history of the country. That’s House Democrats working with Senate Democrats, working with the Democratic Governors, the Democratic Secretaries of State, as well as the Democratic Attorneys General like Tish James, of course, here in New York State. And also partnering with civil society—so the civil rights groups, of course, Reverend Sharpton, making sure we partner with civil liberties organizations, organized labor, good government groups and the faith community. This is an all-hands-on-deck effort underway to make sure that it is the American people, at the end of the day, who are the ones who get to decide who’s in control of Congress, who wins these Governors races, not MAGA extremists.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, last question. You’re spending the August recess crisscrossing the country for Democratic candidates. And next month, you’ll be hosting a massive fundraiser with former President Obama right here in New York City. At the same time, Republicans are holding their midterm convention. Democrats are feeling hopeful about their chances in November. But as you know, these midterms are coming in the midst of the most intense attack on voting rights and Black representation in this country since the Civil Rights era. That’s why you were with us yesterday at the March on Washington, which I helped organize with the King family in my capacity as head of National Action Network, which you’re a member of. Are you optimistic that your party can overcome the Supreme Court decision gutting the Voting Rights Act and Republican efforts to redraw congressional maps to eliminate Black-majority districts throughout the South and elsewhere? Will you be holding the Speaker’s gavel when PoliticsNation celebrates its 16th anniversary next year?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’re going to work to do everything that we can to make sure we win back control of the United States House of Representatives on November 3rd. In terms of any change in title, that’ll be a January 3rd issue and if we have the opportunity to work on that we certainly will. But our commitment is to make sure that we continue to aggressively push back against all of the extremism unleashed on the American people and that certainly is the attack—unprecedented in modern American history—on Black political representation and the opportunity for African American communities in the South and throughout America to elect the candidate of their choice. This Callais decision was egregious. It’s why we need dramatic Supreme Court reform and certainly, as House Democrats, we’re committed to making sure one of our top priorities in the majority is passage of the John Robert Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, so we can end the era of voter suppression here in this great country of ours once and for all.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Well, it’s our honor that you kicked us off on our anniversary of PoliticsNation. Thank you, Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Thank you, Rev.

Full interview can be watched here.

NORTH LAS VEGAS – Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04) hosted House Oversight and Government Reform Committee Ranking Member Robert Garcia (CA-42) for an immigration roundtable in North Las Vegas, bringing community leaders and individuals directly impacted by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to speak directly with the lawmaker responsible for holding those agencies accountable.

“ICE has acted recklessly and without oversight for far too long, costing the lives of four people who were killed by ICE agents, all while this Administration strips Temporary Protected Status (TPS) from families who have lived, worked, and raised their kids here for years, leaving them exposed to that same reckless enforcement.” Rep. Horsford stated. “That’s exactly why it mattered that Ranking Member Garcia was here to hear directly from community leaders and the people living through it. With a $75 billion slush fund now behind ICE and CBP and American lives on the line, Congress has a constitutional responsibility to conduct oversight because detention does not erase people's rights, and federal authority does not excuse abuse, secrecy, or misconduct."

“The stories we heard today highlighted the urgency we need to bring to holding the Trump Administration accountable for their cruel policies, unconstitutional actions, and brutal immigration enforcement misconduct." said Ranking Member Robert Garcia. "Thank you for Congressman Horsford for ensuring that our immigrant communities receive the support they need during this time. We will continue to fight for due process and the protection of immigrant communities in Las Vegas and across the country.”

Congressman Horsford has exercised his oversight authority at the ICE facility in Pahrump on more than one occasion, including a visit where he was initially denied access before returning to see conditions inside for himself. Together, Horsford and Ranking Member Garcia examined the impact of ICE's expanding footprint and the termination of TPS on one of the nation's most diverse congressional districts.

Congressman Horsford emphasized that ICE enforcement actions must include meaningful guardrails that protect communities rather than spread fear and anguish. He has cosponsored legislation to strengthen oversight, increase transparency, and protect the rights and dignity of individuals in immigration custody, including:

H.R. 5653, Trust Through Transparency Act — Requires immigration enforcement officers to use body-worn cameras during public-facing enforcement actions.

H.R. 6890, PROTECT Immigration Act — Ends the Section 287(g) program, which authorizes state and local law enforcement to carry out federal immigration enforcement functions in partnership with ICE.

H.R. 5941, Restoring Access for Detainees Act — Ensures detained noncitizens have timely, confidential access to legal counsel, family members, and applicable oversight entities while in DHS custody.

H.R. 4667, VISIBLE Act — Requires federal immigration enforcement officers to display visible identification, such as a name or badge number, during public-facing operations.

H.R. 3473, Humane Accountability Act — Strengthens congressional oversight of immigration enforcement by requiring DHS to report detailed data on migrant encounters, detentions, and removals.

###
title: Horsford, Oversight Ranking Member Garcia Hear Directly from Nevada Families Impacted by ICE and CBP

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente Pablo José Hernández Rivera anunció su respaldo a la legislación federal que crearía un programa para el desarrollo de destrezas laborales mediante realidad virtual, realidad aumentada y otras tecnologías inmersivas.

El Immersive Technology for the American Workforce Act (H.R. 6968) daría $50 millones anuales para desarrollo laboral relacionado al gaming y realidad virtual. “Necesitamos bajar el costo de vida; para bajar el costo de vida necesitamos desarrollo económico; y la industria de gaming y tecnología es una oportunidad de desarrollo económico para Puerto Rico, particularmente la juventud”, expresó el Comisionado Residente.

Hernández realize el anuncio durante GAMERGYPR 2026, la convención internacional de videojuegos celebrada en el Centro de Convenciones de Puerto Rico en San Juan. Allí caminó por las exhibiciones y compartió con jóvenes y adultos vinculados a la industria de videojuegos. Los organizadores estiman que la asistencia fluctuó entre 5,000 y 7,000 personas.

“Mientras algunos políticos viven en el pasado y rehúsan reconocer el valor que tiene esta industria para retener jóvenes y fomentar desarrollo económico en Puerto Rico, nosotros estamos aquí para apoyarlos”, añadió.

Según el Entertainment Software Association, en Estados Unidos la industria de gaming genera más de 250,000 empleos y aporta más de 65,000 mil millones a la economía. La edad promedio de los jugadores es 37 años.

La medida es encabezada por los representantes John Mannion de Nueva York y Gabe Evans de Colorado, y cuenta con el respaldo de Jobs for the Future, la National Association of Workforce Boards y la XR Association.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Reps. George Whitesides (D-CA) and Pat Harrigan (R-NC) introduced the Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act, bipartisan legislation to reduce the risk of superintelligent AI by monitoring how capable frontier AI systems are becoming at conducting AI research and development on their own.

The largest AI labs are increasingly using their own AI systems to run experiments, write code, and drive research internally, and the most advanced systems at those labs are not always the ones the public sees. Last month,an AI system broke out of its testing environment during an internal evaluation and autonomously compromised a third party’s production systems — an episode no federal agency had advance visibility into. Today, the U.S. government has no reliable way to track how fast these internal capabilities are accelerating, or when they make a sudden, dramatic leap.

“Just in the past few months, we have seen AI systems break out of their testing environments and threaten the security of entire systems,” said Rep. Whitesides. “When you take humans out of the driver’s seat and let machines train machines, small glitches can snowball into major security risks fast. Today, Washington is essentially flying blind on how fast this handoff is happening. This legislation ensures that when frontier labs partner with federal evaluators, we understand who is actually training and improving these models.”

“AI is beginning to play a role not just in solving problems, but in building the next generation of AI itself, and we need to understand what that means before the technology outruns our ability to measure it,” said Congressman Pat Harrigan. “I’m proud to co-lead the Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act to give NIST the visibility it needs to track these capabilities as they develop.”

The bill responds directly toPacing the Frontier, a July statement signed by more than 1,300 employees of leading AI companies – including CEOs, co-founders, and chief scientists – asking the U.S. government to support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development.

The Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act would:

Track AI self-improvement by directing Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) to monitor capability trends, specifically how AI systems autonomously research and develop subsequent AI models to drive scientific breakthroughs.

Add transparency to government-industry testing agreements by giving federal evaluators the authority to request internal developer metrics on AI-driven development, including estimates and methodologies for work completed without human review.

Standardize autonomous R&D evaluations by ensuring federal pre-deployment evaluations directly test a frontier model’s ability to autonomously conduct AI research and development.

###
title: Rep. Whitesides Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Reduce the Risk of Superintelligent AI by Monitoring Self-Improving AI Systems

Fredericksburg, Va. — On Monday, August 24, Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) and Senator Tim Kaine (D-Va.) hosted a roundtable with veterans from the community to discuss their experiences with the Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center. Vindman has repeatedly called for action from leadership at the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to reduce wait times at this state-of-the-art facility.

“Veterans in Virginia’s Seventh District and across the country have earned the very best care our nation can provide, and long wait times for critical health services are unacceptable,” said Vindman. “We heard from veterans whose appointments have been delayed, canceled, or disrupted because the VA doesn’t have the staff it needs. This roundtable helped highlight these stories, renewing our call to increase transparency and accountability at the VA. Our veterans kept their promise to America. We must keep our promise to them.”

“I was glad to hear directly from veterans that they are pleased with the quality of their care, but I will keep pushing the VA to do more to address wait times,” said Kaine. “Virginia is home to one of the largest veteran populations in the nation, and I will always advocate for our servicemembers, veterans, and their families to have access to the high-quality, timely care they deserve.”

View all photos from the roundtable here.

BACKGROUND

In mid-July 2026, 200 Virginians responded to a survey from Vindman about the delays they experienced at the Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center. He personally called over 30 of these veterans to express his commitment to demanding better from the VA.

In June 2026, Vindman introduced bipartisan legislation to increase transparency and accountability at the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), helping address understaffing at facilities across the country, including the Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center, and ensure veterans receive the care they earned.

Prior to that, Vindman called for accountability and a clear timeline to bring the facility to full capacity, ensuring our nation’s veterans receive the care they earned through their service in six different letters. All of these letters have gone without a written or substantial response.

Vindman sent the first letter to Secretary Collins raising the concern on staffing, wait times, and the ability to best serve veterans on April 10, 2025. Read the letter here.

Vindman sent the second letter to Secretary Collins raising the concern on staffing, wait times, and the ability to best serve veterans on October 6, 2025. Read the letter here.

Vindman sent the third letter to Secretary Collins raising the concern on staffing, wait times, and the ability to best serve veterans on October 17, 2025. Read the letter here.

Vindman sent the fourth letter to Secretary Collins raising the concern on staffing, wait times, and the ability to best serve veterans on October 27, 2025. Read the letterhere.

Vindman sent the fifth letter to Secretary Collins raising the concern on staffing, wait times, and the ability to best serve veterans on April 10, 2026. Read the letter here.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – House Armed Services Committee Ranking Member Adam Smith (D-Wash.) released the following statement marking the sixth month anniversary of President Trump’s war against Iran.
“It has been six months since Trump unilaterally launched his catastrophic war of choice against Iran and so far, he has failed to achieve any of his administration’s constantly changing strategic objectives. This includes ending Iran’s support and use of terrorist proxies, eliminating its ballistic missile program, removing its highly enriched uranium, or changing the ruling regime. Instead, Iran has gained greater leverage, continues to destabilize the region, has a younger and more hardline Ayatollah, and we are being forced to negotiate and pay for the opening of the Strait of Hormuz, which was open before Trump launched his war.
“Losses continue to accumulate, including 19 American service members killed and over 750 wounded, while thousands of innocent civilians have been killed across the region. Tens of billions of dollars of taxpayers’ money is being wasted while driving up the cost of gas, utilities, and groceries at home and throttling economies around the world. All of this is happening as we face a $2 trillion deficit, and Trump continues to demand $1.6 trillion for defense spending while slashing critical critically important domestic programs and slashing taxes for the rich.
“It has also become clear that in the opening days of Trump’s war, the United States inadvertently struck a girls’ school in Minab, Iran. Over 150 people were killed, most of them children. DoD has failed to complete its investigation into the tragedy and congressional Republicans have yet to hold DoD accountable for its failure. The lack of transparency and responsibility shown in the wake of this horrible mishap is the antithesis of who we are as a country and a democracy and threatens to undermine our standing with allies and partners as well as adversaries.
“Trump’s war has put extreme stress on our military’s munitions and platforms. Crucially, American service members continue to serve valiantly while being forced to grapple with unnecessary strain from extended deployments. The USS Gerald R. Ford Carrier Strike Group was deployed for 11 months, the longest deployment since the Vietnam war, and the USS Abraham Lincoln continues to face extreme challenges as it makes its way home from the Middle East after numerous unplanned extensions of its current deployment. Service members across all branches of the military have had to shoulder the burden of an unchecked and unprepared executive branch and the failure of congressional Republicans to do their jobs and exercise appropriate oversight of the Trump Administration. This situation also further highlights the Trump Administration’s lack of cooperation with Congress and honesty with the American people. 
“The American people, and a majority in Congress, have made it overwhelmingly clear that Trump’s war must end now. The longer Trump waits, the more likely the U.S. will find itself embroiled in another decades-long foreign conflict, which is precisely what Trump promised voters he would never do when he ran for office.”

title: Smith Statement on Six Months of Trump’s War Against Iran

text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Representative Mark Takano (CA-39) participated in the 63rd anniversary of the March on Washington alongside Minority Leader Representative Hakeem Jeffries (NY-8), Congressional Black Caucus Chairwoman Representative Yvette Clarke (NY-9), Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), and Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT).

Leaders provided remarks at the steps of the Lincoln Memorial, then participated in a march to the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial led by Reverend Al Sharpton.

Below are Rep. Taknao’s remarks as prepared:

“We are not here simply to remember history. We are here because the work that began 63 years ago is unfinished. We are here because the battles we thought had been long settled have resurfaced:

“Birthright citizenship is under attack. Americans feel the need to carry a passport to prove they belong. Fascists are using their power to intimidate Americans into silence.

“These are not echoes of some distant past. They are the reality of this moment.

“And this moment is an awakening: norms alone will not protect us.

“Every generation must take up the work of renewing and perfecting the idea of America so that America lives up to its promise. There are those who would have us believe America is about blood and soil. Replacing America’s founding principles with a narrow definition of who belongs and who does not. That being an American is about how many generations your family has lived here, where your parents were born, and what you look like.

“But that is not the America generations of people have struggled, marched, bled, and died for.

“And what is the idea of America?

“It is the idea that all of us are created equal. That government derives its power from the people. That every person deserves liberty and justice. And that being an American is not determined by your race, your religion, or where your parents came from, or who you love.

“The work of renewing and perfecting the idea of America does not happen on its own.

“People had to fight for it.

“John Lewis fought for that idea. At 23 years old he stood here in 1963 and demanded that America live up to it promise. Two years later, on the Edmund Pettus Bridge, police beat him for demanding the right to vote. He knew what awaited him on the other side of the bridge. Yet, he crossed it anyway.

“Because America was an idea worth fighting for.

“Wong Kim Ark fought for that idea. Born in San Francisco to immigrant parents, he challenged the government when it tried to deny him entry into his own country. In 1898, he took his fight to the Supreme Court—and won. If you are born here, you are an American. Period. More than a century later, we are fighting that battle again.

“Because America is an idea worth fighting for.

“And my own family fought for that idea. During World War II, my great-uncle Monzo served in the 442nd Regimental Combat Team. Fighting and bleeding alongside other segregated units like the Buffalo Soldiers and Tuskegee Airmen. He fought for the United States while my parents and grandparents were among more than 120,000 Japanese Americans incarcerated by their own government.

“Think about that contradiction. A country that questioned their loyalty and took away their freedom. And still, Japanese American soldiers fought and died for an America that had not yet lived up to its promise. The motto of the 442nd was simple: Go for Broke. Risk everything. Give everything. And they did.

“Today, we are being called to our own “Go for Broke” moment. To fight for the character of our country. We fight for an America where nobody feels that they have to carry a passport to prove they belong. We fight for an America where citizenship cannot be stripped away because of who your parents are. We must fight for an America where the government does not use fear and intimidation to silence its own people. And we must fight for an America where every eligible citizen can vote and have that vote counted.

“The people who gathered here 63 years ago understood something we cannot afford to forget: Progress is not permanent. Rights do not protect themselves. Democracy does not defend itself.

“Every generation inherits the idea of America—and then must decide whether it is willing to fight for it.

“My great-uncle Monzo made his choice. Wong Kim Ark made his choice. John Lewis made his choice. Dr. King made his choice. Now it is our turn!

“Because America does not belong to one political party. America does not belong to a bloodline. And it certainly doesn’t belong to one man.

“America belongs to all of us. Let’s Go For Broke. Go all in for democracy. Go all in for equality. Go all in for freedom. We cannot turn back. Let’s finish the assignment, make Dr. King’s dream a reality, and fulfill the promise of a better America.”

Video of Rep. Takano remarks can be found here.

###
title: Rep. Takano Addresses 63rd Anniversary of March on Washington Rally: “America is an Idea Worth Fighting For.”

Investment will expand hands-on training in automotive, diesel-electric transportation, and robotics manufacturing/welding for 200 additional students each semester

SANTA ANA, CA — U.S. Representative Lou Correa (CA-46) today presented a check for $850,000 in federal funding to Santa Ana College. These dollars were used to create infrastructure for its Automotive Technology, Diesel-Electric Transportation Technology, and Robotics Manufacturing/Welding programs. The funding, secured by Rep. Correa through the FY26 appropriations process, will allow the college to serve 200 additional students each semester in training for in-demand, good-paying careers.

“Santa Ana College has always been a launching pad for opportunity in our community, and this funding makes sure it stays that way,” said Rep. Correa. “Families in Orange County want access to good jobs that don’t require a four-year degree and a mountain of debt — like jobs in the trades, in manufacturing, and in transportation. This investment means 200 more students a semester get hands-on training and a real shot at those careers.”

"I want to extend my sincere gratitude to Congressman Lou Correa for his continued investment in our students and our community. This $850,000 investment will directly elevate our Automotive, Diesel-Electric Transportation Technology, and Robotic Manufacturing/Welding programs, giving our students access to the modern, hands-on training spaces they need to succeed in high-demand technical careers. We are not just expanding a facility, we are expanding opportunity for the workforce Orange County depends on. I am deeply thankful for Congressman Correa's partnership and his belief in the power of community colleges to change lives," said Dr. Annebelle Nery, President of Santa Ana College.

The programs have at times had over 400 students on waitlists, and the trades they train for pay median hourly wages of roughly $28 to $41. text:
The letter comes following recent news that the U.S. Navy is considering renaming the USS Doris Miller in honor of the president

Doris Miller was a sailor aboard the USS West Virginia when Japan began its attack on Pearl Harbor who put himself in harm’s way to help save his fellow wounded sailors

The letter was signed by 73 members, including Ranking Member Adam Smith and 24 Members from the House Armed Services Committee

Washington, D.C. — Today, Representatives Wesley Bell (D-MO-01), Marilyn Strickland (D-WA-10), and Kweisi Mfume (D-MD-07) led over 70 of their Democratic House colleagues in an effort pressing Department of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao to keep the name of the USS Doris Miller as is.

“Renaming this ship after a sitting President would be unprecedented and break longstanding tradition,” wrote the Representatives. “Most importantly, this would diminish the recognition of one of our country’s greatest military heroes. It was during President Trump’s first term that the Navy announced CVN-81 would bear Doris Miller’s name. Reversing that decision now would be a significant step backward in honoring the courage and sacrifice of those who have served our country.”

News broke last week about the Navy potentially renaming its ship, CVN-81, to honor Trump. During the president’s first term, the Navy had announced that CVN-81 would bear Doris Miller’s name, making it the first aircraft carrier to be named for an African American, as well as the first named in honor of an enlisted sailor.

Doris ‘Dorie’ Miller was serving aboard the USS West Virginia on December 7, 1941, when Japan began its attack. At the time, Miller was a Mess Attendant Second Class, and after his station came under fire, he took control of an anti-aircraft gun and fired at incoming aircraft. Even as the ship sank, he kept fighting until he ran out of ammunition, and assisted his fellow wounded sailors to reach safety.

“Doris Miller’s story is one of extraordinary bravery, service, and pure patriotism,” the Representatives continued. “When he served, segregation restricted the roles available to Black sailors and servicemembers. Yet, when his country came under attack, Miller did not hesitate to put himself in harm’s way to defend his fellow sailors and his nation. This story embodies the finest traditions of the United States Armed Forces.”

“There has never been a time when we have named a warship after a sitting president. Changing course and now to satisfy a sitting President’s ego, especially one who dodged service to his country, would be shamefully wrong. We urge you to reject this plan and ensure that CVN-81 bears the name USS Doris Miller. Our Navy must continue honoring the courage of those that answered their country’s call to service,” the lawmakers concluded.

Congressman Bell is a member of the House Armed Services Committee and has fought to protect the rights of our servicemembers, past, present, and future. Recently, he led a letter calling on Secretary Cao to disclose information about the conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln amidst concerns of crew well-being while deployed in the Middle East for the Iran War. He also led a letter calling on the Department of Defense to take measures to protect the well-being of crew members aboard the USS Gerald R. Ford.

The letter was signed by: Reps. Gabe Amo, Yassamin Ansari, Joyce Beatty, Julia Brownley, Nikki Budzinski, Salud Carbajal, André Carson, Troy Carter, Ed Case, Joaquin Castro, Gilbert Cisneros, Emanuel Cleaver, Steve Cohen, Herb Conaway, Joe Courtney, Jason Crow, Diana DeGette, Christopher Deluzio, Mark DeSaulnier, Debbie Dingell, Sarah Elfreth, Dwight Evans, Shomari Figures, John Garamendi, Daniel Goldman, Maggie Goodlander, Josh Gottheimer, Steven Horsford, Chrissy Houlahan, Glenn Ivey, Sara Jacobs, Jonathan Jackson, William Keating, Timothy Kennedy, Ro Khanna, Greg Landsman, Stephen Lynch, April McClain Delaney, Jennifer McClellan, Christian Menefee, Dave Min, Gwen Moore, Seth Moulton, Jerrold Nadler, Donald Norcross, Eleanor Norton, Frank Pallone, Scott Peters, Brittany Pettersen, Mike Quigley, Patrick Ryan, Bradley Schneider, Robert Scott, Terri Sewell, Adam Smith, Eric Sorensen, Suhas Subramanyam, Shri Thanedar, Bennie Thompson, Dina Titus, Jill Tokuda, Ritchie Torres, Derek Tran, Gabe Vasquez, Marc Veasey, Eugene Vindman, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Maxine Waters, George Whitesides, Frederica Wilson.

The letter text can be viewed HERE.

###

Wesley Bell is the U.S. Representative for Missouri's First Congressional District, which includes St. Louis City and a portion of St. Louis County. He is a member of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, House Armed Services Committee, and House Foreign Affairs Committee.
title: Bell, Strickland, Mfume Lead 70+ Members in Effort to Stop Navy from Renaming Ship Honoring Black War Hero in Honor of President Trump

Today was a milestone for Alewife Brook. Congresswoman Katherine Clark met at the Brook with Save the Alewife Brook and our state and local delegation to see the sewage, sediment, and flooding crisis for herself. We talked with her about engaging the Army Corps of Engineers for a project to dredge, dechannelize, and restore Alewife Brook.

“Protecting our environment means protecting our neighbors. I’m grateful for the incredible advocates at Save the Alewife Brook for their continued work to eliminate sewage pollution, safeguard our local ecosystem, and build the cleaner future our kids deserve. I’m looking forward to partnering with them and with leaders at every level of government to keep moving the ball forward.” Democratic Whip Katherine Clark (MA‑5)

Joining the Congresswoman at the Brook were State Senator Pat Jehlen and State Representatives Christine Barber, Dave Rogers, Sean Garballey, and Steve Owens. From the Town of Arlington, we were joined by Town Manager Jim Feeney and Select Board members Diane Mahon and Steve DeCourcey. Save the Alewife Brook was represented by steering committee members Kristin Anderson, Gene Benson, Ann McDonald, George Laite, and Mike Lonetto.

Why this visit matters

A portion of the Alewife Brook is confined to a 27-foot-wide concrete channel that receives untreated sewage from six active Combined Sewer Overflow (CSO) outfalls. In 2021, MWRA, Cambridge, and Somerville dumped 51 million gallons of untreated sewage into the Brook.

The Brook has accumulated 2 1/2 to 3 1/2 feet of contaminated sediment and, according to the 2024 Inter-Fluve Sediment Study, will lose its remaining capacity as sediment continues to fill in.

The public health toll is already severe. During CSO discharges, E. coli levels in Alewife Brook reach roughly 950 times the EPA safe standard. A Boston University School of Public Health study found that even living near CSOs can increase the risk of illness serious enough to require an ER visit.

Roughly 5,000 residents of Arlington, Cambridge, and Belmont, many in Environmental Justice neighborhoods, live in the Alewife Brook 100‑year floodplain.

—
title: Save the Alewife Brook: A Federal Partnership for a Cleaner, Safer Alewife.

WASHINGTON – Congressman Steve Cohen (TN-9) today announced that the University of Tennessee Health Science Center (UTHSC) will receive a $1 million grant from the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) to expand the maternity care workforce under the direction of Dr. Mary Fouquier of the College of Nursing. Congressman Cohen also announced Methodist Le Bonheur Community Outreach will receive a grant of $450,000 for its Delta Region Maternal Care Coordination Program from HRSA.

St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital will receive a grant of $921,871 from the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke to study the structural basis of signal instigation under the direction of Dr. Georgios Skiniotis, director of its Center of Excellence for Structural Cell Biology. Proteins are 3-dimensional and drug-binding, and can subtly alter that shape to induce, enhance, reduce, or prevent something else downstream in the biological system from occurring. Dr. Skiniotis’ team will use advanced cryogenic electron microscopy techniques to directly observe several proteins, the metabotropic glutamate 2 and 5 (mGluR2 and mGluR5), and γ-aminobutyric acid B receptors (GABABR) which bind the neurotransmitters glutamate and glycine receptor, in combination with another critical protein class, called the G-proteins. The mGluR2, mGluR5, and GABABR are part of a substantial class of receptors, called the G-protein coupled receptors (GPCR). Approximately 35 percent of all FDA-approved drugs target these GPCRs. Thus, the detailed structural information that Dr. Skiniotis’ team seeks to uncover will assist in the development of new drugs for these critical targets.

Congressman Cohen made the following statement:

“In a region with high levels of infant and maternal mortality, these investments in training nurses and outreach to the community will save lives. St. Jude continues to do critical research at the cellular level that will result in discoveries and improve outcomes. I congratulate all three recipients of this funding for the life-saving work they are doing.”

ANNAPOLIS, MD – Yesterday, Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), a member of the Labor Caucus, hosted her annual roundtable discussion with labor leaders in Maryland’s Third District at the Maryland State & DC AFL-CIO. This was the second annual convening since the Congresswoman first took office last year.

“As a proud member of the Labor Caucus and daughter of a union rail worker, I know firsthand the hard-fought protections, rights, and dignity that unions have secured for working families across this country,” said Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth. “I reconvened this roundtable to hear directly from our Third District union leaders as to how we can best support their members and workers across Maryland. Especially as this Administration deepens the affordability crisis, attacks collective bargaining rights, and strips back commonsense worker safety regulations, it is all the more important to stand with our brothers and sisters in organized labor in the fight for workers’ rights on the job.”

At the roundtable, Elfreth delivered an update from Congress, including progress on NDAA amendments and other legislative initiatives to restore the collective bargaining rights of hardworking federal employees and expedite the process of securing labor contracts. The roundtable was an opportunity to hear directly from the representatives of the over 340,000 union workers across the state and 45,000 federal employees in the District. In addition to collective bargaining, the conversation focused on federal funding cuts, healthcare, affordability, and workplace safety for rail, maritime, and emergency responders.

Elfreth was joined by various labor unions from across Maryland’s Third District, including the Maryland State and DC AFL-CIO, Maryland State Education Association (MSEA), Carroll County Education Association (CCEA), Service Employees International Union (SEIU) Local 500 and 32BJ, Howard County International Association of Fire Fighters (IAFF) Local 2000, International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers (IBEW) Local 24 and Local 26, International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees (IATSE) Local 487, Amalgamated Transit Union (ATU) Local 1300, International Union of Painters and Allied Trades (IUPAT) DC51, the International Organization of Masters, Mates & Pilots, the Maritime Institute of Technology and Graduate Studies (MISTAG), American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees (AFSCME) Maryland Council 3, the National Active and Retired Federal Employees (NARFE) Chapter 1734, Laborers’ International Union of North America, American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE), American Maritime Officers, United Association of Plumbers and Pipefitters, Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen - B&O, and the Baltimore-DC Building Trades Council.

“SEIU Local 500 is eager to join Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth alongside our labor partners to discuss the real issues facing Maryland workers. As a state legislator, she was a labor champion. In the face of rising costs and attacks on labor rights by the current administration, we are glad to have her in the United States Congress championing the needs of working people,” said Christopher Cano, Director of Political & Legislative Affairs, SEIU Local 500.

“As an association dedicated to federal workers and retirees, NARFE appreciates Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth’s work to protect the merit-based civil service system and our earned benefits. We pledge to stand with her to fight ongoing threats to public health, food safety, worker rights, and the myriad ways in which the federal workforce protects and enhances the lives of all Americans,” said Teresa Baker, First Vice President, NARFE Maryland Federation.

“IATSE Local 487 is proud to attend this AFL CIO roundtable discussion with Congresswoman Elfreth. Being given the opportunity to discuss the state of the film & television industry in the US, and more specifically the Mid-Atlantic region, allows our skilled craftworkers a voice in how we can bring back the work that supports our families and local industries in Maryland. Our hope is that this conversation highlights the vital importance of a national tax incentive and legislative support for the I.A.T.S.E. workforce—the skilled craftworkers whose labor powers the entertainment industry,” said Vice President Steve Saada, IATSE Local 487.

“Congresswoman Elfreth has been a longtime advocate for Maryland’s firefighters. Her accessibility and commitment to our members are unmatched, whether making time to meet with our leaders in her office on Capitol Hill or visiting local fire stations. Most recently, she co-sponsored H.R. 1269, the Honoring Our Fallen Heroes Act, which extends federal Public Safety Officers’ Benefits to the families of firefighters who die from occupational cancer,” said Adam Nolder, Vice President of IAFF Local 2000.

“The issues that are top of mind for our union today include the Administration’s Jones Act waiver, which is giving American maritime jobs to foreign seafarers while doing nothing to lower gas prices,” said MM&P President Captain Don Josberger. “We are also advocating strongly on Capitol Hill for passage of the Faster Labor Contracts Act, which would ensure that unscrupulous companies cannot indefinitely hinder workers’ legal right to form a union.”

“Public services from our state and local governments, and the public service workers who make them happen, are more important now than ever. Right now, workers face significant challenges on the job, and our union appreciates the partnership and collaboration with Congresswoman Elfreth to ensure public service workers have a voice in Congress fighting for them,” said President Jack Hughes, AFSCME Maryland Council 3.

As the daughter of two civil servants and the representative of over 45,000 federal employees, Congresswoman Elfreth has been laser-focused on protecting and advancing the rights of workers and civil servants. Elfreth has voted in favor of numerous bills to ensure workers receive the benefits they deserve, including the Faster Labor Contracts Act to speed up the process for workers to secure labor contracts and the Protect America’s Workforce Act (PAWA) to repeal a presidential executive order that stripped union rights from 1.5 million federal workers. She has also spoken out in support of legislation like theRailroad Retirement Fairness Act to eliminate provisions that unfairly reduce retirement payments for certain railroad retirees and spouses. On the House Armed Services Committee, Elfreth has fought for civilian DoD civil servants and proudly supported Congressman Donald Norcross’ amendment in each year’s annual defense bill to restore the collective bargaining rights that the President’s executive order stripped.

Federal judge ruled in March that collective bargaining rights at the VA must be reinstated

AFGE Local 1206 reports that months later, these rights have still not been restored

STOCKTON – Today, Rep. Josh Harder (CA-09) called on the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to respond to concerns that union rights at local VA facilities are not being upheld. Harder led nine regional colleagues in a letter to VA Secretary Doug Collins demanding answers on the VA’s progress to comply with a federal order requiring collective bargaining rights to be restored.

In March, a federal district court judge ordered the Department of Veterans Affairs to reinstate its Master Collective Bargaining Agreement with the American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE). Those agreements provide for collective bargaining rights like official time for authorized union representatives and access to union office space and equipment. However, AFGE Local 1206, which represents bargaining unit employees within the VA Northern California Health Care System, has raised concerns that these rights have still not been fully restored.

“We take seriously the concerns raised by union representatives, particularly in light of the ongoing litigation regarding the termination of the Master Collective Bargaining Agreement. Indeed, on August 7, 2026, the federal district court issued a further order requiring the agreement to remain in effect pursuant to its continuation provisions,” wrote the Members. “To better understand the circumstances and VA Northern California Health Care System's implementation of the reinstated agreement, we respectfully request responses to these concerns.”

Key demands of the Members to be provided no later than September 11, 2026:

Steps taken to fully implement the March court order and restore collective bargaining rights at the VA Northern California Health Care System.

Details of any incidents of union representatives being denied pay or access to union space and equipment while performing union representational duties.

Steps taken to resolve outstanding disagreements between the VA Northern California Health Care System and AFGE Local 1206 regarding the bargaining agreement.

Read the full letter here.

Monterey, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) joined Rep. Brad Schneider (IL-10) and Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Peter Welch (D-VT) in introducing the Banning Antiquated Duties and Delivering Equitable American Levies (BAD DEAL) Act to repeal Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 and refund all duties paid under this authority. Over the weekend, trade talks between the United States and Canada broke down, resulting in the United States’ imposition of 50% tariffs on roughly $20 billion in Canadian goods under Section 338. In response, Canada is pledging dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs slated to come into effect after Labor Day.

The United States and Canada share one of the world’s largest and most integrated trading relationships. In 2025, bilateral trade in goods and services totaled approximately $872 billion, including nearly $426 billion in U.S. exports. Canada is the United States’ second-largest trading partner and the top merchandise export market for 32 states. These new tariffs threaten to disrupt cross-border supply chains, raise costs for American families and businesses, and invite further retaliation against U.S. industries.

“This Administration’s senseless tariff policies and self-defeating trade wars have already hurt American businesses and raised costs for working families. Now, the President’s 40-year fixation on tariffs is producing yet another bad deal for the American people by imposing massive new duties on Canada, our second-largest trading partner and a longstanding ally,” said Rep. Panetta. “I’m proud to join Rep. Schneider and other Ways and Means colleagues in introducing the BAD DEAL Act to repeal this antiquated authority under Section 338 and refund the duties American businesses have already been forced to pay. It is long past time for Congress to reclaim its constitutional authority over trade and put an end to this Administration’s destructive tariff regime.”

“Every American deserves a fair shot to get ahead, and Trump’s capricious and costly tariffs are making it exceedingly difficult to simply make ends meet,” said Rep. Schneider. “President Trump’s brazen and counterproductive trade war only damages the long-standing, mutually beneficial relationship with our neighbor, and second largest trading partner, Canada. This is a bad deal! It’s a bad deal for American families, and it’s a bad deal for American small businesses. I’m proud to work with my colleagues to introduce the aptly named BAD DEAL Act to repeal this outdated tariff authority AND refund the tariff duties paid. We will continue fighting to rein in Trump’s costly tariffs and reassert Congress’ authority before his on-again, off-again trade policy damages our international relationships for years to come.”

In addition to Rep. Panetta, cosponsors of the BAD DEAL Act include Reps. Don Beyer (VA-08), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Greg Stanton (AZ-04), and Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10).

In 2025, Rep. Panetta joined Rep. Schneider in introducing the Repealing Outdated and Unilateral Tariff Authorities Act, which would repeal Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930.

Full text of the bill is available here.

Rep. Steven Horsford issued the following statement in response to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit's ruling against prediction markets offering sports betting.

“Today, the Ninth Circuit affirmed what Nevadans have always known: prediction markets are gambling. This ruling is an important victory for States’ and Tribes’ authority to regulate gambling.

But the fight is not over. We must continue working to protect consumers, ensure young people aren't targets, preserve state and Tribal rights, and safeguard gaming workers across the country. This issue is far from settled and will likely make its way to the U.S. Supreme Court. Congress must act now to make clear, once and for all, that sports betting - and gambling at large - belongs under state and Tribal gaming laws.

“It is time to stop unelected regulators from bypassing states by passing my bipartisan Prediction Markets Are Gambling Act. This legislation would close the loophole that allows prediction market platforms to offer sports betting and casino-style games. Prediction markets must play by the same rules as traditional gaming operators, including the same consumer protections and licensing requirements.

“The message from the Ninth Circuit is clear. Now it is time for Congress to act and make this principle the law of the land.”

The unanimous ruling was issued by a three-judge panel consisting of judges appointed by President Donald Trump. The case originated in Nevada, where state regulators sought to prohibit Kalshi from offering prediction-market contracts tied to sporting events. Additionally, new analysis by CNN found that young adults between 18 and 21 - who are legally barred from most gambling in the United States - have traded an estimated $5.4 billion so far this year on Kalshi.

title: Horsford Demands Congress Close Prediction Markets Loophole After Court Win: ‘The Fight Is Not Over’
