U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and Diana Harshbarger (R-TN-01) introduced the Automotive National and Economic Security Act of 2026, bipartisan legislation that would direct the U.S. Secretary of Commerce to conduct a comprehensive study of the national and economic security risks foreign adversaries pose to the United States automotive industry.

“I'm a car girl—I will always fight for our auto workers and this critical industry that is the backbone of America's economy. I am proud to help lead this bipartisan piece of legislation that will create good-paying jobs and protect our national security. And we must continue our efforts to decrease our reliance on China and create a level playing field,” said Congresswoman Debbie Dingell.

“China has a playbook, and we've watched them run it on critical minerals, shipbuilding, and batteries,” said Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger. “Now they're setting their sights on the global automotive market, building out their industrial base with state subsidies and flooding markets with artificially cheap products to undercut American manufacturers. As vehicles become more connected and software-driven, that strategy isn't just an economic threat, it's a national security threat and a risk to the data of every American behind the wheel. This bill gives policymakers the facts we need to understand how deep this penetration goes and to protect our automotive industry before it's too late.”

Specifically, the study would examine:

Foreign ownership of, and state-directed investment in, U.S. automakers by foreign military organizations, political parties, and state-owned enterprises.

Joint ventures, subsidiaries, and commercial partnerships between U.S. manufacturers and foreign adversaries.

Transfers of critical and emerging technologies to foreign adversaries.

Impacts on U.S. national security, economic competitiveness, and intellectual property protection.

The bill requires the Secretary of Commerce to submit findings to the House Energy and Commerce Committee and the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, and to publish an unclassified report, within two years of enactment.

Households already enrolled in the SNAP program in eight ZIP codes are eligible: 38004, 38108, 38111, 38115, 38116, 38119, 38126 and 38141. The number of SNAP beneficiaries in the affected area is estimated at 65,222. The total monthly issuance of benefits to the affected areas is $29,682,489.

Normally, recipients would be required to request replacement benefits within 10 days of an emergency or disaster, but the waiver gives recipients until September 11.

Congressman Cohen made the following statement:

“The severity of the damage and length of time electric power was out after Saturday’s storm makes these sensible waivers necessary. I am hopeful affected recipients will take advantage of this prolonged application period.”

SNAP enrollees can apply for replacement benefits through the Tennessee Department of Human Services through the state’s One DHS portal at https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp.

# # #
title: Congressman Cohen Announces SNAP Timely Reporting Waiver and Mass Replacement of SNAP Benefits for Shelby County

“A brazen and unlawful abuse of power, and a direct attack on congressional oversight”

WASHINGTON, DC — On Wednesday, the Third Circuit Court of Appeals threw out Congresswoman LaMonica McIver’s (NJ-10) motion to dismiss her case, U.S. v. McIver. Since the news broke, McIver has received a groundswell of support for the case which she said in a Wednesday statement is “not over.” One thing is clear: The case against McIver is not only baseless, but it poses a threat to democracy. The people are talking and they’re not happy about this outcome. Here’s what they’re saying.

What lawmakers are saying:

“Donald Trump wants Congressmembers to fall in line & not conduct oversight of detention centers. And he wants to make an example out of @RepLaMonica. But we’re not letting up.” (Rep. Ayanna Pressley)

“Criminalizing oversight deters lawmakers from holding Trump accountable—even if Democrats take back Congress. LaMonica is strong and won’t be intimidated, but the continued attacks on her for doing her job is dangerous to our democracy.” (Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman)

“Trump weaponizing the Department of Justice to target members of Congress simply for doing their jobs is straight out of his corruption playbook. It’s a brazen and unlawful abuse of power, and a direct attack on congressional oversight.” (Gov. Mikie Sherrill)

What the press is saying:

“Between going to doctor’s appointments, attending congressional hearings, serving her constituents, meeting with her lawyers, raising money for her defense and continuing to keep a spotlight on the treatment of immigrants in detention, McIver isn’t just fighting for her seat — she’s fighting for her freedom.” (Errin Haines, The 19th)

“McIver faces up to 17 years in prison if convicted in the case. She argued that the charges brought against her were for political reasons, citing numerous statements by the Trump Administration, President Trump himself and former prosecutor Alina Habba, who initially brought federal charges against McIver before leaving her position and becoming an aide in the administration.” (Brandon Caldwell, TheGrio)

What advocacy groups are saying:

“One of the more troubling features of the current administration is its apparent penchant for prosecuting perceived political adversaries of the President. The prosecution of Congresswoman McIver bears the hallmarks of just such a prosecution.” (Washington Litigation Group)

“Today’s decision is a grave miscarriage of justice… What is happening to Rep. McIver is no accident: it is an intimidation tactic aimed at silencing a sitting member of Congress who stood up to protect her community members from human rights violations.” (Fatima Goss Graves, NWLC)

“Weaponizing the DOJ to target a sitting Member of Congress undermines our system of checks and balances and threatens our democracy.” (Amol Sinha, ACLU NJ)

“The Trump administration is using LaMonica McIver as an example. It is a message to all lawmakers– if you stand up to ICE, if you fight back, we’ll come after you. Rep. McIver is showing us what fighting back looks like. Despite a split appeals court declining to drop the case, she is standing strong against these politically motivated charges… We stand with her 100%” (Vote Mama)

McIver and her legal team are currently exploring all options for moving the case forward. Those options include but are not limited to asking for the case to be heard en banc by the Third Circuit or by the U.S. Supreme Court. McIver is running for re-election and is eight months pregnant. For additional information on the upcoming developments in McIver’s case, please contact Hanna.Rumsey@mail.house.gov.
title: What They’re Saying: Responses to the Third Circuit’s Refusal to Dismiss U.S. v. McIver

This week, U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) joined more than 180 House and Senate Democrats in filing an amicus brief at the Supreme Court in the case of St. Mary Catholic Parish v. Roy. In this case, religious preschools are seeking an exemption from the nondiscrimination provision in Colorado’s universal preschool program so they can refuse to admit LGBTQ+ children or the children of LGBTQ+ people while still receiving public funding.

“It’s not complicated: organizations accepting taxpayer dollars should not be allowed to discriminate against LGBTQ+ children or parents,” said Rep. Larsen. “I urge the Supreme Court to protect LGBTQ+ families from discrimination, and Icontinue to stand with the LGBTQ+ community in Northwest Washington and across the United States.”

The members’ brief urges the Supreme Court to uphold the nondiscrimination provision and not grant a religious exemption. The brief argues that:

The Supreme Court defers to legislatures and the political process when assessing exemptions from neutral, generally applicable laws;

Petitioners’ rule would endanger numerous federal nondiscrimination laws that Congress has carefully crafted over decades; and

The Court should be mindful not to destabilize or undermine that legislative role by effectively legislating ad hoc exemptions to nondiscrimination laws.

The amicus brief is available to read here.
title: Larsen Urges Supreme Court to Protect LGBTQ+ Students from Discrimination

Today Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) announced that his DISCLOSE Act has gained 43 additional cosponsors since its introduction, bringing the total number of cosponsors to 181 in the House. Pappas introduced this legislation in March alongside U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (RI), House Judiciary Committee Ranking Member Jamie Raskin (MD-08) and House Administration Committee Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25).

The DISCLOSE Act would end the scourge of dark money in our democracy, shine a bright light of transparency on politics, and make government more accountable to the will of voters.

"Trust in our government is nearing historic lows, and we need to take action to bring greater transparency to our elections and restore Americans’ faith that their voices will be heard in our democracy,” said Congressman Pappas. “The DISCLOSE Act would stop billionaires and corporate special interests from secretly buying our elections by requiring dark money groups to disclose who their donors are and shining a light on payments made to social media influencers to promote or attack candidates. I’m thrilled to see support for this legislation grow, bringing us closer to putting the power of our democracy back in the hands of the people.”

Since the 2010 Citizens United decision, secret spending in U.S. elections by corporations, ultra-rich ideological extremists, and secretive front groups has exploded. These dark-money expenditures that corrupt our politics increased from less than $5 million in 2006 to more than $300 million in the 2012 election cycle, and topped $1.9 billion in 2024, shattering the previous record of $1 billion in 2020.

The DISCLOSE Act would restore transparency in American elections and restore fairness and accountability in our political system by:

Requiring super PACs, 501(c)(4) “dark money” groups, corporations, and other organizations spending more than $10,000 in elections and on judicial nominations to promptly disclose donors who contribute more than $10,000;

Shutting down the use of transfers between organizations to cloak the identity of the original contributor.

Strengthening prohibitions against foreign actors participating in election spending in the United States, including in state and local referenda;

Prohibiting the establishment of corporations to conceal election contributions and donations by foreign actors;

Expanding “stand by your ad” disclosure requirements to online ads and ads that may promote or attack a candidate but stop short of expressly advocating for a vote for or against a candidate; and

Requiring identification of top funders of outside groups paying for video, text, or audio political ads.

The bill has been adapted to the modern political ecosystem. The DISCLOSE Act of 2026 would:

Capture payments made to social media influencers to promote or oppose a candidate as political spending that must be disclosed and disclaimed;

Narrow and specify what constitutes threats and harassment to qualify for an exemption to disclosure, and put commonsense guardrails on the process to grant such exemptions; and

Allow more flexibility for disclaimers for short political ads instead of limiting it to hyperlinks.

Several prominent good-government organizations support the bill including Campaign Legal Center, Democracy Defenders Action, Public Citizen, Democracy21, End Citizens United, Common Cause, Center for American Progress, and the Brennan Center.

A summary of the DISCLOSE Act of 2026 can be found here. The House bill text can be found here, and the Senate bill text can be found here.

Background:

Rep. Pappas has been an original cosponsor of the DISCLOSE Act since he came to Congress. He led efforts to pass the DISCLOSE Act in the 118th Congress following the retirement of Rep. David Cicilline.
title: Pappas Announces 43 New Cosponsors of His Bill to End Corrupting Influence of Dark Money in American Elections, Bringing Total to 181

text:
St. Helena, CA – Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04), Chair of the Congressional Wildlife Refuge Caucus and a member of the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission (MBCC), applauded the U.S. Department of the Interior’s decision to halt proposed changes that could have weakened longstanding protections for wetland easements in the Prairie Pothole Region. The announcement came after Rep. Thompson spoke out against the proposal and more than 200,000 Americans submitted comments on the proposal.

The proposed changes could have allowed increased drainage near protected wetlands, threatening critical waterfowl breeding habitat in the region that produces more than half of North America’s migratory waterfowl.

“I'm glad the Administration reversed course on this dangerous proposal. I spoke out against these changes and urged the Administration to maintain these longstanding protections because these wetlands are critical to our migratory birds and waterfowl,” said Rep. Thompson. “The Administration never should have put these protections at risk in the first place. This is a win for conservation, but we must remain vigilant to make sure these wetlands are protected for generations to come.”

“Waterfowl nesting in the Prairie Potholes are critical for the continental migrations. Recent proposed changes from US Fish and Wildlife Service opening up voluntary conservation easements to tile draining could have been disastrous. Thank you to the wise conservation-minded hunters and fishers, and our own Congressman Mike Thompson who spoke up to defeat this sad proposed change,” said Dr. Frederic Reid, Wildlife Ecologist.

BACKGROUND

The Prairie Pothole Region spans portions of Montana, the Dakotas, Minnesota, and Iowa and produces more than half of North America’s migratory waterfowl. For more than 60 years, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) has maintained protections for wetlands covered by voluntary conservation easements.

In July, USFWS opened a 14-day public comment period on potential changes to its drain-tile setback policies. More than 200,000 comments were submitted during the review. On August 14, USFWS announced that “no further action is planned” at this time as it reviews the information received.

Rep. Thompson joined members of the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission in sending a letter to the Administration urging it to maintain the existing protections and reject the proposed changes.

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

The Honorable Doug Burgum

Secretary

U.S. Department of the Interior

1849 C Street, N.W.

Washington, DC 20240

Dear Secretary Burgum:

As Members of the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission (MBCC), we write to express our strong support for maintaining long-standing and science-based U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service wetland easement protections and the current drain tile setback standards that have allowed for the conservation of wetlands in the Prairie Pothole Region for more than sixty years while providing benefits and certainty to participating landowners. These protections are essential to sustaining North America's migratory bird populations, protecting taxpayer-funded conservation investments, and preserving one of the continent's most important waterfowl breeding landscapes.

Congress established the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission to oversee and advance the conservation of migratory birds and their habitat through strategic federal investments and collaboration and partnership with private landowners. The Commission plays a central role in reviewing and approving land acquisitions, easements, and habitat conservation projects funded through the Migratory Bird Conservation Fund, including revenues generated by the Federal Duck Stamp program, and the North American Wetlands Conservation Fund. Through these authorities, the Commission helps ensure that public conservation investments produce lasting benefits for waterfowl, other migratory birds, sportsmen and women, and the American public.

The Prairie Pothole Region produces more than half of the continent's migratory waterfowl. Wetlands protected through federal easement programs provide critical nesting and brood-rearing habitats that support waterfowl populations across the nation.

As Commissioners, we are concerned by recent actions that call into question the science-based, conservation-focused, and collaborative protections associated with permanent Fish and Wildlife Service wetland easements. These easements were voluntarily entered into by willing landowners and purchased using taxpayer resources to conserve wetlands in perpetuity. The value of these investments depends on maintaining the integrity of protected wetlands. Allowing activities that undermine wetland function would diminish both the biological benefits of these easements and the public return on decades of successful public-private wetland conservation spending.

The Commission has long championed the principle that conservation investments must be durable, provide benefits and certainty for private landowners, and manage vital waterfowl habitat using the best available science. We respectfully urge the Department of the Interior to maintain the science-based drain tile setback standards that have successfully protected Service easements for decades; uphold the integrity of voluntary easement agreements; prevent the drainage of protected wetlands; and provide landowners with legal safe harbor and the certainty necessary to fulfill their conservation commitments. Doing so will honor commitments made to willing landowners, protect taxpayer investments, support healthy migratory bird populations for generations to come, and build upon the success of this conservation model.

Thank you for your continued commitment to conserving America's wetlands and migratory bird resources.

Sincerely,

###

Congressman Mike Thompson is proud to represent California’s 4th Congressional District, which includes all or part of Lake, Napa, Solano, Sonoma and Yolo Counties. He is a senior member of the House Committee on Ways and Means. Rep. Thompson is Chairman of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force. He is also Co-Chair of the bipartisan, bicameral Congressional Wine Caucus and a member of the fiscally-responsible Blue Dog Coalition.
title: THOMPSON APPLAUDS REVERSAL OF DANGEROUS PRAIRIE POTHOLE WETLAND ROLLBACK

Hartford, CT - In advance of International Overdose Awareness Day, which is commemorated annually on August 31, Connecticut officials reaffirmed their commitment to combating the overdose crisis and bringing attention to addiction, recovery, and overdose prevention resources available to people across Connecticut.

International Overdose Awareness Day is a global campaign to end overdose, remember without stigma those who have died, and acknowledge the grief of the family and friends left behind.

“Every community across our state and the nation has been touched by the opioid epidemic. As we recognize International Overdose Awareness Day, we stand together to remember those who lost their lives to addiction and recommit to investing in prevention and treatment services. I will continue to support programs in communities that connect families with the resources they need to combat substance abuse and support those in recovery,” said Congressman John B. Larson.

“Today we mourn the lives lost to overdoses this year and commit to honoring them with action," said Senator Richard Blumenthal. "While Connecticut has made progress over the last few years to reduce the number of these tragic deaths, we need to dismantle the destructive grip addiction has on our communities. I will keep fighting for federal funding to support addiction prevention and recovery efforts.”

“Overdose deaths are on the decline in Connecticut, but addiction and mental health issues still affect the lives of countless individuals and families across the country, including the hundreds who have died from drug overdoses in Connecticut last year," said Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro. "As the lead Democrat on the Appropriations Committee, I have proudly fought for federal investments to address this addiction crisis, including against the unconscionable cancellation of grants earlier this year. I will continue to advocate for the resources necessary for those struggling with addiction.”

“Every life lost to an overdose leaves a hole in the lives of family and friends left behind. On Overdose Awareness Day, we remember those we have lost and stand with the families and communities carrying that grief. We must continue expanding access to treatment and recovery resources and ensuring that anyone struggling with addiction knows they are not alone,” said Congressman Jim Himes.

“In advance of International Overdose Awareness Day, I want to acknowledge the 836 lives we’ve lost over the past year. Each one of these individuals represents a loss in our Connecticut community and an immeasurable impact on their loved ones. Through tireless efforts across the state, countless lives have been saved, but even one overdose is one too many. This fight is not over. On this day, we commit to continuing building a future where no one in the Connecticut community experiences the loss of a loved one to overdose. Our work is not done until every person living with substance use disorder has access to the support they need not just to live, but to thrive,” said Governor Ned Lamont.

“On International Overdose Awareness Day, we reassert our state’s commitment to fighting the impacts of the overdose epidemic in Connecticut," said Lt. Governor Susan Bysiewicz. Today we remember those we have lost over the past year and honor their lives. For everyone living with substance use disorder, you are not alone. We see you and help is available. We will continue working towards creating a community where every person living with substance use disorder has the support they need for their journey towards recovery.”

“On International Overdose Awareness Day, we remember every life taken by the opioid epidemic and recognize the toll this crisis continues to take on our communities," said Attorney General William Tong. "We also stand with those who are battling addiction and the loved ones, advocates, and providers who work tirelessly to make sure they have the support they need to recover. Connecticut has fought to hold the companies that fueled this crisis accountable, helping secure more than $50 billion nationwide, including $600 million for Connecticut, for treatment, prevention, and recovery services. No amount of money will bring back the lives that were lost, but we will continue fighting to keep other families from suffering that same loss.”

“Today, we remember the people we have lost to overdose in the past year and the families and communities who continue to feel that loss," said Comptroller Sean Scanlon. "These tragedies, this epidemic, must always propel us to continue our work to combat substance use disorder in Connecticut. We must lead with compassion to face the challenge ahead and build a better tomorrow.”

“International Overdose Awareness Day is an intentional recognition of the 836 lives that have been lost to overdose in Connecticut over the past year. On this day we stand with the families and communities who carry that loss and reaffirm our commitment to saving lives. DMHAS will continue to make investments in programs focused on prevention, treatment, recovery, and harm reduction. Every person living with substance use disorder is a member of our Connecticut community and deserves our support. We will continue to fight for them to receive the care and resources they need for recovery,” said Connecticut Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services Commissioner Nancy Navarretta.

“International Overdose Awareness Day is a time to remember and honor every life lost to overdose, and to stand with the families, friends, and communities who continue to carry that loss. But remembrance must also inspire action," said Connecticut Department of Public Health Commissioner Manisha Juthani, M.D. "At DPH, we are committed to preventing overdose deaths through evidence-based prevention, harm reduction, strong community partnerships, and efforts to prevent substance use before it begins. We must also continue to replace stigma with compassion and understanding. Addiction is a medical condition, not a moral failing, and everyone deserves the opportunity to seek help, access treatment, and recover. Together, we can save lives and build a healthier future for Connecticut.”

Connecticut has made progress in reducing fatal drug overdoses in recent years. In 2025, 836 individuals died from a drug overdose in Connecticut, representing a 45% decline from the state’s peak in 2021. The number of fatal drug overdoses has declined each year since 2021. While this progress is encouraging, the loss of 836 lives in a single year underscores that the overdose crisis remains a serious public health issue and that continued prevention, treatment, recovery, and harm reduction efforts are essential.

Connecticut has dedicated significant resources toward preventing overdose, expanding access to treatment and recovery services, increasing the availability of naloxone, and reducing the stigma associated with substance use disorder. State officials and community partners continue to encourage residents to learn how to recognize and respond to an overdose, carry naloxone, and connect people struggling with addiction to treatment and recovery supports.

The following resources on addiction, recovery and overdose prevention are available to everyone in Connecticut:
title: Connecticut Officials Bring Attention to Addiction and Recovery Resources in Advance of International Overdose Awareness Day

LONG BRANCH, NJ — Congressman Frank Pallone, Jr. (NJ-06) today announced that the US Army Corps of Engineers is awarding a $38.3 million contract to Weeks Marine to begin a targeted sand replenishment project in Monmouth County, including sections of the towns of Monmouth Beach, Sea Bright, and Long Branch. In a new analysis, the consumer advocacy group Public Knowledge backed Congresswoman Lori Trahan (D-MA-03) and Congressman Jay Obernolte’s (R-CA-23) Frontier Risk Oversight, National Transparency, Independent Evaluation, and Reporting (FRONTIER) Act, calling it the strongest proposal yet to manage the risks of the most powerful AI systems.

“The frontier needs real rules, not voluntary guardrails. That requires binding legal regimes for evaluating and managing the risks from frontier models: as they are being developed, before they are deployed, and after they are in widespread use,” wrote Nicholas Garcia, Senior Policy Counsel at Public Knowledge. “The best proposal (so far) to move past frameworks, lists of principles, or nibbling at the edges of this challenge is the ‘Frontier Risk Oversight, National Transparency, Independent Evaluation, and Reporting (FRONTIER) Act’ from Representatives Jay Obernolte and Lori Trahan.”

“For years, Public Knowledge has been one of the most serious and principled voices fighting to protect the public from the risks posed by cutting edge technologies. When they engaged in the discussion draft process, we took their criticisms seriously and worked with them to address their concerns,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “That kind of rigorous, good-faith feedback is a big reason the FRONTIER Act is the strongest frontier AI safety legislation ever introduced. Public Knowledge’s support is critical as we work to broaden the coalition backing this bipartisan bill and push for its consideration. We’re in a race against the clock right now, and Congress needs to act before the next major incident.”

The FRONTIER Act would establish a tiered, risk-based national framework for overseeing the most advanced AI models. It requires the largest developers to publish their safety frameworks, submit to independent third-party audits and verification, and report critical safety incidents to a new Under Secretary of Commerce for AI Security. The bill is an updated version of the Commerce-focused portions of Trahan and Obernolte's Great American AI Act (GAAIA) discussion draft. The sponsors reworked it over seven weeks of stakeholder feedback, narrowing its preemption of state law and sharpening its auditing and reporting provisions.

Public Knowledge's endorsement marks a notable evolution. When the sponsors released the GAAIA discussion draft in June, Public Knowledge opposed it, warning that its preemption clause reached too far and would lock states out of even light-touch AI transparency and evaluation rules. At the same time, the group made clear it was ready to work with the sponsors to get the policy right.

Trahan and Obernolte took that feedback and rewrote the bill. When they introduced the FRONTIER Act in July, the preemption had been narrowed to cover only the catastrophic-risk issues the federal framework itself addresses, leaving state authority over child safety, privacy, consumer protection, and procurement intact. That change answered Public Knowledge's central concern, and the group now backs the bill.

Public Knowledge joins a broad, bipartisan coalition of AI policy experts and organizations that have praised the FRONTIER Act as the strongest federal AI safety proposal introduced to date.

Read the full analysis HERE.

###
title: ICYMI: Public Knowledge Calls the FRONTIER Act “the best proposal (so far)” for Reining In Frontier AI

SAN ANTONIO, TX — Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) released the statement below regarding a San Antonio student whose mother is being detained at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center. Today, Castro will go to Dilley for his ninth visit this year alongside the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Congressional team.

“Earlier this year, I proudly nominated David Garcia to the U.S. Naval Academy because of his academic excellence and commitment to service. He began as a midshipman this summer.

“I am calling for ICE to release David’s mom Maria immediately.”

Background:

Earlier this year, Congressman Castro successfully nominated David Garcia to be appointed to the U.S. Naval Academy. Garcia started as a midshipman this summer. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detained his mother, Maria Rocio Rocha, while she was at a U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services office for a green card interview on August 25, 2026. She was then transferred to the Dilley Immigration Processing Center, also known as the Dilley Trailer Prison.

Additional Information:

This morning, Castro joined Democracy Now! and called on ICE to immediately release Maria Rocio Rocha. Find the transcript below:

The Trump Administration, it's clear, is also targeting military families. We've seen this kind of story come up now several times.

David Garcia is an outstanding young man from San Antonio in my congressional district. I nominated him to the U.S. Naval Academy and he's there right now. Unfortunately, his mom had been granted parole in place and showed up for her green card interview and when she did, ICE took her.

Now she's sitting in that Dilley Trailer Prison as her son is at the U.S. Naval Academy as we speak. I've been in contact with ICE. I'm working on his mom Maria's case, and I'm hoping to see her today. But we were still working out getting all of the privacy and permission forms that we need.

You've got this young man who is serving his country, who absolutely represents the best of us—his mom that was doing everything right, as they say—and still, Donald Trump and his administration, with the help of governors like Greg Abbott, are targeting them.

###
title: Castro Calls for Release of San Antonio U.S. Naval Academy Midshipman’s Mom to Be Released from Dilley Trailer Prison

GARDEN CITY, NY — This past month, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04) traveled across Nassau County to deliver millions in federal funding to communities, meet directly with Long Island residents, leaders and law enforcement and support local small businesses. Rep. Gillen continues to focus on bringing resources back home to Long Island.

"This past month, I was glad to visit and support our small businesses, patrol the streets with local law enforcement and hear directly from Long Islanders about their greatest concerns,” said Rep. Gillen. “I was also proud to announce millions of dollars in new federal funding for Nassau County, including more than $1.5 million to invest in clean water, public safety and libraries, in addition to over $2 million to safeguard our houses of worship. I look forward to bringing my conversations back to Washington as I continue fighting to make life in Nassau County safer and more affordable."

Supporting Local Businesses and Entrepreneurs

Rep. Gillen toured Fresh Fizz Sodas in Island Park, meeting with owners Rebecca and Yoni Schwartz to discuss the business’s operations and the significant role small businesses play in strengthening Long Island's economy. Following this visit, Rep. Gillen also stopped by Frippery in Long Beach to meet with the boutique owner Rachel Bernstein and share how she’s supporting small businesses in Congress.

Rep. Gillen also visited and toured Soft Sips, a Black-owned small business in Baldwin, as part of National Black Business Month. Rep. Gillen met with owner Domonique Louis-Charles to hear about her journey of transforming her creativity into a thriving business and the important role Soft Sips plays in the Nassau County community.

Standing With First Responders on Long Island

Public safety remains a key concern and central focus for Rep. Gillen, who is a strong advocate for law enforcement in Nassau County. This month, she joined the Garden City, Floral Park and Rockville Centre Police Departments for patrol ride-alongs, observing each police department’s work firsthand and discussing how she can further support and deliver resources to local law enforcement across New York's Fourth Congressional District.

Rep. Gillen, who also serves as the Vice Ranking Member of the Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, visited the U.S. Coast Guard Station Jones Beach. She joined Coast Guardsmen on their patrol, heard about their work to keep our waterways safe and discussed healthcare access challenges for service members.

Delivering Millions in Community Project Funding

This month, Rep. Gillen announced over $1.5 million she secured to improve Nassau County’s water, public safety and public libraries. Rep. Gillen delivered $1 million for Long Beach’s water treatment system. She also delivered $250,000 in new federal funding to the Floral Park Fire Department for a new hook-and-ladder fire truck that will replace the current 30-year-old vehicle. Thirdly, Rep. Gillen delivered $250,000 in new federal Community Project Funding she secured to replace the roof and HVAC at Franklin Public Library.

Secured Millions in New Federal Funding to Local Houses of Worship

Watch Rep. Gillen's Announcement here.

Rep. Gillen announced over $2 million in new federal security funding for faith-based institutions that she secured through the Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP). Her office worked directly with Nassau County congregations to apply for and secure these grants. The funding will help houses of worship protect their congregations with safety enhancements, such as physical barriers, security cameras and contracted security personnel.

Speaking with Long Islanders About Skyrocketing Healthcare Costs

Rep. Gillen hosted a roundtable at Harmony Health in Roosevelt to discuss the impact of rising healthcare costs with Long Islanders. She continues to fight in Congress to extend federal tax credits to lower health insurance costs and ensure every Long Island family has access to affordable healthcare. She will bring the stories she heard at the roundtable and throughout Nassau County with her back to Washington as she continues to fight for Long Islanders.

Bipartisanship Top Grades

This month, Rep. Gillen was ranked one of the most bipartisan members of Congress. She earned a 96.5 Bridge Score and an “A” grade in the latest Bridge Grades report. Bridge Grades evaluates every member of Congress using data measuring bipartisan collaboration. She continues to work across the aisle to deliver for Long Islanders and every bill she has introduced in Congress has earned bipartisan support.

SAN JOSÉ, CA — On Wednesday at San José State University, Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), Ranking Member of the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee, convened a roundtable of civic, academic, agricultural, and technology leaders to discuss the potential impacts artificial intelligence may have on agricultural productivity and water security. California’s 18th district, containing both Silicon Valley and the Salinas Valley, is uniquely positioned at the intersection of technology and agriculture, two of California’s defining economies. Some topics during the discussion included the obstacle of broadband deployment, automated weeding and harvesting technology already at work in strawberry and celery fields, predictive groundwater modeling that could address resource constraints, and expanding ag-tech engineering pathways for students in the area.

“Congress needs to be well-informed and proactive when it comes to addressing artificial intelligence’s role in our agriculture sector,” said Rep. Lofgren. “As with other industries, this new technology presents great possibilities but also valid concerns. I wanted to hold this roundtable to hear from some of the region’s brightest minds about how AI is already shaping agriculture and what should be done to protect and develop our workforce. As the leading Democrat on the House Science Committee, listening to experts is a big part of my role, and I appreciate all of the participants who shared their insights on these important topics which impact both Silicon Valley and the Salinas Valley."

In addition to her committee leadership, Lofgren serves as an Ex Officio Co-Chair of the House Democratic Commission on AI and the Innovation Economy. She has led multiple bipartisan bills in the 119th Congress to support responsible AI innovation with necessary guardrails, including the AI-Ready Federal Data Guidelines Act (H.R. 9341) and the Workforce for AI Trust Act (H.R. 9334). Both pieces of legislation passedunanimously out of the House Science Committee in June.

The roundtable included San José State University President Cynthia Teniente-Matson; SJUSD Board Chair José Magaña; Silicon Valley Leadership Group CEO Ahmad Thomas; Reservoir VC General Partner Nicola Kerslake; Monterey Bay Economic Partnership President and CEO Tahra Goraya; Synopsys Director of Government Affairs Victoria Tung; and San José State University's Dr. Katherine Cushing, Chair of the School of Planning, Policy, and Environmental Studies.

"AI has tremendous potential to help address challenges such as water conservation, precision irrigation, groundwater modeling and crop monitoring,” from Cynthia Teniente-Matson, President of San José State University. "I am proud that so many SJSU faculty members and students are deeply interested in connecting their research with real-world challenges, while helping ensure innovation advances the public good. The opportunity before us is to move from what AI makes possible to what California needs us to make possible. I thank Congresswoman Lofgren and everyone who contributed their expertise to this important conversation."

"Congresswoman Lofgren's leadership on the House Science, Space and Technology Committee and the Democratic Commission on Artificial Intelligence gives Silicon Valley a direct line into how federal AI policy gets made," said Ahmad Thomas, CEO of Silicon Valley Leadership Group. "Conversations like this one aren't just symbolic; they're a chance to make sure the people writing the rules for AI understand what's actually happening on the ground. SVLG is proud to help build a bridge from the Silicon Valley to the Salinas Valley that lifts up the voices of all stakeholders."

"AI has real potential to help Salinas Valley growers manage water, labor, and crop health more precisely, but none of that works without the infrastructure to connect it,” said Tahra Goraya, President and CEO of Monterey Bay Economic Partnership. "At MBEP, we've seen firsthand through our broadband buildout across rural, underserved parts of our region that closing the connectivity gap isn't a side issue to AI adoption in agriculture, it's the prerequisite. Rural broadband is the infrastructure that determines whether the next generation of ag technology reaches every farm in this valley, or just the ones that can already afford to leapfrog the gap."

"AI is going to reshape nearly every career path our students consider, which means the investments we make in TK-12 STEM education today directly determine who gets to participate in that future economy,” said José Magaña, President of the San José Unified Board of Trustees. "Early exposure to STEM changes outcomes, particularly for Latino students who remain underrepresented in these fields relative to their share of California's student population. Conversations like this one, informed by Congresswoman Lofgren's role on the AI Commission, are a chance to make sure that federal AI policy doesn't just focus on innovation but that it focuses on the pipeline of talent that has to exist for that innovation to be built by, and benefit, communities like ours."

“Synopsys provides engineering solutions that help companies design and optimize complex systems, from chips to industrial equipment to digital infrastructure and more,” said Victoria Tung, Director of Government Affairs at Synopsys. "Discussions like this underscore the importance of designing technologies that meet customer requirements while balancing the needs of the communities where they are deployed.”

"AI's intersection with agriculture and water resources raises complex and important issues, requiring an approach that engages multiple research disciplines and sectors in our society,” said Dr. Crist S. Khachikian, Vice President for Research and Innovation at San José State University. "A comprehensive public research university like SJSU is ideally suited to helping us get the governance right, ensure growers of every size can put these tools to use, and prepare the workforce for the changes ahead. California agriculture feeds the nation and the expertise in that room was diverse and palpable. I thank the Congresswoman and everyone around the table for a thoughtful and meaningful conversation.”

###
title: Lofgren Convenes Experts to Discuss AI’s Potential Impact on Agriculture & Water Conservation

Congressman Ryan has been the leading voice of opposition to Trump’s war in Iran; he sits on the House Armed Services Committee, is the first West Point graduate to represent the Academy in Congress, and served two combat tours in Iraq earning him two Bronze Stars

After a March 1st Iranian drone strike killed 6 U.S. servicemembers in Kuwait, Ryan blasted Secretary Hegseth face to face for putting troops in danger, refusing to take accountability, and then calling survivors of the horrific attack liars

As the war in Iran reaches its sixth month – with 18 brave U.S. servicemembers killed and billions in taxpayer dollars spent – Ryan is continuing to demand Hegseth’s resignation and fighting to pass his No Funds for Iran War Act

WASHINGTON, DC – Today marks six months since Trump launched his war in Iran. Throughout the course of the war, Congressman Pat Ryan – who sits on the House Armed Services Committee, is the first West Point graduate to represent the Academy in Congress, and served two combat tours in Iraq earning him two Bronze Stars – has been the leading voice of opposition to the costly, deadly war in Iran. As the administration continues its war with no strategy, Ryan is escalating his calls to end the war and for Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth to resign.

“From Day 1 of this reckless war in Iran, Trump and Hegseth have lied to and betrayed the American people on every level. They lied about the timeline, lied about the cost, and left hardworking Americans to foot the bill for a war they never wanted in the first place,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “18 brave American Patriots have died because of their utter incompetence, and hundreds more have been injured while their families are left in the dark. The entire war has been a total fiasco – and instead of ending it, the chickenhawk President and unfit SecDef are doubling down on a losing strategy. I’m going to keep fighting everyday, with every fiber of my being, to end this war, bring our troops home, and hold everyone accountable – especially Hegseth – for this historic disaster.”

In the first week of the war, President Donald Trump said it would take “four to five weeks” to achieve the war’s objectives. Six months later, 18 brave U.S. servicemembers have been killed – 6 of whom were knowingly sent to an unfortified position and denied additional protection – at least 750 more have been injured, and zero objectives have been achieved.

A Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll found that 61 percent of Americans believe using military force against Iran was a mistake, making Trump’s war as unpopular among Americans as the Iraq War during the peak of violence in 2006 and the Vietnam War in the early 1970s.

The Pentagon’s internal overall cost estimate has exceeded $100 billion. That number doesn’t even account for the cost to the American people. Gas prices have soared, as people across NY‐18 have spent an additional $172 million on gas since the beginning of the war, costing the average family in our district an additional $646 in gas costs over the past six months. Grocery prices have also skyrocketed as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

Ryan has repeatedly cosponsored and voted in favor of War Powers Resolutions to end the war in Iran five separate times.

In May, amid reports that the Pentagon would seek $200B in supplemental funding for the war, Ryan introduced the No Funds for Iran War Act, which would prohibit the use of additional taxpayer funds for military action against Iran in the absence of an Authorization for the Use of Military Force (AUMF) or official declaration of war from Congress. Ryan introduced the legislation with the support of his fellow Democratic veterans in Congress, and it has continued to grow in support in the enduring months of the war.

In April, Ryan confronted Hegseth himself during a House Armed Services Committee hearing, pressing him on his failure to protect troops at Port Shuaiba. Following new reporting on the strike on Port Shuaiba, Ryan opened an investigation in August into how the Department of Defense failed to provide adequate medical care to service members injured and demanded answers about the Department's lack of preparation for a strike against Port Shuaiba.

Last month, Ryan spoke on the House floor against handing Hegseth’s Pentagon a $1.5 trillion blank check through the FY27 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). He criticized colleagues for again refusing to consider his No Funds for Iran War Act, especially following the successful passage of a War Powers Resolution.

“It's personal to me. Having served twenty-seven months in combat in Iraq. Watching us double down on a losing strategy, year after year, while my friends and fellow soldiers – many of whose names are on this memorial bracelet I wear – fought and died. It's personal to the now eighteen families who lost their loved ones in this reckless war in Iran — sons, daughters, husbands, wives, somebody's whole world. It’s personal to the hundreds more wounded, many carrying injuries that will last their entire lives from this war,” Ryan said on the House floor.

Ryan’s full floor remarks can be viewed here.

Most recently, when the Trump administration tried to downplay the number of casualties in the war, Ryan again joined his Democratic veteran colleagues in demandingthe Administration accurately and transparently account for U.S. servicemembers killed and wounded in the Iran war.

Congressman Ryan is a U.S. Army veteran, served two combat tours in Iraq, and is the first West Point graduate to represent the Academy in the U.S. House of Representatives. Amid recent threats to veterans’ benefits, national security concerns, and rising threats worldwide, Congressman Ryan led his fellow veterans in Congress to create the Democratic Veterans Caucus. He sits on the House Armed Services Committee and has led extensive legislation to deliver relief for veterans, servicemembers, and military families.

Washington, DC – Today, Congresswoman Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Ranking Member of a Subcommittee on the Homeland Security Committee, led 28 colleagues in opening an investigation into a new data-sharing agreement between the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) that has resulted in a spike in immigration enforcement activities at airports across the country. In the inquiry, the members raise the possibility of violations of privacy and civil liberties, as well as safety concerns, for all U.S. residents and international visitors traveling through airports. The letter was co-led by Congressman Robert Garcia (CA-42) — Ranking Member of the Oversight Committee, Congressman Henry C. "Hank" Johnson (GA-04), and Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib (MI-12).

The inquiry directed to the Department of Homeland Security follows American Oversight obtaining a partially redacted memorandum of agreement (MOA) signed in May 2025 that formalized a new data-sharing partnership between TSA and ICE. The agreement documents that TSA is sharing personally identifiable information, including passenger names and birth dates, and other data with ICE to conduct immigration enforcement, contradicting former Acting TSA Administrator Ha Nguyen McNeill’s sworn congressional testimony that TSA does not send such information to ICE.

“Handing travelers' private information over to immigration officers for the purposes of conducting immigration enforcement without warrants or due process violates long-standing safeguards meant to protect the safety and rights of the American people. TSA must acknowledge the dangerous precedent associated with forging secret agreements that allow the government to expand how it uses residents’ personal information absent consent, guardrails, transparency, or oversight,” wrote the Members. “The consequences of such action reach far beyond immigration and raise profound concerns about privacy, civil liberties, and public trust. TSA and ICE must change course immediately.”

According to a Reuters report, as of April 2026, TSA reportedly shared the personal information of more than 31,000 travelers with ICE, which led to more than 800 immigration-related arrests. Since TSA and ICE have not publicly disclosed the unredacted information-sharing agreement, it remains unclear how information is shared and why immigrants are targeted for arrest.

The department has until September 7, 2026, to provide details about the agreement and its effect on immigration enforcement and travelers' privacy.

The letter was signed by Representatives Judy Chu (CA-28), Lou Correa (CA-46), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Danny Davis (IL-07), Diana DeGette (CO-01), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), John Garamendi (CA-08), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Dan Goldman (NY-10), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Jahana Hayes (CT-05), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Robin Kelly (IL-02), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Morgan McGarvey (KY-03), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Emily Randall (WA-06), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Adam Smith (WA-09), and Jill Tokuda (HI-02).
title: Ramirez, Garcia, Johnson, Tlaib Lead Congressional Inquiry Into TSA Data Sharing, ICE Enforcement at Airports

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Marc Veasey (TX-33) is calling on the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to expedite the release of Elmira Azizi, an Iranian Christian pastor currently detained at the Prairieland Detention Center in Alvarado, Texas, after she was granted asylum in the United States. Azizi fled Iran after facing persecution because of her Christian faith. According to her attorneys, she has now been granted asylum, has no criminal record, and remains in federal immigration custody while awaiting DHS to complete the process necessary for her release. Azizi suffers from a life-threatening medical condition which she was able to successfully manage prior to detention. During her detention, Azizi’s health has rapidly deteriorated, and her declining health has now left her reliant on a wheelchair. “Elmira came to this country seeking refuge from religious persecution, and the United States granted her asylum. She has no criminal record, and there is no reason for allowing bureaucratic delays to put her life at further risk,” said Congressman Veasey. “Elmira has been detained for months without real justification, all the while her health has been rapidly deteriorating. She is now in a wheelchair, and is still not receiving the necessary medical care. “DHS must act with the urgency her condition demands, complete the remaining process, and release Elmira so she can get the life-saving medical treatment she desperately needs.” Congressman Veasey’s office has previously raised concerns regarding conditions and access to information and services for individuals detained at the Prairieland Detention Center. After several reports of alarming conditions and poor treatment of detainees, Congressman Veasey conducted several oversight inspections and alerted DHS and ICE to the concerns.

Today, joined by members of the Congressional Black Caucus, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries delivered remarks at the 63rd Anniversary event for the March on Washington hosted by the National Action Network and Drum Major Institute.

LEADER JEFFRIES: It’s a high honor and a distinct privilege to stand with my colleagues in the Congressional Black Caucus, Reverend Sharpton, the King family, the National Action Network and the civil rights community as we commemorate the 63rd anniversary of the March on Washington and prepare for the battles ahead.

We certainly have come a long way in the United States of America, but we still have a long way to go. These are challenging times in this country right now. We have a hater in the White House, a reckless and costly war of choice raging in the Middle East, a Supreme Court that’s out of control. Black unemployment is up, Black home ownership is down and Black political representation is under assault with Jim Crow-like tactics all throughout the South. Challenging times. Wickedness in high places. But we’re not distressed because our community knows how to make a way out of no way.

We’re facing a crossroads right now here in the United States of America. The question is which direction will we choose? We want to move America forward. The extremists are trying to turn back the clock. We’re working hard to bring people together. The extremists are tearing the country apart. We believe in truth and reconciliation. The extremists want to erase our history, but Black history is American history. Our story will never be erased.

And so we come today in the spirit of Frederick Douglass. We come today in the spirit of Sojourner Truth. We come today in the spirit of Jackie Robinson. We come today in the spirit of Rosa Parks. We come today in the spirit of Martin Luther King, Jr. We come today in the spirit of Muhammad Ali. We come today in the spirit of Fannie Lou Hamer. We come today in the spirit of Adam Clayton Powell, Jr. We come today in the spirit of Shirley Chisholm. And we come today in the spirit of the great John Lewis, because it’s time for us to get into some good trouble. Necessary trouble. Good trouble.

We fight for liberty and justice for all. We fight for equal protection under the law. We fight for free and fair elections. We fight for work, wages and wealth creation. We fight for jobs and freedom. We fight for racial justice. We fight for economic justice. We fight for social justice. We fight for civil rights. And we fight to pass the John Robert Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act so we can end the era of voter suppression in the United States of America once and for all.

So let’s continue to show up, to stand up and to speak up to make this country the best version of herself. And when we do, together, I’m confident that we will win the day, win the week, win the month, win the year, win the hearts and minds of the American people and then on November 3rd, win back control of the United States House of Representatives so we can end this national nightmare and continue our march toward a more perfect union.

Full remarks can be watched here.

WASHINGTON – Today, Congresswoman April McClain Delaney alongside U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (all D-Md.) announced $240,000 in federal funding for infrastructure upgrades at Frederick Municipal Airport’s air traffic control tower. The investment will fund the rehabilitation of the tower’s HVAC system. This funding is in addition to $1.6 million in federal support that the lawmakers have secured for other infrastructure projects at Frederick Municipal Airport, which serves as a reliever airport for Baltimore Washington International Airport and supports local business and a range of community-related operations, including emergency medical needs.

"As Frederick County continues to grow, we need infrastructure that grows with it,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney. “This $240,000 federal investment will modernize Frederick Municipal Airport’s air traffic control tower, strengthen safety and reliability, and support an airport that is critical to our local economy. I’m proud to work with Senators Van Hollen and Alsobrooks to bring federal dollars home and deliver for Frederick County.”

“As Maryland’s second busiest airport, Frederick Municipal Airport serves as a local economic hub, driving regional businesses, bringing visitors to Maryland, and supporting the surrounding community with a broad array of services. That’s why we’ve worked to support the airport’s modernization and deliver federal investments to upgrade its infrastructure. This investment will help ensure the airport’s control tower has the infrastructure it needs to continue providing safe and efficient service to all travelers,” said Senator Van Hollen.

“This $1.6 million in critical federal funding will enable the Frederick Municipal Airport to continue serving Maryland—supporting small businesses, moving goods, and strengthening our health care response. This investment will improve our infrastructure, strengthen our economy, and help keep Marylanders safe,” said Senator Alsobrooks.

This investment is provided through the Federal Aviation Administration’s Contract Tower Competitive Grant Program, which was created and funded at $100 million over five years through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act passed by Congress in 2021.

title: McClain Delaney, Van Hollen, Alsobrooks Announce $240,000 for Frederick Municipal Airport’s Air Traffic Control Tower

LINCOLNSHIRE, IL – Today, Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) and Congressman Wesley Bell (MO-1), joined by 70+ Democratic colleagues, urged Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao to reject any effort to rename the future USS Doris Miller (CVN-81) after reports that the Navy is considering naming the carrier after President Trump.

The future USS Doris Miller will be the first aircraft carrier named for an African American and the first named in honor of an enlisted sailor. Doris “Dorie” Miller remains one of the most celebrated enlisted sailors in American military history for his bravery and courage during the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941. The potential move to name the carrier after a sitting president would break with longstanding Navy tradition and diminish the recognition of Miller’s extraordinary acts of bravery and his service to our nation.

As home to Naval Station Great Lakes, naval tradition and history run deep throughout Illinois’ 10th District. Every enlisted sailor in the Navy begins their journey at Great Lakes, completing basic training before going on to serve our nation. The 10th District has long been proud to play a role in preparing these sailors for service, and we must continue to honor the legacy of those who have helped shape the Navy and our nation.

“A strong Navy is built on the courage and valor of its sailors, both in times of conflict and peace,” said Schneider. “Doris Miller’s extraordinary service, unwavering loyalty to his fellow sailors, and devotion to his country are a source of pride for all Americans. Honoring his legacy is the right thing to do and an opportunity to inspire future generations. Doris Miller should not be robbed of this rightful honor and am proud to join my colleagues in this effort to urge Secretary Hegseth and Acting Secretary Cao to recognize Miller’s heroism and reject another Trump vanity project.”

“The decision to name CVN-81 for Doris Miller recognized not only one extraordinary sailor, but generations of enlisted servicemembers whose courage and contributions have too often gone unnoticed and unrecognized,” the members wrote.

“We urge you to reject this plan and ensure that CVN-81 bears the name USS Doris Miller, the members concluded. “Our Navy must continue honoring the courage of those that answered their country’s call to service.”

View the full text of the letter here and below:

Dear Secretary Hegseth and Acting Secretary Cao:

We write regarding the recent reporting that the Department of the Navy is considering renaming the USS Doris Miller potentially in honor of President Trump.1 Renaming this ship after a sitting President would be unprecedented and break longstanding tradition. Most importantly, this would diminish the recognition of one of our country’s greatest military heroes. It was during President Trump’s first term that the Navy announced CVN-81 would bear Doris Miller’s name. Reversing that decision now would be a significant step backward in honoring the courage and sacrifice of those who have served our country.

The future USS Doris Miller will be the first aircraft carrier to be named for an African American and the first named in honor of an enlisted sailor. Those distinctions reflect the bravery and courage during the attack on Pearl Harbor by Doris ‘Dorie’ Miller, who was later awarded the Navy Cross, the Navy’s second-highest honor.

On December 7, 1941, Miller was serving aboard the USS West Virginia when Japan’s attack began. At the time, Miller was a Mess Attendant Third Class, and after his station came under fire, despite lacking proper training, he took control of an anti-aircraft gun and fired at incoming aircraft. Even when the ship began to sink, it was only when he ran out of ammunition did he abandon his position. But in the process, he still managed to assist his fellow wounded sailors and help them reach safety. Doris Miller’s story is one of extraordinary bravery, service, and pure patriotism. When he served, segregation restricted the roles available to Black sailors and servicemembers. Yet, when his country came under attack, Miller did not hesitate for one second to put himself in harms’ way to defend his fellow sailors and his nation. This story embodies the finest traditions of the United States Armed Forces.

Black Americans have served in every major American conflict, often defending a country that did not provide or even recognize their equal rights while home. Their service and sacrifice are an integral part of our country’s military history. The decision to name CVN-81 for Doris Miller recognized not only one extraordinary sailor, but generations of enlisted servicemembers whose courage and contributions have too often gone unnoticed and unrecognized.

In 2020, then-Acting Secretary of the Navy Thomas Modly announced the decision to honor Doris Miller by placing his name on CVN-81, the newest and most powerful warship. It was Acting-Secretary Modly who said that the decision honored “the contributions of all our enlisted ranks, past and present, men and women, of every race, religion, and background.”

Our aircraft carriers are among the most visible symbols of American military power. They are stationed all over the world, projecting strength, protecting our national security, and reminding our allies that we will have their backs at their time of need. The names these ships carry should preserve the legacies of Americans whose service, sacrifice, and leadership represent the very best of our democracy and our Armed Services.

There is no question that Dorie Miller meets that standard. His story deserves to be remembered aboard one of the most powerful warships ever constructed. There has never been a time when we have named a warship after a sitting president. Changing course now to satisfy a sitting President’s ego, especially one who dodged military service to his country, would be shamefully wrong.

We urge you to reject this plan and ensure that CVN-81 bears the name USS Doris Miller. Our Navy must continue honoring the courage of those that answered their country’s call to service.

title: SCHNEIDER, BELL, TOGETHER WITH 70+ DEMOCRATIC COLLEAGUES, URGE DEFENSE SECRETARY HEGESETH AND ACTING SECRETARY OF THE NAVY HUNG CAO TO PROTECT LEGACY OF THE FUTURE USS DORIS MILLER

WASHINGTON — This week, Rep. Lauren Underwood, a member of the House Homeland Security Appropriations Subcommittee, wrote to the Department of Homeland Security in opposition to recently reported plans to spend up to $20 million to equip U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) personnel with electric shock gloves.

The devices, known as Generated Low Output Voltage Emitters, or G.L.O.V.E., are designed to be worn by officers and administer an electrical shock when an officer makes physical contact with an individual.

“The idea that we would spend millions of taxpayer dollars to put these electric shock gloves on the hands of ICE personnel is disturbing and completely unacceptable,” said Rep. Underwood. “This agency is already out of control, and they cannot be given another tool to terrorize and brutalize our communities. These devices should not be deployed under any circumstances, and I am demanding DHS abandon this procurement.”

The manufacturer of G.L.O.V.E., Compliant Technologies, warns against using the devices on elderly people, small children, pregnant women, and people with severe disabilities. Underwood is demanding answers about what restrictions DHS will place on their use, including protections for vulnerable populations and safeguards to prevent involuntary reactions caused by an electrical shock from being mistaken for resistance and used to justify additional force.

Underwood also raised concerns about accountability, particularly given recent incidents in which DHS’s initial characterization of use of force encounters has been contradicted by video and other evidence, as G.L.O.V.Es can administer shocks without leaving burns, marks, or scars,

The letter comes just weeks after Underwood met with DHS leadership about gaps in body worn camera deployment, where officials cited the significant costs of fully equipping ICE and CBP personnel with cameras. Underwood questioned why DHS is prepared to spend up to $20 million on electric shock gloves while those gaps remain.

WEST HOLLYWOOD, CA — On August 26, 2026, Congresswoman Laura Friedman (D-Los Angeles) convened a panel of the region’s top transportation officials alongside U.S. Representatives Ted Lieu (D-Los Angeles), Maxine Waters (D-Los Angeles), Judy Chu (D-Los Angeles), and Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-Los Angeles) to examine what the 2026 FIFA World Cup revealed about Los Angeles County’s readiness to move millions of people during the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games. The panel came just weeks before Congress decides how much federal funding Los Angeles gets for the Games.

The panel brought together the agencies that run public transit across the region:

LA Metro Chief Customer Experience Officer Jennifer Vides, who spoke to what the agency needs to move visitors across dozens of venues over sixteen days, including the buses, operators, and storage capacity a Games-scale operation requires and the capital projects Metro is working to finish before 2028.

Los Angeles Department of Transportation General Manager Laura Rubio-Cornejo, who runs the second largest municipal transportation department in the country and is delivering street and transit improvements before 2028, including an additional zero-emissions bus maintenance facility.

City of Santa Monica Department of Transportation Director Anuj Gupta, who oversees the Big Blue Bus and a department of more than 470 employees in a city that will host no Olympic venues but will be the site of at least a dozen nation houses.

LA Metro Chief of Police and Emergency Management Bill Scott, who led Metro's security coordination during the World Cup and is standing up the agency's new in-house Transit Community Public Safety Department while preparing for the 2027 Super Bowl and 2028 Games.

“I am honored to represent California’s 36th Congressional District, which will host the Olympic Athletes Village at UCLA and the first LA 28 medal event, the Women’s Triathlon in Venice Beach. Ahead of the Olympics, we must ensure that athletes are able to get to and from their events safely and efficiently. Just as importantly, we must make sure the millions of Angelenos and visitors from around the world attending the Games can reliably travel to the venues while minimizing traffic impacts on Los Angeles County residents,” said Congressman Lieu. “I look forward to working with my colleagues to secure the federal funding needed to address Los Angeles’ critical transportation and security needs.”

“The World Cup proved that Los Angeles can deliver, but eight matches at one stadium over five weeks is not the same as sixteen days of events at dozens of venues across the region,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman. “The agencies responsible for moving those visitors have never had to work at that scale together. So, we brought them into one room to tell Congress what they need to pull this off, and when they need it because the window for that closes in weeks, not years. I am going to keep fighting to bring our tax dollars home, and to make sure what this region builds for 2028 is still serving Angelenos long after the Games leave town.”

"The American Decade of Sports is an opportunity for Los Angeles to shine bright on the world stage while leaving our region better than fans found it," said Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove. “Hosting successful games and delivering lasting benefits for our community starts with investing in our transportation infrastructure. The 2026 World Cup was the ultimate test run for the 2028 Olympics, and convenings like today help us learn from the past so we can build a safer, more accessible, and better-connected LA long after the Olympic flame is extinguished."

WHAT THE WORLD CUP SHOWED:

More than 212,000 rides were taken on Metro’s enhanced bus service to and from SoFi Stadium at $1.75 each way.

Enhanced service included direct shuttles connecting the stadium to 15 transit hubs across Southern California.

June system ridership was 2 million riders higher than last June, with Metro recording its highest single-day ridership of the month on June 18.

Metro CEO Stephanie Wiggins has said there were zero major security incidents during the tournament.

WHAT THE 2028 GAMES REQUIRE:

Metro has requested approximately $2 billion for its Games mobility plan. Congress approved only $94.3 million earlier this year.

The House Appropriations Committee approved $875 million for the request in its FY27 Transportation, Housing and Urban Development bill. This has not been signed into law and falls short of what Los Angeles will need to make the games safe and secure.

The President’s FY27 budget request did not include funding.

Metro needs approximately 1,700 additional buses against a current fleet of roughly 2,100, and has secured roughly half of that total to date.

The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act expires September 30, 2026.

Metro has publicly stated that without the full request, the complete scope of the Games Enhanced Transit System would not be feasible.
title: REPS LIEU, FRIEDMAN, CHU, KAMLAGER-DOVE, & WATERS CONVENE LA’S TRANSPORTATION LEADERS ON OLYMPIC READINESS

CARNEGIE, PA – Today, Congressman Chris Deluzio (D-PA-17) and Congressman Brad Finstad (R-MN-01) announced the reintroduction of the Water Authority Cybersecurity Protection Act. This now bipartisan bill doubles the amount of funding available in certain grants and technical assistance to local water authorities to strengthen cybersecurity efforts.

Congressman Deluzio first introduced the bill in December 2024 following an Iranian-based hack of the Municipal Water Authority of Aliquippa on November 24, 2023 that suddenly shut down water pressure technologies. Congressman Deluzio led a call for a Department of Justice investigation into the incident.

Since then, hackers have launched cyberattacks on water systems across the country. So far in the summer of 2026, at least 12 states have reported possible cyberattacks to their water systems—with some experiencing flooding and reduced water pressure or going offline completely. At least 100 municipalities have reported potential hacking efforts to their water systems. U.S. intelligence again suggests that Iranian hackers are to blame.

“Any attack on our nation’s critical infrastructure is unacceptable, and the 2023 Iranian hack in Western Pennsylvania should have been a major wake-up call for our federal government,” said Congressman Deluzio. “Especially while the Iran War continues, we need to make sure our local water authorities have the resources and training they need to defend against cyber threats from the Iranians and others. Residents should be able to trust that their drinking water is safe from attacks. I am proud to reintroduce the Water Authority Cybersecurity Protection Act to help local leaders better secure our water system.”

“We have seen far too many instances of cybersecurity threats to our critical water systems,” said Rep. Finstad. “Just this summer, Minnesota experienced over 30 cyberattacks targeting operational technologies that our communities rely on. I am proud to join Congressman Deluzio in introducing this important, bipartisan legislation that will help ensure our local water authorities have the proper capabilities to respond to threats from foreign adversaries."

This legislation would renew the Drinking Water Infrastructure Risk and Resilience Program through 2029 and provide grants to owners and operators of community water systems based on community size. The bill authorizes $50 million each fiscal year to assist local water authorities plan, design, and implement programs for emergency responses. Key among these is improvements for automated and remote systems, and training programs for security and resilience.

The full text of the bill is available here.

title: Deluzio, Finstad Reintroduce ‘Water Authority Cybersecurity Protection Act’ Following Recent Hacks on Water Systems Across America

MINNEAPOLIS – Today, Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN) released the following statement to commemorate the one year anniversary of the mass shooting at Annunciation Catholic School in her district.

"Today, our community gathers to remember Fletcher Merkel and Harper Moyski, honor the survivors, and stand with every child, family, educator, parishioner, and first responder whose life was forever changed by the tragedy at Annunciation one year ago.

"Fletcher and Harper were targeted while doing something so innocent: sitting in prayer at the first all-school Mass of the school year. As a mother, I cannot imagine the heartbreak their families have endured. As a Minneapolis resident and your representative, my heart remains utterly shattered. I refuse to accept that this is the reality our children must grow up in.

"Annunciation Church has been a fixture of our Southside community for more than 100 years. My district office is just 10 minutes away, and members of my staff have deep ties to this church. They have celebrated weddings, baptisms, and first communions there. This tragedy struck not only a school and a parish, but a community that we hold close to our hearts.

"At the heart of today is a simple belief: one meaningful way we can remember is by showing up for others and moving our feet. Through acts of service and generosity, we can carry forward the love, courage, and care that have surrounded the Annunciation community over the past year. But remembrance must also be coupled with action.

"Gun violence is the number one killer of children and teens. Our leaders at every level of government have an obligation to confront this crisis and keep our children safe. As a legislator, I continue to be ashamed by the lack of political will to act, even after Columbine, Parkland, Uvalde, and far too many other tragedies. We must do whatever is within our power to protect our kids.

"It should not be controversial to pass commonsense lifesaving measures, including banning assault weapons and high-capacity magazines. Our elected leaders should care more about the safety of our children than protecting access to weapons of war.

"We owe it to Fletcher and Harper, to the survivors, and to every single child who deserves to feel safe at school and in a house of worship to do everything in our power to prevent this from ever happening again."

###
title: Rep. Omar Statement on One Year Anniversary of the Annunciation Catholic School Shooting
