Harder’s bill expands local training programs and builds a national job training strategy based on Valley successes

STOCKTON – Today, during a tour of a local foster care and job training nonprofit, Rep. Josh Harder (CA-09) announced new legislation to scale up local workforce development programs and kickstart a national job training model in the Valley. Harder met with students and staff from Main Street Youth & Family Services, which helps vulnerable youth build skills and get hired at local businesses. Harder’s Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act, introduced with Rep. Lucy McBath (GA-06), would unlock new federal funding to not only expand these programs but also build a national workforce development model around proven local strategies.

“Finding a good-paying job to support a family on has gotten way too hard, but Valley organizations have already proven that evidence-based training can bridge that gap,” said Rep. Harder. “What we need now is for the federal government to supercharge these efforts and make sure that the next generation has the training to develop skills, get hired in high-demand jobs, and achieve lifelong career success. My bill takes what’s working in the Valley and jumpstarts efforts to build a national model around these local workforce successes.”

How the Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act scales up proven local programs:

New Federal Funding – Three tiers of funding to support the development and expansion of evidence-based employment and training programs that generate demonstrated, long-term economic improvements for jobseekers and employers.

Cuts Red Tape – Makes it easier for proven workforce programs to scale nationally without navigating the eligibility requirements of more than one hundred local workforce development boards.

Valley Leadership – Puts funding in the hands of Valley programs that are already leading the way to identify innovative and cutting-edge practices that would ensure 21st-century workers have access to sustainable, high-demand, and high-wage careers.

“At Main Street, young people learn to work by working. They staff our café and kitchen, run our shops, and even help run a worker-owned social enterprise, building the skills and the ownership stake that turn a first job into a lasting career,” said Tony Yadon, Chief Executive Officer, Main Street Youth & Family Services. “The Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act would give organizations building models like ours the federal support to grow what works and test what's promising, helping to move a whole generation toward economic mobility.”

The Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act is endorsed by Main Street Youth & Family Services, America Forward, and over 60 workforce development advocacy organizations from California and across the country.

“America Forward applauds Representatives Josh Harder and Lucy McBath for their leadership of the Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act, which would provide an accessible, efficient pathway for the development and expansion of evidence-based workforce programs across the nation,” said Deborah Smolover, Executive Director of America Forward. “As the pace of change in our labor market accelerates, this legislation ensures that high-impact organizations driving economic mobility, many of which are members of the America Forward Coalition, can nimbly and creatively respond to the needs of workers, communities, and employers.”

“I'm proud to lead the Better Jobs Through Evidence and Innovation Act alongside my colleagues, because there is more than one path to a successful career,” said Rep. McBath. “Consider the single parent looking for a more targeted training program to move into a stable, well-paying job. This legislation will modernize our workforce development pipeline, directing resources where they will have the greatest impact and supporting folks from every background chasing every kind of career.”

###
title: CAREERS: Harder Announces New Legislation to Scale Up Valley Job Training Programs Across the U.S.

PACIFIC COUNTY — Last week, Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez visited Pacific County’s Ocean Beach Health, a Critical Access Hospital in Ilwaco. Staff at the hospital gave the Congresswoman a tour of the facility, including a new MRI lab that will be paid for with federal funding that the Congresswoman helped shepherd as a member of the House Appropriations Committee. In total, the hospital will receive $1.25 million in federal funding to improve its imaging services. Following the tour of the hospital, the Congresswoman joined staff at the newly constructed Long Beach women’s and children’s clinic. The clinic will focus on care for women and young children, with a specific focus on maternal health.

Ocean Beach Hospital is one of few remaining hospitals serving communities in Pacific County and the only hospital on the Long Beach Peninsula. As a Critical Access Hospital, Ocean Beach Health is more than 15 miles from the next nearest hospital with only secondary road connections between facilities. Hospital staff voiced concerns about how the One Big Beautiful Bill’s cuts to rural healthcare will exacerbate access issues in rural America and hurt patients in Pacific County. Prior to receiving federal funding for MRI equipment, patients were forced to either travel across the Columbia River to Oregon or wait for a mobile MRI unit to be available to get imaging services.

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez speaks with hospital staff about the challenges facing rural healthcare

“When you live in a rural community, the nearest hospital might be 20 miles away and there’s a real anxiety there. You have to make tough decisions based on your access to care. People working shift jobs or moms with young kids–we don’t have time to spend three hours or more driving out just to see a doctor or get an MRI,” Said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “Supporting rural healthcare is vital to ensuring people have agency and security in making healthcare decisions and continuing healthcare access. Thank you to Ocean Beach Health for showing me what it takes to open a new health care facility in a critical access area.”

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez tours the new women and children’s clinic in Long Beach

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez is working in DC to improve access to quality, reliable health care in Southwest Washington. Over the summer, Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez successfully passed an amendment to the Fiscal Year 2027 Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies Appropriations bill directing the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to study pain management improvement strategies for miscarriage–something made worse by health care gaps in coverage and access. This Congress she also passed the Rural Veterans’ Improved Access to Benefits Act, aimed at expanding access to disability exams to veterans living in rural areas.

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez voted against H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which was signed into law on July 4, 2025. This law eliminated Medicaid eligibility for roughly 17 million Americans–including 31,000 in Southwest Washington. The bill also terminated the temporary expansion of the Affordable Care Act (ACA) enhanced premium tax credits, which helped cover health care coverage costs for lower-income households. Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez co-led the Bipartisan Premium Tax Credit Extension Act to extend these tax credits for one year, giving families more time to make these important health care decisions.

title: Gluesenkamp Perez Visits Pacific County To Tour Hospital and Discuss Rural Healthcare

Atlanta, GA – Today, Rep. Lucy McBath (GA-06) and Rep. Josh Harder (CA-09) announced new legislation to scale up local workforce development programs and kickstart a national job training model. The Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act would unlock new federal funding to expand programs which help vulnerable youth build skills and get hired at local businesses, while also building a national workforce development model around proven local strategies.

“I’m proud to lead the Better Jobs Through Evidence and Innovation Act alongside my colleagues, because there is more than one path to a successful career,” said Rep. McBath. “Consider the single parent looking for a more targeted training program to move into a stable, well-paying job. This legislation will modernize our workforce development pipeline, directing resources where they will have the greatest impact and supporting folks from every background chasing every kind of career.”

“Finding a good-paying job to support a family on has gotten way too hard, but Valley organizations have already proven that evidence-based training can bridge that gap,” said Rep. Harder. “What we need now is for the federal government to supercharge these efforts and make sure that the next generation has the training to develop skills, get hired in high-demand jobs, and achieve lifelong career success. My bill takes what’s working in the Valley and jumpstarts efforts to build a national model around these local workforce successes.”

How the Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act scales up proven local programs:

New Federal Funding – Three tiers of funding to support the development and expansion of evidence-based employment and training programs that generate demonstrated, long-term economic improvements for jobseekers and employers.

Cuts Red Tape – Makes it easier for proven workforce programs to scale nationally without navigating the eligibility requirements of more than one hundred local workforce development boards.

Local Leadership – Puts funding in the hands of local programs that are already leading the way to identify innovative and cutting-edge practices that would ensure 21st-century workers have access to sustainable, high-demand, and high-wage careers.

The Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act is endorsed by Main Street Youth & Family Services, America Forward, and over 60 workforce development advocacy organizations across the country.

“At Main Street, young people learn to work by working. They staff our café and kitchen, run our shops, and even help run a worker-owned social enterprise, building the skills and the ownership stake that turn a first job into a lasting career,” said Tony Yadon, Chief Executive Officer, Main Street Youth & Family Services. “The Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act would give organizations building models like ours the federal support to grow what works and test what’s promising, helping to move a whole generation toward economic mobility.”
title: McBath, Harder Announce New Legislation to Scale Up Job Training Programs Across the U.S.

On Friday, August 21, U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24) hosted a press conference at UC Santa Barbara’s (UCSB) OASIS Facility to highlight a $20 million grant from the National Science Foundation (NSF). The NSF grant will go towards UCSB’s COAST PCL, one of 20 facilities in a new national network of programmable cloud laboratories. Carbajal was joined by Dr. Rachel Segalman, Vice Chancellor for Research at UCSB; Dr. Ram Seshadri, Associate Dean for Research in The Robert Mehrabian College of Engineering; Dr. Javier Read de Alaniz, Co-Director of COAST PCL; and Dr. Chris Bates, Co-Director of COAST PCL.

Following the speaking program, Carbajal and the university leaders toured the COAST PCL laboratory.

Download photos here.

The $20 million grant will be used to create a remotely accessible, AI- and robotics-enabled laboratory for discovering new polymers and soft materials. Researchers anywhere in the country will be able to design experiments online, have robots conduct the experiments at UCSB, and receive and analyze the results without having to travel to the university.

The initial research focus will be sequence-defined polymers and biomolecular materials, with potential applications in medicine, energy, electronics, aerospace, and other advanced technologies. Additional background is available here.

“As a proud Gaucho, I am thrilled to highlight this $20 million grant from the National Science Foundation to support UC Santa Barbara’s COAST PCL project,” said Rep. Carbajal. “With this federal investment, UC Santa Barbara will host state-of-the-art programmable cloud laboratories, allowing researchers from across the country to perform experiments completely remotely. The work conducted right here on the Central Coast will revolutionize materials research and lay the foundation for breakthroughs across many industries, from medicine and construction to advanced aerospace and energy technology. I will keep fighting in Congress to bring our tax dollars back home to support world-changing projects like this one.”

"We are grateful to Congressman Salud Carbajal for his unwavering support of UC Santa Barbara and the pioneering research made possible through federal investment," said Rachel Segalman, UC Santa Barbara’s vice chancellor for research and a professor of materials and chemical engineering,” said Rachel Segalman, UC Santa Barbara’s vice chancellor for research and a professor of materials and chemical engineering. “AI is changing how we approach scientific discovery, but it cannot discover new materials on its own. AI needs high-quality experimental data to learn from and validate its predictions. COAST creates a powerful connection between AI, computation and experimentation, allowing researchers to generate new data, learn from it, and move more quickly toward materials that could have applications ranging from medicine and water purification to microelectronics.”

“COAST PCL is a testament to The Robert Mehrabian College of Engineering’s proud tradition of materials discovery,” said Ram Seshadri, the associate dean for research and a distinguished professor of materials, and chemistry & biochemistry. “For decades, our faculty have advanced the fundamental understanding of materials while building a culture of collaboration and shared infrastructure that allows ambitious ideas to flourish. This new investment builds on that legacy and on Dean Umesh Mishra’s vision for OASIS as a bridge between laboratory discovery and real-world impact. COAST PCL will be a key part of realizing that vision and shaping how the next generation of materials are discovered.”

“What excites me most about COAST PCL is the opportunity to rethink how experiments are designed and carried out,” said materials professor Chris Bates, who will serve as co-director of COAST PCL. “By automating workflows and making them remotely accessible, we can move toward a model where sophisticated materials research is available to anyone, anywhere, at any time. That has the potential not only to accelerate discovery, but to fundamentally change how the next generation of scientists and engineers approaches experimentation.”

“COAST PCL is about changing what is possible in materials research. A researcher anywhere in the country will be able to design an experiment remotely, have our automated systems carry it out here at OASIS, and use the resulting data to decide what to test next,” said Javier Read de Alaniz, co-director of COAST PCL and a professor of chemistry & biochemistry. “By combining remote access, robotics, and standardized data, we can accelerate discovery while giving a much broader community of researchers access to capabilities they otherwise might never have.”
title: Carbajal Highlights $20 Million Federal Grant for UCSB Advanced Research Lab

PATERSON, NJ – Congresswoman Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) today joined Passaic County officials at Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park to celebrate $1.2 million in federal money she secured with U.S. Senator Andy Kim to improve stormwater management along River Street in Paterson.

Passaic County Commissioners Orlando Cruz and Nick Veliky attended the event, along with Leonardo Fuentes, North Jersey Regional Director for Senator Kim.

The funding stems from requests from Passaic County to Pou and Kim’s offices. The requests were combined during the competitive FY2026 congressional appropriations process into a single $1.2 million award for the county.

“There could hardly be a more fitting place to celebrate this funding than at the Great Falls. Water helped build Paterson and our nation more than two centuries ago, but today we also know the damage it can cause when heavy rain overwhelms our streets and drainage systems,” said Congresswoman Pou. “Instead of waiting for the next storm, we are preparing for it. I am proud Senator Kim and I worked together to bring this federal money home. New Jersey gets the best results when our delegation works together as a team.”

"As North Jersey continues to be hit with life-threatening storms and increasingly dangerous floods, this $1.2 million investment will help the Paterson community make needed repairs to River Street to fortify their resilience efforts," said Senator Andy Kim. "It takes partnership at all levels to deliver for our constituents, and I'm grateful that Rep. Pou and I were able to secure this funding to help Paterson stay safe."

Flooding is a familiar threat across North Jersey, and especially in the Passaic River Basin. Heavy rainfall can quickly overwhelm older drainage systems, sending water into streets and threatening homes. For residents who live in flood-prone areas, these are constant concerns. A single severe storm can cause enormous damage and leave families dealing with the effects long after the water recedes. Stormwater systems like the one this money will help fund carry water away when severe weather hits.

Congresswoman Pou has made water infrastructure a major focus of her first term in Congress and serves on the House Subcommittee on Water Resources and Environment.

In response to a ruptured pipe that cut off water to four Passaic County communities last summer, Pou introduced the Water Crisis Prevention Act to help identify areas at risk of water crises and get federal aid to communities faster. Pou’s bill would also improve access to federal relief for states, towns, businesses, and residents affected by water emergencies.

The $1.2 million Passaic County award is part of Pou’s broader effort to bring federal resources directly back to New Jersey’s Ninth District. In her first term, Pou has already delivered more than $24 million in federal money for local projects across the district, supporting work identified by the communities themselves.

###
title: Congresswoman Pou and Senator Kim Deliver $1.2 Million to Fight Flooding in Passaic County

Cincinnati, OH – This week, Congressman Greg Landsman (D-OH-01) called on Ohio Governor Mike DeWine to act after failing to respond for 60 days to Hamilton County Commissioner Alicia Reece’s concerns over Duke Energy’s continued rate increases.

In June, Hamilton County Commissioner Alicia Reece sent a letter to Governor Mike DeWine regarding continued rate increases from Duke Energy and the financial strain it’s putting on Southwest Ohio families.

Reece’s letter requested three action items, and after 60 days without a response, Landsman followed up asking Governor DeWine to consider Reece’s request reading, in part:

“Commissioner Reece calls on your administration to take immediate action by establishing a moratorium on additional utility rate increases and urges your Public Utilities Commission of Ohio (PUCO) appointees to prevent rate increases. In addition, she asks for an additional $1 million to Hamilton County to assist residents with their utility costs. I’d like to express my support for taking these actions…

“There is a time for rate increases, but this is arguably the worst possible time for such an increase.”

Congressman Landsman:

“Local folks need help. At a time when families are already paying more for gas, groceries, healthcare – they shouldn’t have to worry about another big bill. We have to act now before it gets worse.”

Commissioner Reece:

“On June 18, 2026, I wrote Governor DeWine on behalf of the residents of Hamilton County to call for a moratorium on any additional electric rate increases as so many working families are struggling economically. Over 38,000 residents in Southwest Ohio have had their electric disconnected due to increased costs. This is an urgent matter and warrants immediate attention. Affordability is the number one issue.”

Read Landsman’s full letter HERE.

###
title: Landsman, Reece Call on DeWine to Rein in Energy Costs in Southwest Ohio

WASHINGTON – Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) joined Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) in leading 39 Members of Congress, including six Senators, in a letter to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, demanding the immediate and permanent release of U.S. citizen Sama Safi, a 20-year-old student with a severe chronic health condition, from Israeli military prison. On June 2, in the middle of the night, Sama was torn from her family’s home in the occupied West Bank as part of a series of raids targeting Birzeit University students.

Congresswoman Pressley also met virtually with Sama’s parents to discuss efforts for her release, and demanded accountability from the Israeli government and for the Trump administration to secure Sama’s immediate release, continued access to medical care, and end all unjust and arbitrary detentions.

“Every day that Sama remains wrongfully detained in these inhumane conditions, she is at greater risk of irreversible and life-threatening repercussions,” the lawmakers wrote to Secretary Rubio. “It is your responsibility to ensure the safety of all Americans abroad, with no exceptions. Her life is at risk on your watch. We urge you to act swiftly and use every tool at your disposal to secure the immediate release of Sama Safi so that she can receive the medical care she urgently needs and return to her family, her studies, and the life and freedom that every 20-year-old deserves.”

“With every additional day that Sama is subjected to deprivation and abuse by Israel, our fear grows that her spark is being dimmed; that we are losing pieces of her health, her strength, and the vibrant, loving spirit that makes her who she is,” said Sama’s parents. “Every morning, we wake wishing this was only a nightmare, hoping to open our eyes to the sound of Sama playing music. Every waking moment, we cannot help but imagine what she must be facing alone. Yet we are holding on to hope through those who stand with us and are helping us bring Sama home. We are deeply grateful to Congresswoman Tlaib and all the signatories of this letter for standing with us in our urgent call to free Sama.”

Sama has described horrific conditions and violence by guards in Israeli military detention, including frequent physical assault, gas and stun grenades thrown in overcrowded cells, and lack of food and water. Every day, thousands of Palestinians in Israeli detention are subjected to these conditions as part of what the United Nations Committee Against Torture described as “a de facto State policy of organized and widespread torture and ill-treatment.”

“Such wretched conditions and treatment have caused Sama’s health to rapidly decline to dangerous levels in detention. Sama suffers from a severe and complex chronic medical condition known as Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF), which requires regular monitoring, daily medication, and recurring specialized biologic treatment abroad,” the lawmakers wrote. “Sama has reported receiving her medication inconsistently, resulting in several missed doses. Stress positions and shackling have exacerbated her condition, causing severe rheumatoid and chest pain. Her doctors have warned that with her continued military detention and ‘being constantly exposed to conditions that exacerbate her inflammatory status, the possibility of progressive tissue injury and irreversible organ damage is our greatest concern.’”

On August 17, over 100 faith-based groups wrote a letter to Secretary Rubio demanding Sama’s release.

In reaction to a proposal for a major overhaul to the federal Head Start program by the Trump administration, Gov. Maura Healey and three members of the Massachusetts federal delegation are calling on the president to reverse the newly proposed standards they say will “dismantle” the program in the Bay State.

The proposed changes to the program, according to the U.S. Dept. of Health and Human Services (HHS), would give individual states more flexibility regarding the curriculum, staff-to-student rations, and group sizes. It would also lower the cap on administrative expenses from 15% to 5% in an effort to reduce overhead costs and introduce new nutritional requirements along with baseline requirements for physical activity among students.

“President Trump has repeatedly targeted Head Start, and now he is trying to dismantle it from the inside out. This proposal would strip away the standards that keep class sizes small, keep kids safe and make sure they get the services they need,” Healey said Wednesday during a press conference at ABCD Head Start in Malden. “That isn’t flexibility. It means lower-quality care and fewer supports for families. We’re urging people across Massachusetts to speak out and help us protect Head Start.”

HHS says the proposed rule is projected to save U.S. taxpayers $2.2 billion while preserving or expanding up to 236,000 Head Start slots nationwide. Its the largest known reinvestment in the program since it was created 61 years ago, the Trump administration says.

“Head Start began as a bold commitment to the health, dignity, and potential of every child. My uncle, Sarge Shriver, founded the program on a simple conviction: strong families, wholesome nutrition, and healthy childhood development can change the course of a child’s life,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “Today, we are returning Head Start to those roots. We are removing unnecessary bureaucracy, strengthening nutrition and physical health, trusting parents and local communities, and opening Head Start to hundreds of thousands more children. That’s how we renew the promise of Head Start for the next generation.”

Healey and House Minority Whip and Congresswoman Katherine Clark say the new rule would provide no additional funding and eliminate federal standards ensuring consistent care for children in the program.

“They (Republicans) told us flat out in Project 2025 that their objective is to dismantle the Head Start program and spend that money on tax cuts for billionaires. First they tried to defund it totally. They wrote a budget that eliminated funding for Head Start in its entirety, and we beat that back,” added Clark.

“[The proposed rule] would increase class sizes. It would forbid the use of any language but English. It would curtail developmental screenings,” Clark continued. “Even the Republican administration has admitted that there are risks with that. But they are willing to risk our kids in order to continue to fund the very wealthiest Americans.”

Head Start serves over 10,000 children in Massachusetts, providing early education, child care, health and dental screenings, developmental supports and other services for low-income families.

Healey and Clark are urging Massachusetts residents, educators and providers to speak out against the proposed changes during the federal public comment period, which runs through October 6.

—
title: Boston Herald: Gov. Healey, Whip Katherine Clark call on Trump to reverse ‘devastating’ proposed overhaul of Head Start program

text:
San Francisco – Today, Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi joined San Francisco women leaders, workers, small-business owners and disability advocates at San Francisco City Hall to commemorate Women’s Equality Day and the 106th anniversary of the certification of the 19th Amendment.

The event featured Kim Tavaglione, Executive Director of the San Francisco Labor Council; Lauren Crabbe, Owner and Founder of Andytown Coffee Roasters; Kelly Dearman, Executive Director of the San Francisco Department of Disability and Aging Services; and Sascha Bittner, Commissioner on the San Francisco Disability and Aging Services Commission.

Speakers celebrated the generations of women who fought to secure and expand the right to vote while sounding the alarm over renewed Republican efforts to restrict access to the ballot. The SAVE America Act would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, threatening to disenfranchise millions of eligible Americans—including nearly 70 million married women whose current names do not match their birth certificates.

The event also highlighted the Trump Administration’s assault on mail voting and attempt to seize federal control over elections, including an executive order directing federal agencies to create centralized voter lists and subject state and local election officials to new federal mandates.

View photos from today's event here.

Read Speaker Emerita Pelosi's remarks as delivered below:

Speaker Emerita Pelosi.

They said women would have to wait. Women did not wait.

We worked, we demonstrated, we had hunger strikes. There were quite a few that were rejected from their families. They had courage to make a difference. Part of that was tied into the abolitionist movement. Fredrick Douglas was a great suffragist as well as an abolitionist. For many of the women who were working all that time came from that community as well....

So when it happened over 100 years ago, it was cause for great jubilation. I visited Tennessee on a number of occasions to see what they had done to commemorate the fact that Tennessee was the last state to ratify that amendment to the Constitution.

So again, it's a happy day for all that they did. But everything we do is about the future. And the future is impaired by what the White House is trying to do now, with the "Save Act."

Just for an example, because we can talk more about it if you have questions about it, but I'll give you the provisions here. My name, first born Nancy D'Alesandro, a long time ago in Baltimore, Maryland, thousands of miles away. This bill says that's in in my house today. Now just think of women having to go back and get their birth certificate so they can go over a name that they haven't used for decades.

This especially affects older women, some younger than me. But my kids—half of them use their own name, Pelosi, but half of them use their married names. But for you to marry him, you may not be able to vote. Is that a problem? When they think this up?

I'm a long way into this. I won't start over. I will use my mother of five voice in the mean time. So what we have to do right now is protect what the suffragists did and also what it meant to our country, because the right to vote is about policy.

I'm so glad that the women who are here today are making their own mark. They are able to do that because of policy that helps women succeed, whether it's in the workplace, in the neighborhood, and all the rest. So we cannot allow this so-called "Save Act."

They can't win on the policy. They cannot win on the policy. Even denying that affordability is an issue, that the cost of living is up.

So this is a fight that we are engaged in and of course, this morning you may have seen—I don't have all the particulars here but all the Democratic committees have spoken out against what the Supreme Court did the other day.

I'll just say this about affordability. I have a daughter that raised three teenage boys. She told me her grocery bill now for just her and her husband is more than it was when she was feeding three very hungry children.

So affordability, Mr. President, is an issue. So don't bring that up with us. So anyway, as a salute to the women who made this happen, women in the African American community very much a part of it, not as recognized as I think they—as many of us agree, they were not recognized enough, but we are changing that. As well as just all the people who made it possible.

We can talk more about—I get enthusiastic about it, we can talk more about it as we go along. But again, I'm particularly happy because the first woman Speaker of the House gavel was part of the 250th anniversary of the unfolding of increasing democracy in our country.

With that, I'd like to introduce Kim Tavaglione, whom I've learned so much from. She's the Executive Director of the San Francisco Labor Council and she has been an advocate for women in the workforce and women in society in so many ways. I'm honored to have her with us this morning.

Thank you.
title: Pelosi Marks Women’s Equality Day: “They Said Women Would Have to Wait. Women Did Not Wait.”

Today, Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07) announced that her office has successfully resolved more than 17,000 matters for residents of Texas’ Seventh Congressional District. Her office assists residents with matters before federal agencies, including obtaining benefits from Social Security, Medicare, and the Department of Veterans Affairs, as well as addressing matters before the Small Business Administration, United States Citizenship and Immigration Services, Internal Revenue Service, and other federal government agencies.

“Every day, our team of constituent advocates works to serve our constituents on matters of all kinds, helping those seeking assistance with federal agencies,” said Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher. “I am grateful to the residents of Texas’ Seventh Congressional District who have put their trust in me and my team to help resolve some of their most pressing problems. I am proud of our team, and I look forward to continuing to serve our neighbors and helping our community in every way we can.”

Below are some testimonials from constituents Congresswoman Fletcher and her team have helped:

United States Citizenship and Immigration Services

"I contacted the office of Lizzie Fletcher two weeks ago to address an issue I had with getting my citizenship process moving as I was out of answers from contacting them myself. Within a week, I received an email from USCIS with an interview for my citizenship. I am so glad that we have people looking out for the public and taxpayers. Thank you very much to the office of Lizzie Fletcher for resolving my inquiry."

- Thomas L.

United States Department of State

“My brother and his family applied for a tourist visa in June 2023, but their application was quickly placed in administrative processing. Despite providing additional evidence for their eligibility, the case remained stalled. For two years, we reached out every six months, but the status was in an endless limbo with no clear way to track its progress.

“I wrote to Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher’s office to explain our situation. As an American Venezuelan family, we had not been able to gather since 2017, and we were in desperate need of support to move the visa forward. I also had the opportunity to meet with her constituent advocates in Alief, and they were incredibly open and receptive, especially Sofia, who offered to investigate my case.

“After two years had passed, I was already discussing the need to re-apply when an email arrived from [Constituent Advocate] Sofia, notifying me that the visas would finally be issued by the Rio de Janeiro U.S. Consulate! Their swift intervention helped to get the process back on track. This [meant] that our three siblings and our entire family—separated for seven long years—[could] be reunited for Christmas. I was super excited to hear the great news!

“What I most appreciate is the openness and efficiency of Congresswoman Fletcher’s office. I felt instantly heard, and they acted upon my request right away. It was my first time asking for this kind of support, and I never imagined the help could be provided so quickly. Thank you to Congresswoman Fletcher and her entire team for their hard work. You have made this Christmas an unforgettable one for our family. We will be forever grateful."

- Sheila M.

Social Security Administration

“I contacted Congresswoman Fletcher’s office because I was having difficulty with my Social Security Disability. After several phone calls to SSA, I decided to contact Representative Fletcher for assistance. Her office responded to me extremely quickly and was so kind in assisting me. They took their time to understand the problem and helped me resolve the issue. Within a week of talking with Representative Fletcher’s office, the problem with my disability was resolved. What I had been dealing with for months, her office resolved in a week. I can’t thank Congresswoman Fletcher and the amazing staff that she has enough. Without them, I would very likely still be trying to resolve the issue on my own. Thank you so much, from the bottom of my heart!”

- Charles L.
title: Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher Announces More Than 17,000 Matters Resolved on Behalf of Texas’ Seventh Congressional District Residents

text:
Governor Maura Healey criticized the Trump administration’s proposal to scale back regulations for the federally funded Head Start child-care program, calling it “reckless and wrongheaded” on Wednesday.

The rollback would result in more children being turned away from free child care, she said, as well as less well-trained teachers and a reduction in medical screenings, mental health services, and other support for low-income families.

“This is an attack on families and kids,” she said during a press conference after touring the ABCD Head Start center in Malden Wednesday with other elected officials and early education advocates. “This seems to be all part of Donald Trump’s plan to destroy education in this country.”

The proposed changes would do away with previous requirements on class size, health and developmental screenings, and home visits. Bilingual instruction would be eliminated outside of Indigenous communities, program hours could be shortened, and teaching standards for literacy, math, and social and emotional development would be dropped.

Head Start facilities would have to comply with state rules, but there are few comparable state-level requirements, raising concerns that quality will suffer and fewer services will be offered to some of the country’s most vulnerable families.

The federal Administration for Children and Families said the proposed rule changes would remove regulations that go beyond what the Head Start Act requires and give local providers more latitude. The program would continue to require hearing and vision screenings, family support for health, nutrition, and English proficiency, and other federally mandated provisions.

“By removing hyper-specific directives on how to meet these requirements gives recipients more flexibility to design comprehensive services best suited to their community’s needs,” the agency said in a statement.

Eliminating ”one-sized-fits-all federal mandates” could save as much as $2.2 billion a year and create 236,000 new slots, it said.

“They are willing to risk our kids in order to continue to fund the very wealthiest Americans,” said Representative Katherine Clark, who was also at the Malden Head Start Wednesday. “This is about weakening and watering down a program that serves hundreds of thousands of families across the country every day. … to free up money for billionaires.”

The administration had previously tried to freeze funding for Head Start, noting in a White House budget document reviewed by The New York Times that it would help end the “radical indoctrination of our children” in a program “riddled with social-emotional learning.” In June, a report by the Heritage Foundation, a conservative think tank that has advised the Trump administration on past policies, called for the administration to “sunset Head Start and deregulate the program until officials end it.”

Massachusetts receives $190 million a year to serve about 10,000 children, in addition to $20 million supplemented by the state each year to boost worker wages, said Michelle Haimowitz, executive director of the Massachusetts Head Start Association.

This would have a definite impact at the Head Start program in Malden, which has 13 teachers and 10 support staff serving 110 children, said director Georgette Chiasson. The state’s strict student-teacher ratios would protect instructors, she said, but the number of support staff who meet with families and provide health support and other services would have to be cut.

Massachusetts has some of the highest standards for health and safety, said Amy Kershaw, the state’s Early Education and Care commissioner, but Head Start regulations go beyond what the state requires.

“Our health and safety standards can’t replace what the federal government is trying to take away,” she said.

The state has tried to make up for previous federal cuts to food programs and health care, but it can’t cover everything, Healey said.

“It’s hard with the mounting challenges and the cuts coming out of the Trump administration and Republicans in Congress,” she said.

The comment period for the proposed changes to Head Start lasts until Oct. 6, and Healey urged community members to reach out to the White House to advocate for the program.

Carmen Rondash, a single parent with four children, relied on the Head Start program in Charlestown for help with child care, early-intervention checks, and other resources his family needed.

“It’s a really important tool for people like me to change our lives, to empower us, and to let us build ourselves,” said Rondash, who is now on the board of directors for ABCD, one of 28 organizations in the state that administers Head Start programs.

Research has shown that Head Start increases the likelihood that children will graduate from high school and attend college, but it provides much more than early childhood education, said Sharon Scott-Chandler, president of ABCD.

“A child cannot learn when they are hungry,” she said. “A parent cannot always focus on their child’s education when they are worried about healthcare, housing, food, and their child’s development.”

“The education and wellbeing of our most vulnerable children are key to the success of Massachusetts.”

—
title: Boston Globe: ‘An attack on families and kids’: Healey slams Trump’s proposed Head Start changes

WASHINGTON, D.C.– Today, Congressman Maxwell Alejandro Frost (FL-10) and Congressman Jerry Nadler (NY-12) are calling on the Department of Justice (DOJ) and Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to closely scrutinize Sysco's proposed $29.1 billion acquisition of Restaurant Depot and investigate its potential anticompetitive effects. In the letter sent to the DOJ and FTC, the Congressmen warn that the deal could reduce competition, drive up costs for independent restaurants, and ultimately make dining out more expensive for consumers

Restaurant Depot currently operates 166 locations across 35 states and serves more than 700,000 restaurants and food service operators. As a direct competitor to Sysco, Restaurant Depot provides independent restaurants with an important alternative when purchasing food and negotiating prices.

“Restaurants are already struggling with rising costs, and eliminating competition in food distribution could make the problem worse. If this merger drives up the cost of food for small restaurants, those costs will ultimately be passed on to consumers. Families can’t afford another hit to their wallets, and that’s why the DOJ and FTC need to closely scrutinize this deal,” said Congressman Maxwell Frost (FL-10).

“Soaring food prices are forcing Americans to struggle to put food on the table for their families. The last thing our districts need is another bloated corporation using their unfair market power to raise food prices further. The Department of Justice must take its job seriously by fairly and carefully examining this proposed transaction to ensure that American consumers are protected,” said Congressman Jerry Nadler (NY-12), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on the Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust Committee on the Judiciary.

"Independent restaurants operate on razor-thin margins, and Restaurant Depot gives them an essential alternative to large distributors like Sysco and a critical price benchmark when negotiating with suppliers. If Sysco is allowed to acquire a major competitor, independent restaurants will lose that leverage, face higher food costs, and ultimately have little choice but to pass those costs on to diners. We thank Representatives Frost and Nadler for urging federal regulators to thoroughly investigate this deal before it does lasting harm to independent restaurants and the communities they serve,” said Erika Polmar, Executive Director Independent Restaurant Coalition.

The proposed acquisition would eliminate a major competitor to Sysco, the nation’s largest food distributor, and could give the company greater leverage over the prices restaurants pay for ingredients and supplies. For independent restaurants operating on already-thin margins, even modest increases in food costs can have significant consequences, including higher prices for customers.

Frost warned that the impact of the merger could extend beyond restaurant owners to consumers and workers. If restaurants face higher costs, they may have little choice but to pass those costs on to customers at a time when families are already cutting back on dining out because of rising prices.

The proposed acquisition could also have implications for independent farmers and growers. Sysco has touted the increased purchasing power that would result from the acquisition, raising concerns about how greater market concentration could affect the prices paid to producers.

Frost is calling on the Department of Justice and Federal Trade Commission to closely examine the proposed acquisition and launch an antitrust investigation into its potential effects on competition, independent restaurants, farmers, workers, and consumers.

Read the full letter here.

###
title: Frost, Nadler Demand Antitrust Investigation Into Sysco’s $29.1 Billion Acquisition of Restaurant Depot Over Threats of Higher Costs for Restaurants

WASHINGTON, DC — Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Subcommittee on Indian and Insular Affairs, and Congressman Jared Huffman (CA-02), Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee led 18 members of Congress in demanding answers from Interior Secretary Doug Burgum about the Trump Administration’s rushed effort to revoke protections for lands surrounding Chaco Culture National Historical Park.

The Department of the Interior is proposing to revoke Public Land Order No. 7923, which established a 10-mile mineral withdrawal surrounding Chaco Canyon. Revoking the order would reopen these culturally significant public lands to oil and gas leasing and mining activities.

“Chaco Canyon is not just a historical site; it’s a living cultural landscape,” the lawmakers wrote. “The Department’s current fast-tracked efforts to overturn the withdrawal area do not respect the historical, cultural, and spiritual value of Chaco Canyon.”

“The Department’s rushed review undermined the Department’s trust responsibility to Tribal nations and the Tribal consultation process under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act,” they continued.

The lawmakers’ letter raises serious concerns that the Department failed to fulfill its trust responsibility to Tribal nations and honor Burgum’s public commitment to meaningful consultation. During a June 2025 House Natural Resources Committee hearing, Burgum committed to Leger Fernández to send an official with decision-making authority to conduct individual, in-person consultations with every Tribe with an interest in Chaco Canyon. However, Interior’s own draft Environmental Assessment indicates that the Department moved forward before completing all requested consultations. Several Tribes received only “informational meetings,” while requests to meet with a decision-maker remained unmet.

The Department also provided only 21 days for public comment and held no public meetings before advancing its proposal. Despite that abbreviated process, the public submitted an estimated 300,000 comments.

By contrast, the existing protections were finalized in 2023 following 150 days of public comment, eight public meetings, and years of advocacy by Tribal nations. An archaeological study identified more than 4,730 cultural sites within the protected area.

The lawmakers are asking Burgum to disclose:

● How many Tribal consultations included an Interior official with decision-making authority;

● Why the Department failed to honor Tribal requests to meet with a decision-maker;

● Why Interior published its draft proposal before completing Tribal consultation;

● Whether all requested consultations will occur before the Department completes its review; and

● Why Interior conducted a limited Environmental Assessment instead of a more comprehensive Environmental Impact Statement.

The lawmakers requested answers by Friday, August 28.

The letter was signed by Representatives Teresa Leger Fernández, Jared Huffman, Melanie Stansbury, Gabe Vasquez, Sharice Davids, Betty McCollum, Eleanor Holmes Norton, Mark DeSaulnier, Val Hoyle, Donald Beyer Jr., Judy Chu, Dina Titus, Jesús “Chuy” García, Sylvia Garcia, Rashida Tlaib, Diana DeGette, Julia Brownley, and Raja Krishnamoorthi.
title: Leger Fernández Leads 18 Members Demanding Answers on Trump Administration’s Rush to Strip Chaco Canyon Protections

NAGUABO, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández Rivera anunció hoy un avance en el Congreso para atender la erosión costera en Naguabo, tras lograr incluir una medida que autoriza el estudio de soluciones para proteger comunidades vulnerables del municipio.

La medida fue incluida en la versión de la Cámara de la Ley de Desarrollo de Recursos Hídricos, conocida como el Water Resources Development Act (WRDA). Este proyecto autoriza al gobierno federal a estudiar alternativas para reducir la erosión costera y los riesgos que enfrentan comunidades de Naguabo durante huracanes y otros eventos atmosféricos. La medida ya fue aprobada en comité y está pendiente de consideración por la Cámara.

El Comisionado Residente anunció el avance durante una reunión con la alcaldesa Miraidaliz Rosario Pagán, en la que también discutieron otras prioridades de infraestructura y vivienda del municipio.

“Me place trabajar con la alcaldesa y la representante Sol Higgins para atender las necesidades de Naguabo y adelantar en el Congreso una medida para atender la erosión costera. Estamos trabajando con la alcaldesa y la representante para identificar las herramientas federales que puedan ayudar a mover otras prioridades hacia adelante”, expresó el Comisionado Residente.

Como parte de la visita, el Comisionado Residente recorrió el Cementerio Municipal en el barrio El Duque y el nuevo Centro de Salud y Servicio (CDT) de Peña Pobre, actualmente en construcción, para evaluar junto a la alcaldesa alternativas de financiamiento federal para ambas instalaciones. El Comisionado Residente reiteró que continuará trabajando con el Municipio y conectándolo con agencias federales y del Gobierno de Puerto Rico para identificar fondos que apoyen futuras expansiones del cementerio, incluyendo oportunidades a través del programa Community Facilities de USDA Rural Development, que ha defendido durante el proceso de asignaciones federales.

El Comisionado Residente también informó sobre una oportunidad federal para fortalecer los esfuerzos de rehabilitación de viviendas en Naguabo a través de los Housing Preservation Grants de USDA Rural Development. La convocatoria, abierta en Puerto Rico hasta el 8 de septiembre, permite apoyar reparaciones de viviendas de familias de bajos y muy bajos ingresos en comunidades rurales y podría beneficiar iniciativas municipales como “Manos que Transforman”.

La visita forma parte de los esfuerzos del Comisionado Residente para trabajar directamente con los municipios y ampliar el acceso de Puerto Rico a programas y recursos federales.

###
title: Comisionado Residente impulsa protección costera para Naguabo en el Congreso

Last week, Congressman Adam Gray (CA-13) and California Democratic Congressional Delegation Chair Zoe Lofgren (CA-18) led the California Democratic Congressional Delegation along with Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff, in sending a letter to U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz urging the agencies to work with California to resolve outstanding concerns and release $867.5 million in deferred federal Medicaid payments.

The effort comes in response to CMS’s decision in July to defer $867.5 million in federal Medicaid payments to California while the state provides additional documentation related to certain Medicaid claims.

In their letter, the Delegation raises concerns that the payment deferral could put additional strain on the state and threaten access to care for vulnerable Californians. For Central Valley families, doctors, hospitals, and care providers, reliable Medicaid funding is essential to making sure patients can get the care they need.

“We should always take fraud, waste, and abuse seriously and make sure taxpayer dollars are being used responsibly. But withholding hundreds of millions of dollars in Medicaid payments without identifying specific fraud puts patients and providers in the middle of a dispute they didn't create,” wrote the Delegation.

“California is working with CMS to provide the information being requested. The federal government should work with the state to resolve these concerns quickly and make sure patients continue to have access to the care they need,” the Delegation continued.

The letter also pushes back on the suggestion that increased spending on California’s in-home care programs is, on its own, evidence of fraud. The Delegation notes that the growth of these programs has been intentional because in-home care can be less costly than institutional care, while California has also implemented additional safeguards to address areas of concern.

"We're grateful to California's congressional delegation for pushing back on this unprecedented deferral. We share their concern that withholding these funds — without identified fraud — puts access to care at risk for millions of Californians. Community health centers care for every patient and strengthen every community, delivering care linked to up to 22% lower annual Medicaid costs per patient and $9.6 billion in savings in 2023. That's the kind of results CMS should be supporting, not jeopardizing,” said Dr. Melissa Marshall, CMO of the California Primary Care Association.

“California physicians support pragmatic solutions that strengthen oversight, protect taxpayer dollars and maintain a stable health care system. But CMS's decision to defer another $867.5 million in Medicaid payments, on top of the previous $1.3 billion deferral, is not responsible oversight – it puts patients at risk. Medicaid policy should be driven by verified facts, not rhetoric, and patients must remain the priority,” said René Bravo, M.D., President of the

California Medical Association.

The letter is signed by the entire California Democratic Congressional Delegation.
title: GRAY, LOFGREN PRESS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TO RELEASE $867 MILLION IN WITHHELD MEDICAID FUNDING

WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congresswoman Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03) announced $249,404 in federal funding for the City of Wyoming, the City of Kentwood, and the City of Grand Rapids and Kent County, through the U.S. Department of Justice's Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) Program. The funding will support public safety equipment, community policing, and emergency response capabilities across West Michigan.

“Keeping our communities safe requires consistent investments in the personnel and tools that protect them,” said Congresswoman Scholten. “From new patrol equipment on our trails to community policing programs and emergency operations upgrades, this funding reflects the kind of practical, on-the-ground investment that makes a real difference here in West Michigan. I am proud to support the local leaders and first responders on the front lines of this work every day.”

Individual awards listed below:

$196,530 – City of Grand Rapids and Kent County

This funding will support the City of Grand Rapids' Neighborhood-Based Public Safety program, which organizes block clubs and neighborhood watch groups, and will fund technology upgrades for Kent County's Emergency Operations Center.

$33,574 – City of Wyoming

This funding will support the purchase and upfit of a street-legal utility task vehicle (UTV) for public safety patrols on the city's nonmotorized trail network and at large community events.

WEST HOLLYWOOD, CA – Today, August 26, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) convened a panel of the region’s top transportation officials alongside U.S. Representatives Maxine Waters (CA-43), Judy Chu (CA-28), Ted Lieu (CA-36), and Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37) to examine what the 2026 FIFA World Cup revealed about Los Angeles County’s readiness to move millions of people during the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games. The panel came just weeks before Congress decides how much federal funding Los Angeles gets for the Games.

The panel brought together the agencies that run public transit across the region:

LA Metro Chief Customer Experience Officer Jennifer Vides, who spoke to what the agency needs to move visitors across dozens of venues over sixteen days, including the buses, operators, and storage capacity a Games-scale operation requires and the capital projects Metro is working to finish before 2028.

Los Angeles Department of Transportation General Manager Laura Rubio-Cornejo, who runs the second largest municipal transportation department in the country and is delivering street and transit improvements before 2028, including an additional zero-emissions bus maintenance facility.

City of Santa Monica Department of Transportation Director Anuj Gupta, who oversees the Big Blue Bus and a department of more than 470 employees in a city that will host no Olympic venues but will be the site of at least a dozen nation houses.

LA Metro Chief of Police and Emergency Management Bill Scott, who led Metro's security coordination during the World Cup and is standing up the agency's new in-house Transit Community Public Safety Department while preparing for the 2027 Super Bowl and 2028 Games.

“The World Cup proved that Los Angeles can deliver, but eight matches at one stadium over five weeks is not the same as sixteen days of events at dozens of venues across the region,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “The agencies responsible for moving those visitors have never had to work at that scale together. So, we brought them into one room to tell Congress what they need to pull this off, and when they need it because the window for that closes in weeks, not years. I am going to keep fighting to bring our tax dollars home, and to make sure what this region builds for 2028 is still serving Angelenos long after the Games leave town.”

“In less than two years, the world will arrive in Los Angeles for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games. This summer's World Cup was a valuable test run as we prepare to move millions of people safely across dozens of sites throughout our region, for weeks at a time,” said Congressmember Judy Chu (CA-28). “Pasadena, home to the Rose Bowl, and Arcadia, home to Santa Anita Park, are proud to host the world in 2028. But we can't do it alone. Our success will depend on making sure that our local communities have a real voice in this planning process, and ensuring that the federal government provides our region with the resources and funding it needs. I'm committed to making sure the San Gabriel Valley receives the transit investment these Games demand. Done right, this isn't just about hosting a successful Games, it's about leaving our communities with stronger transit infrastructure for decades to come."

"The American Decade of Sports is an opportunity for Los Angeles to shine bright on the world stage while leaving our region better than fans found it," said Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove (CA-37). “Hosting successful games and delivering lasting benefits for our community starts with investing in our transportation infrastructure. The 2026 World Cup was the ultimate test run for the 2028 Olympics, and convenings like today help us learn from the past so we can build a safer, more accessible, and better-connected LA long after the Olympic flame is extinguished."

WHAT THE WORLD CUP SHOWED:

More than 212,000 rides were taken on Metro’s enhanced bus service to and from SoFi Stadium at $1.75 each way.

Enhanced service included direct shuttles connecting the stadium to 15 transit hubs across Southern California.

June system ridership was 2 million riders higher than last June, with Metro recording its highest single-day ridership of the month on June 18.

Metro CEO Stephanie Wiggins has said there were zero major security incidents during the tournament.

WHAT THE 2028 GAMES REQUIRE:

Metro has requested approximately $2 billion for its Games mobility plan. Congress approved only $94.3 million earlier this year.

The House Appropriations Committee approved $875 million for the request in its FY27 Transportation, Housing and Urban Development bill. This has not been signed into law and falls short of what Los Angeles will need to make the games safe and secure.

The President’s FY27 budget request did not include funding.

Metro needs approximately 1,700 additional buses against a current fleet of roughly 2,100, and has secured roughly half of that total to date.

The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act expires September 30, 2026.

Metro has publicly stated that without the full request, the complete scope of the Games Enhanced Transit System would not be feasible.

In February 2026, Rep. Kamlager-Dove led 36 members of the California delegation, including Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff, in a letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy urging the Administration to include Metro’s request in the President’s FY27 budget request. The letter warned that FY27 was likely the region’s final opportunity to get the investments in place in time for the Games.

Friedman serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

Friedman was joined today by Rep. Maxine Waters (CA-43), Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28), Rep. Ted Lieu (CA-36), Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), West Hollywood Mayor John Heilman, LA Metro Chief Innovation Officer Seleta Reynolds, Los Angeles Department of Transportation General Manager Laura Rubio-Cornejo, City of Santa Monica Department of Transportation Director Anuj Gupta, and LA Metro Chief of Police and Emergency Management Bill Scott.

Below: Members of Congress and panelists at today’s event answer and asking questions.

###
title: RELEASE: After World Cup, Reps. Friedman, Chu, Lieu, & Kamlager-Dove Convene LA’s Transportation Leaders on Olympic Readiness

Hawaiʻi — Today, U.S. Representative Jill N. Tokuda (HI-02) and Maui County Councilmember Tamara Paltin released the following joint statement opposing the proposed permanent closure of the Lahaina Downtown Post Office.

“To permanently close the Lahaina Downtown Post Office is yet another slap in the face to a community that has already endured far too much. Lahaina has gone without this downtown post office since the August 2023 wildfires.

Now, as families and small businesses rebuild, USPS wants to eliminate another essential public service. The people of Lahaina deserve better.

A 30-minute online meeting held during the workday, with only a few days’ notice, does not constitute meaningful community engagement. It excludes working families, kūpuna, and residents without reliable internet access, and falls far short of the transparency and public participation this decision demands. The people of Lahaina deserve a genuine opportunity to be heard, not a half-hearted process designed to check a box.

And it comes as residents moving back into rebuilt homes are facing another loss: direct home mail delivery. Rebuilt neighborhoods are not new subdivisions. They are restored communities, and residents deserve the same level of service they had before the disaster.

USPS should be working with Lahaina to restore service, not finding new ways to take it away. We are demanding a halt to this closure plan, genuine in-person engagement with the community, home delivery for returning residents, and a serious effort to restore the downtown post office. Lahaina has been through enough. Our community deserves more than a pitiful excuse for engagement. It deserves a Postal Service that shows up, listens, and helps rebuild Lahaina, not one that abandons it.”

###
title: Joint Statement from U.S. Representative Jill N. Tokuda and Councilmember Tamara Paltin on the Lahaina Downtown Post Office

PITTSBURGH, PA – AUGUST 25, 2026 — Today, Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) joined Westmoreland County leaders in Irwin and North Huntingdon to celebrate $1,075,000 in federal Community Project Funding she secured to address abandoned mine drainage from the Biddle Mine and help restore the Turtle Creek watershed.

Congresswoman Lee toured Tinkers Run and Brush Creek, where pollution from the Biddle Mine continues to visibly impact local waterways, including stretches of creek turned orange by mine runoff. She also visited the future site of a treatment facility that will help clean polluted water before it reaches the surrounding watershed.

Following the tour, Congresswoman Lee presented Westmoreland County Commissioners with a ceremonial $1+ million check representing the federal investment she helped bring home for the project.

“When you can stand next to a creek and quite literally see the water turning orange from mine pollution, you don’t need anybody to explain why this investment matters,” said Rep. Lee. “For generations, communities across Western Pennsylvania have lived with the environmental consequences left behind by industries that built enormous wealth off our region, impacting their health, quality of living, and cleanup costs. That’s why I fought to bring home more than $1 million for this project, so we can clean up these waterways, protect the Turtle Creek watershed, and invest in a healthier future for the people who live here.”

“As a Biddle native this area often served as a playground for me and my friends. Our children today and in the future deserve better. This is a really important project for our environment and our community. And I am so grateful for all of the project partners, including Congresswoman Summer Lee for the federal support,” said Westmoreland County Commissioner Ted Kopas.

The project will support efforts to remediate mine drainage associated with the Biddle Mine and reduce pollution entering Tinkers Run, Brush Creek, and the broader Turtle Creek watershed.

Congresswoman Lee was joined by Westmoreland County Commissioners Ted Kopas, Sean Kertes, and Doug Chew, along with local officials and community partners involved in the remediation effort.

The $1,075,000 investment was included in the Fiscal Year 2026 federal funding package as a Community Project Funding request secured by Congresswoman Lee.

Through her Community Project Funding efforts, Rep. Lee has secured direct investments for community-based organizations, including a $1 million CPF award to the Greater Pittsburgh Community Food Bank, $450,000 to the Trade Institute of Pittsburgh, over $1.5 million in federal support for the Tree of Life rebuilding and healing initiatives, $1 million in Community Project Funding for historic renovations at the Carnegie Library of Homestead, more than $1 million in federal funding to combat blight and revitalize housing in North Braddock, and $1 million to help turn vacant office space into affordable homes, create good-paying jobs, and bring new life to downtown Pittsburgh.

These projects are part of more than $24.9 million in Community Project Funding secured during her time in Congress. Rep. Lee’s office has consistently directed federal dollars to historically overlooked communities to ensure equitable access to opportunities and long-term regional growth and stability.
title: Rep. Summer Lee Delivers $1+ Million for Biddle Mine Cleanup and Turtle Creek Watershed Restoration

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) announced his support for two new bills to hold massive data center developers accountable, protect New Mexico families from higher electricity costs, and give communities the information they need to weigh the costs and benefits and decide whether to allow these projects to move forward.

“New Mexico’s water, air, and resources belong to us, not to billionaires from coastal states who see an opportunity to extract profit from our land. I’ve been appalled at the backroom deals, silencing of dissenting voices, shady NDAs and shell companies, and the overall lack of transparency from those who seek to do business in our state,” said Vasquez. “New Mexico should absolutely compete for the jobs and technology of the future, but we are not going to sell out our water, our clean air, or our way of life to do it. If you want to do business here, you need to be transparent, listen to local residents, and most importantly, prove to New Mexicans that projects will serve, not steal from, our communities.”

Vasquez announced that he is championing the following legislation to put new guardrails in place around data center proposals:

The FAIR Data Act (H.R. 9655), which would stop data center projects from driving up energy bills for families and small businesses.

The bill would force large corporate electricity users to pay their own way, protecting residential customers and small businesses from being forced to foot the bill for costs related to massive data centers, including increased rates and electric grid upgrades needed to serve massive data centers.

The Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act (H.R. 9825), which requires data center developers to transparently disclose their energy and water usage.

The bill would force developers to make information regarding data center energy and water consumption available to state and local governments that have or are considering new data center projects in their communities and force noncompliant data centers to pay fines up to $20,000 per day.

A Victory in Socorro: Vasquez has already demonstrated his willingness to stand up to data center developers when communities are not being heard and respected. Earlier this year, after residents on both sides of the aisle in Socorro County raised serious concerns about a proposal to build one of the largest data centers in the world in their backyard, Vasquez was the only statewide or federal official to stand with residents and publicly call for an end to the proposal. In response to Vasquez’s public leadership, the foreign company behind the proposal pulled out, and Socorro County commissioners unanimously approved a one-year moratorium to give the community time to develop appropriate safeguards.

Mostly recently, Vasquez condemned the use of force to stifle local opposition at a community meeting in Doña Ana County on Project Jupiter.

Vasquez’s support of the legislation announced today builds on his ongoing work to hold data center developers accountable to local communities, which includes:

Leading the Energy Bills Relief Act, which includes a provision directing states to enact policies to protect consumers from utility rate increases stemming from data center energy demands.

Championing bill language during the FY27 appropriations process that requested the inclusion of report language directing the Department of Energy to develop a National Strategic Data Center Plan to guide the responsible growth of data center infrastructure across the United States.
