FAIRFIELD, CA – Congressman John Garamendi (CA-08) joined Solano Supervisor Wanda Williams and Senior Pastor Dr. Sam Morris at a community forum held at the BayNorth Church of Christ in Fairfield, where he explained how his recently passed HOME Act, a key provision of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, the most substantial pieces of housing legislation in years, will help build affordable housing in Solano County.

“California has faced a severe affordable housing shortage for far too long. Today, a minimum-wage worker in California must work nearly 90 hours a week just to afford a modest one-bedroom apartment at fair market rent. That is unacceptable,” said Rep. Garamendi.

“This year, Congress passed one of the most substantial affordable housing bills in years, including a bill I have spent years working on called the HOME Act. The HOME Act modernizes HUD’s premier affordable housing grant program and will give cities and counties the tools they need to build more affordable housing.

“Now that this bill is the law of the land, we are already speeding down the path to making California a more affordable place to live. In fact, just last month, I was joined by local leaders in highlighting the building of new affordable housing in my district. California families have been bearing the weight of unaffordable housing for too long. Now, it’s time to build.”

Background

Garamendi’s legislation puts federal dollars directly toward building new affordable homes. For the first time, communities can use Community Development Block Grant funding to construct new affordable housing, giving cities and counties another major federal funding source to increase housing supply. The law also creates a $200 million-a-year Housing Innovation Fund to reward communities that increase their housing supply through reforms like streamlined permitting, density bonuses, and zoning changes.

The legislation makes it cheaper and faster to build common housing types. It does this by streamlining environmental reviews for federally supported housing, delegating more reviews to state and local governments, and removing duplicative requirements for smaller and infill projects, reducing delays and financing costs.

The HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) is the largest federal affordable housing block grant and HUD’s flagship affordable housing production program. Garamendi’s HOME Act allows communities to use HOME funds for water and sewer lines, sidewalks, roads, and utility connections directly tied to HOME- or Low-Income Housing Tax Credit projects—helping remove costs that can keep otherwise viable affordable housing from getting built.

Since 1992, the HOME program in California has:

Invested $5.27 billion in housing across the state;

Built or preserved 121,727 homes;

Provided rental assistance to 43,840 families;

Supported 277,318 jobs; and

Generated $19.2 billion in local income.

With the HOME Act’s additional spending authority and flexibility, the impacts of the HOME program in California will grow even faster. Garamendi originally introduced the HOME Investment Partnership Reauthorization Act in 2020 and has continued to champion affordable housing legislation in Congress.

###
title: Garamendi Touts His Recently Passed Housing Affordability Legislation at Solano Church Community Forum

Today Representatives Suzan DelBene (WA-01) and Greg Steube (FL-17) introduced the Safeguarding America’s Nonprofits Act, legislation that would clarify that a nonprofit’s federal tax-exempt status does not constitute federal financial assistance.

The bill amends Section 501 of the Internal Revenue Code to state that a federal income tax exemption does not count as federal financial assistance for organizations described under sections 501(c), 501(d), or 401(a).

There are roughly 2 million nonprofit organizations in the United States. Many operate without any direct government assistance, thereby avoiding the compliance burdens that federal subsidies often impose. When the tax code was written, Congress intended for a clear distinction between nonprofits that do and do not accept government assistance. This bill affirms Congress’ intent and limits legal uncertainty.

“Nonprofits across the country rely on clear, consistent federal rules to continue serving their communities effectively. In recent years, conflicting court decisions have created uncertainty by suggesting that nonprofits could be subject to regulations that Congress never intended for them. This bipartisan legislation would clarify that an organization’s tax-exempt status is not federal financial assistance. It would protect charities, philanthropies, community‑based organizations, and religious institutions from unnecessary regulations so they can stay focused on delivering critical services,” said DelBene.

“Nonprofits across the country depend on their tax-exempt status to carry out their work. That status should never be treated as a form of government assistance,” said Steube. “The Safeguarding America’s Nonprofits Act puts a clear, permanent rule in statute so nonprofits do not have to worry about their tax exemption being reinterpreted as a government handout.”

“Nonprofit organizations are the heart of our communities. They play an essential role in supporting families and hardworking Americans, advancing research, educating students, and providing countless other public benefits, often stepping in where government and business can’t or shouldn’t. Their strength lies in their independence. The Safeguarding America’s Nonprofits Act protects tax-exempt organizations independent from the federal government from unnecessary and burdensome risks of litigation or bureaucratic overreach. We appreciate Congressman Greg Steube (R-FL) and Congresswoman DelBene for their bipartisan leadership so nonprofits can continue to focus on their missions,” said Community Impact Coalition Co-Chairs: Tommy Goodwin and Mary Wheatley.

“Associations are among the most trusted institutions in American life,” said Michelle Mason, FASAE, CAE, President and CEO, American Society of Association Executives. “They set the standards that keep products safe and professions credible, train and credential the workforce, and convene the people who solve problems no single company or agency can solve alone. That work depends on their independence. The Safeguarding America’s Nonprofits Act makes clear what has always been true: tax exemption is not federal financial assistance, and it should never become a lever for government control over organizations that accept no federal dollars. ASAE thanks Congressman Steube and Congresswoman DelBene for introducing this important legislation and urges members of Congress to support it.”

“Representing family forestry businesses across Rural America, the Forest Landowners Association understands firsthand the important role nonprofit organizations play in strengthening communities and advancing the interests of the people and industries they serve,” said Scott Jones, CEO, Forest Landowners Association. “Tax-exempt status is not a government grant or subsidy, and it should not be treated as federal financial assistance. The Safeguarding America’s Nonprofits Act provides important clarity and protects organizations like FLA from unnecessary regulatory burdens that could hinder our ability to carry out our missions. FLA is proud to support this bipartisan legislation.”

“Community Associations Institute (CAI) is proud to support the Safeguarding America’s Nonprofits Act,” said Dawn M. Bauman, CAE, CEO of CAI. “Nonprofit organizations like CAI play an essential role in providing important resources to support the integrity and strength of America’s communities. This legislation helps ensure CAI can continue to prioritize our members and provide the education, advocacy, and resources they need to support thriving community associations. We thank Congressman Steube and Senator Lankford for their leadership on this important legislation.”

The legislation is supported by a broad coalition of nonprofit organizations, including the Community Impact Coalition, Career Education Colleges and Universities, American Society of Association Executives, National Scleroderma Foundation, Women in Trucking, Florida Association of Free and Charitable Clinics, Community Associations Institute, The Handcrafted Soap & Cosmetic Guild, Inc., Household and Commercial Products Association, American Rental Association, American Council of Academic Physical Therapy, Bostrom, National Association for Regulatory Administration, Association Management Services, Inc., Association CEO, American Society for Nondestructive Testing, American Society for Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics, and the National Emergency Number Association.
title: DelBene Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Protect Nonprofits’ Tax-Exempt Status

Washington, D.C. — Today, Representatives Jake Auchincloss (D-MA) and Dan Newhouse (R-WA), alongside House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI) and Ranking Member Ro Khanna (D-CA), reintroduced the CCP Fentanyl Sanctions Act to hold the Chinese Community Party responsible for its role in the U.S. fentanyl crisis.

After its establishment in 2024, the House Select Committee on China’s Fentanyl Policy Working Group uncovered for the first time how the CCP directly subsidizes fentanyl precursors and analogues entering North America.

The CCP Fentanyl Sanctions Act strengthens sanctions on China-based and CCP-backed entities engaged in drug trafficking, by targeting the Chinese chemical manufacturers and online vendors that are profiting by poisoning the American people.

As Co-Chairman of the Policy Working Group (PWG) last Congress, Auchincloss and his colleagues focused on combating the CCP’s role in the fentanyl epidemic with legislation to curtail the threat via sanctions, trade and customs enforcement, and regulatory and enforcement measures.

The CCP Fentanyl Sanctions Act will address fentanyl exports from China by:

Targeting the “Achilles’ heel” of fentanyl and related synthetic narcotics producers—their exposure to the U.S. banking system courtesy of their licit activity;

Codifying important new authorities to address this threat while working to target those responsible for the epidemic;

Codifying and building on Executive Order 14059, which established critical new sanctions authorities against actors involved in fentanyl trafficking;

Expanding existing sanctions authorities to target PRC vessels or ports that knowingly or recklessly facilitate shipment/transportation of illicit synthetic narcotics, as well as PRC online marketplaces and other entities that knowingly or recklessly facilitate sale of illicit synthetic narcotics;

Providing authority to restrict foreign financial institution correspondent accounts and payable-through accounts if the President determines the account has knowingly facilitated transactions on behalf of individuals engaging in synthetic narcotics trafficking.

“Thousands of families in Massachusetts have been scarred by fentanyl,” said Rep. Auchincloss. “Chinese chemical manufacturers that are exporting this addictive poison to American shores should bear the full force of U.S. sanctions and anti-money-laundering measures.”

“The Chinese Communist Party must be held accountable for helping manufacture the fentanyl crisis,” said Rep. Newhouse. “For too long, they have subsidized and exported illicit narcotics, and Congress must take aggressive action to counter this epidemic that’s ruining American lives and families. This bipartisan legislation is a strong step in the right direction, as it targets CCP-backed entities, like Chinese chemical companies, who continue wreaking havoc on our communities.”

“The Chinese Communist Party has long had a role in facilitating the fentanyl crisis that has killed hundreds of thousands of Americans,” said Chairman Moolenaar. “The Select Committee’s groundbreaking report in 2024 showed how the CCP subsidized the production of fentanyl precursors sold to the Mexican cartels. The bipartisan legislation we are introducing today targets the entities and individuals who participated in this deadly and illicit practice. It is a crucial step toward holding them accountable for the pain they have caused American families.”

“Fentanyl has devastated communities across America,” said Ranking Member Khanna. “I’m proud to join Rep. Auchincloss’s bipartisan effort to hold the networks responsible accountable. We must stop the flow of fentanyl and illicit precursors into our country and protect American families.”
title: Reps. Auchincloss, Newhouse, Moolenaar, and Khanna Reintroduce Bipartisan Legislation Targeting China’s Role in U.S. Fentanyl Crisis

NEW YORK, NY — Today, U.S. Representative Paul Tonko (D-NY-20), Senate Democratic Leader Charles Schumer (D-NY), and U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), following continued concern from local Capital Region veterans, called on Secretary of Veterans Affairs Doug Collins to provide more information about the planned closure of the Schenectady Veterans Affairs (VA) Community Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) at the end of the month. When the closure was announced in March 2026, the lawmakers immediately called on the VA to halt the closure and provide immediate answers to ensure that healthcare for the over 1,500 Capital Region veterans who rely on this clinic would not be disrupted. Now, five months following their original letter and with the closure looming, few questions have been answered.

In the letter, the members addressed the lack of communication from the VA and the confusion that Capital Region veterans are experiencing with little to no guidance as to the future of their care. They wrote, “Since the closure was announced this past spring, vanishingly little detail or communication has been made available to veterans or the broader public in the Capital Region. The lack of communication has raised concerns about the burden this disruption will place on veterans with ongoing care. Five months since the announcement of the closure, we continue to hear from veterans and non-profit organizations working to cover gaps in care and transportation for veterans, who find themselves less informed, more confused, and in greater precarity.”

The members noted that this would be the second CBOC closure in the Capital Region in five years, forcing veterans to seek out alternative care in places that may be even farther from their homes. They continued, “The communities we represent have expressed significant doubt regarding the VA’s claim that transportation time to the new clinics will be shorter for 80% of veterans. Many older veterans in the area are reliant on public transportation, ride-share services, and friends, family, and their communities for transportation to VA appointments. We are especially concerned that the decision to shift care away from the Schenectady CBOC does not account for the additional bus routes, ride-share costs, and time commitments from friends and families to ensure that veterans have regular access to care at a different facility.”

In a series of questions, the members demanded immediate transparency and requested that the VA release concrete data and outreach plans regarding the facility's closure by August 27th. The inquiry pushes the VA to detail its justification for the closure and the projected impact on veterans in the region, as well as the VA’s plans for ensuring that patients maintain their access to high-quality care.

The lawmakers stressed that not a single local veteran or advocacy group had reached out to their offices to voice support for the clinic’s closure. They concluded, “The lack of clear communication and proper planning has caused significant anxiety for veterans in the Schenectady region who place their trust in the VA to manage their care. We urge the VA to listen to the community that would be most immediately affected by this plan, halt the closure of this clinic until all the questions posed in this letter can be properly addressed, and work with us to rebuild trust among veterans in the Capital Region.”
title: Tonko, Schumer, Gillibrand Raise Alarm Amid Impending Closure of Schenectady Veterans Affairs Community Based Outpatient Clinic

CAGUAS, Puerto Rico — En medio de la controversia por el contrato de energía temporera de Power Expectations, el Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, lideró un esfuerzo bipartidista para que el Departamento de Energía de Estados Unidos (DOE) actúe de inmediato ante el riesgo de más apagones.

En una carta dirigida al secretario de Energía, el Comisionado Residente y los congresistas presentaron cuatro medidas que la DOE debe tomar inmediatamente para atender el problema de los apagones.

Que el DOE reúna de inmediato a la Autoridad de Energía Eléctrica (AEE), LUMA Energy, Genera PR, el Negociado de Energía de Puerto Rico y al liderato energético del Gobierno de Puerto Rico para coordinar una respuesta conjunta.

Que dirijan la implantación de un plan operacional de confiabilidad para los próximos 90 días.

Que usen la autoridad que les brinda la orden de emergencia para proveer más recursos de generación.

Que envíen a sus expertos técnicos para determinar qué plantas pueden regresar a servicio en 7, 14 y 30 días y reducir el riesgo de nuevos apagones.

“Queremos acabar con los apagones, y el gobierno federal tiene recursos que no está maximizando. Este es un reclamo bipartidista para atender la crisis en Puerto Rico, que se agravó con la cancelación del contrato de generación temporera”, expresó el Comisionado Residente.

Al esfuerzo se unieron, entre otros, Rob Menendez, miembro del Comité de Energía y Comercio; Sean Casten, vicepresidente de la Coalición de Energía Sostenible y Medio Ambiente de la Cámara (SEEC); y el delegado republicano de Guam, James Moylan.

La gestión cobra mayor urgencia tras la cancelación de un contrato de $5,900 millones que buscaba añadir generación al sistema. Sin esa capacidad adicional, Puerto Rico queda con menos margen para responder a fallas y mayor riesgo de apagones que pueden significar comida perdida, negocios detenidos y más gastos en combustible y generadores.

El Comisionado Residente ha estado fiscalizando las decisiones sobre generación temporera desde el año pasado. En junio de 2025, junto a un colega republicano, reclamó explicaciones sobre alternativas de generación que habían sido descartadas y exigió respuestas a funcionarios federales y de Puerto Rico. Ahora, tras la cancelación del contrato de $5,900 millones, el Comisionado Residente continuará esa fiscalización desde el Congreso para esclarecer qué ocurrió, quién tenía conocimiento de las irregularidades y por qué no se actuó antes.

Puerto Rico Congressman Leads Bipartisan Push for Immediate Federal Action on Blackouts

The bipartisan effort comes amid generation-related outages and the cancellation of the temporary power generation contract.

CAGUAS, Puerto Rico — Amid the controversy surrounding the Power Expectations temporary power generation contract, Puerto Rico Congressman Pablo José Hernández led a bipartisan effort urging the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to take immediate action to address the risk of further blackouts.

In a letter to U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright, Congressman Hernández and his colleagues outlined four steps DOE should take immediately to address Puerto Rico’s ongoing power outages:

Immediately convene the Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority (PREPA), LUMA Energy, Genera PR, the Puerto Rico Energy Bureau, and the Puerto Rico government’s energy leadership to coordinate a unified response.

Direct the implementation of a 90-day operational reliability plan.

Use the authority provided under the federal emergency order to make additional generation resources available.

Deploy DOE technical experts to determine which generating units can be returned to service within 7, 14, and 30 days to reduce the risk of additional blackouts.

“We want to put an end to the blackouts, and the federal government has resources that are not being fully utilized. This is a bipartisan effort to address Puerto Rico’s energy crisis, which has been made worse by the cancellation of the temporary generation contract,” said Congressman Hernández.

This bipartisan effort drew support from lawmakers including Rep. Rob Menendez, a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee; Rep. Sean Casten, vice chair of the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition (SEEC); and Republican Guam Delegate James Moylan.

The effort has taken on greater urgency following the cancellation of a $5.9 billion contract intended to add generation capacity to Puerto Rico’s power grid. Without that additional capacity, Puerto Rico has less ability to withstand generation failures and faces a greater risk of blackouts that can mean spoiled food, disrupted businesses, and additional costs for fuel and generators.

Congressman Hernández has been conducting oversight surrounding this matter since last year. In June 2025, alongside a Republican colleague, he demanded explanations regarding generation alternatives that had been rejected and sought answers from federal and Puerto Rico officials. Now, following the cancellation of the $5.9 billion contract, Congressman Hernández will continue that congressional oversight to determine what happened, who was aware of the irregularities, and why action was not taken sooner.

ELMHURST, Illinois — Today, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi joined the DuPage Water Commission (DWC) to announce $1 million in federal Community Project Funding he secured to advance Stage 1 of the Lake Michigan Regional Water Supply Initiative, a major regional infrastructure project that will provide safe, reliable drinking water while addressing contaminants including lead, PFAS, and microplastics.

The approximately $3 billion, 15-year initiative will create a modern regional water system expected to benefit up to 2 million residents across Northeastern Illinois. The project will include a new Lake Michigan raw-water intake, regional drinking-water treatment plant, and tunnels, pipelines, and pumping stations across Cook and DuPage counties. The new treatment plant will be specifically designed to treat microplastics, PFAS, and other emerging contaminants, while the broader project will replace aging infrastructure and help reduce risks associated with lead entering drinking water.

The $1 million Congressman Krishnamoorthi secured will support geotechnical work to provide a foundational engineering report for the installation of finished-water tunnels that will help deliver Lake Michigan drinking water to communities across the region.

“Every family deserves to know that when they turn on the faucet, the water coming out is safe to drink,” said Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi. “I’m proud to have secured $1 million in federal funding for this project, which will provide safe Lake Michigan drinking water to communities across our region while protecting Illinoisans from threats like microplastics and PFAS. As I continue leading the fight in Congress to combat microplastics in our drinking water, I’ll keep supporting investments here at home that will build the modern water infrastructure our families need for generations to come.”

Last month, Congressman Krishnamoorthi led a bicameral letter with Representative Janelle Bynum and Senators Jeff Merkley and Cory Booker, joined by 53 additional lawmakers, urging the Environmental Protection Agency to begin nationwide monitoring of microplastics in drinking water. The lawmakers called on EPA to add microplastics to its Sixth Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule to measure Americans’ exposure, inform future health-protective standards under the Safe Drinking Water Act, and respond to emerging research linking microplastics to serious adverse health effects.

“This federal funding is an important step forward for the Lake Michigan Regional Water Supply Initiative and a testament to the power of regional collaboration,” said James F. Zay, Chairman of the DuPage Water Commission. “We are grateful to Congressman Krishnamoorthi for his support of this transformative project. By working together, we are making a long-term investment in the region’s future growth, resiliency, and quality of life.”

“A multi-billion-dollar investment of this scale is about building critical water infrastructure—and sustaining thousands of good-paying jobs, supporting skilled trades, and creating a stable pipeline of work for working families across Northeast Illinois for the next 15 years,” said James M. Sweeney, President-Business Manager of International Union of Operating Engineers Local 150. “Long-term infrastructure investment gives labor the certainty to train, hire, and build the workforce needed to deliver projects that will serve our communities for generations.”

The project is expected to provide a more reliable regional water supply while supporting future growth and business investment and creating significant union employment during its approximately 15-year design and construction period.

Congressman Krishnamoorthi and the DuPage Water Commission were joined at the event by state and regional elected officials, labor representatives, professional service associations, and representatives of environmental and state agencies.
title: Krishnamoorthi Delivers $1 Million for Major Lake Michigan Water Infrastructure Project to Provide Clean Drinking Water and Combat Microplastics

ALBUQUERQUE — Congresswoman Melanie Stansbury (NM-01) is requesting answers from New Mexico state officials regarding the water use, water rights, permitting, quality, and compact compliance associated with Project Jupiter, a 1,400-acre artificial intelligence data center campus under construction near Santa Teresa in Doña Ana County, New Mexico. Stansbury’s calls for answers come as the New Mexico Supreme Court issued two emergency orders Sunday night regarding the project’s emergency well permit, used for construction of the project, and a proposed air quality permit.

Stansbury is directing the public request for information by close of business this Friday, August 28, as the Court has ordered the parties to respond to its orders by Wednesday of next week. Stansbury’s letter, addressed to the New Mexico Attorney General, the State Engineer, the State Environment Secretary, and the Chair and Director of the New Mexico Interstate Stream Commission, requests information about the project’s proposed water use, analysis of potential impacts, and compliance requirements under the Rio Grande Compact.

The request comes as New Mexico confronts unprecedented water challenges and works to meet its obligations under a court-supervised settlement following litigation with Texas over the Rio Grande Compact. Under the settlement, New Mexico must reduce groundwater pumping in the Lower Rio Grande Basin by 18,200 acre-feet annually by 2036.

Project Jupiter is expected to become a significant industrial water user in the basin, with estimates putting its water use at over a million gallons a day. Stansbury is asking the Office of the State Engineer (OSE) and others to provide a clear public accounting of how the project’s water needs will be met and what water rights and permits support those needs.

"In New Mexico we know water is life and our communities are facing a historic water crisis,” Rep. Stansbury said. "Every new major water use deserves a transparent accounting of where its water is coming from and how that use fits within our state’s obligations to our tribes and Pueblos, acequias, farmers and ranchers, the communities who already depend on these waters, and our surrounding neighbors. New Mexicans demand and deserve to know how their water is being used, how those rights may be obtained or transferred, and what permits the State has approved. This is about transparency, accountability, and protecting New Mexico’s water future."

In her letter to the OSE, Stansbury requests information on four key areas:

Project Jupiter’s water use: Estimated and reported daily and annual water consumption during construction and future operations, including the intended end uses of the water, such as cooling, power generation, and domestic use, and potential consumptive use and return flows.

Project Jupiter’s water rights: The water rights currently associated with the project, their origin—including whether they derive from prior agricultural use—and the legal process through which any transfer or change of use was reviewed and approved. The request also asks whether any new groundwater appropriations have been sought or granted.

Project Jupiter’s permits and applications: A complete list of applications and permits filed with or issued by OSE, including filing dates, current status, and any protests or objections submitted.

Analyses Conducted on Project Jupiter’s Water Impacts: Any analysis performed of the project’s proposed water use or discharge on state water supplies, water quality, other users, and compliance with in-state, interstate, and international laws, agreements, and management requirements on the Rio Grande.

“The scale of Project Jupiter makes this an important test case for how New Mexico evaluates major industrial water users in a water-scarce future,” Stansbury said. “The public should have a clear accounting of what water resources are being proposed for this project, the process by which those decisions are being made, and must have a say on how water in New Mexico is used.”

This request follows two unanimous orders from the New Mexico Supreme Court on August 23rd, 2026, pausing Project Jupiter proceedings. One order temporarily halts a scheduled September 14th air quality permit hearing at the New Mexico Environment Department on Project Jupiter’s proposed natural gas fuel cell system. The second order directs the Office of the State Engineer to pause an emergency permit for a specific well being used for the data center’s construction. These orders follow concerns from environmental groups alleging a lack of due process in the state's permitting processes. The New Mexico Supreme Court gave the parties involved until September 2, 2026, to respond to their orders.

Find a recording of the press call on this topic here.

Find a copy of the letter here or read the full letter below:

Dear Attorney General Torrez, State Engineer Anderson, Secretary Kenney, Chair Sanchez, and Director Riseley-White:

I am writing to urgently request information from applicable state agencies regarding the water usage, water rights, water permitting, and potential impacts to water quality and interstate river compact compliance associated with Project Jupiter, a 1,400-acre artificial intelligence data center campus under construction near Santa Teresa in Doña Ana County, New Mexico. While the New Mexico Supreme Court has stayed the administrative proceeding on the project’s air quality permit and the use of its emergency water-well authorization this week, we remain deeply concerned about the proposed water usage by this facility. Specifically, we are concerned about whether it has obtained the proper water rights and/or permits to operate in compliance with New Mexico water law and the state's obligations under the Rio Grande Compact and interstate agreements.

This request comes at a critical moment for New Mexico’s water future. As you know, the state is currently experiencing one of its worst water years on record: water curtailments have hit users and farmers statewide following record-low snowpack, Elephant Butte Reservoir has fallen to its lowest storage level since 1971, and the Rio Grande has now run dry through the middle reach for more than three months—one of the longest such stretches on record. While we are hopeful that weather conditions will improve this year to provide increased precipitation, we understand that these conditions represent a longer-term trend and shift in our water supplies due to climate change—which raise significant concerns about the impacts of this project.

With increasing constraints on our water supply, New Mexico is already experiencing significant pressures to restrict and reduce existing uses. Following litigation with Texas over the Rio Grande Compact, New Mexico is now under a binding, court-supervised settlement requiring a reduction in groundwater pumping of 18,200 acre-feet annually in the Lower Rio Grande Basin by 2036—the very basin from which Project Jupiter draws its water. Given New Mexico’s record-breaking drought and ongoing water availability crisis, your agencies’ decisions governing the allocation, permitting, and oversight of our limited water resources deserve the utmost public accountability and transparency. This is especially true when the State is legally obligated to bring into balance a large new industrial water user entering the basin—one that is currently reported to require over a million gallons of water a day.

The questions Project Jupiter has raised matter to and affect New Mexicans statewide. Given the size of this project and the precedent it may set for how similar large-scale industrial water developments will be reviewed in the future, the public deserves a clear and complete record of the water resources at stake and how water rights and permitting determinations will be made.

This request follows significant public concern raised regarding the project’s water requirements at several local proceedings. At the Doña Ana County Board of Commissioners meeting in September 2025, commissioners voted to approve $165 billion in industrial revenue bonds for Project Jupiter. That meeting drew several hundred residents, many of whom requested that the vote be delayed, to allow more time for questions about water and other impacts to be answered. Subsequently, on October 29, 2025, the New Mexico Legislature’s Water and Natural Resources Committee met in Artesia and received a briefing on Project Jupiter, during which committee members raised concerns regarding water use and the availability of information about the project to the public.[4] Similar concerns were also raised in recent public listening sessions held by New Mexico lawmakers over the last several weeks and have been raised by federal state, tribal, and local leaders across New Mexico.

At this time, a full accounting of Project Jupiter’s proposed water usage, permits and water rights has not been made publicly available nor has any analysis of its potential impacts on New Mexico’s water supply, water quality, and compliance with interstate compacts, agreements, and court orders been made public. To shed light on these issues we are respectfully requesting that each of your agencies provide the following information as it pertains to your agency, office, or commission and any relevant information your office may have on the matter:

Project Jupiter’s estimated and reported water usage, in daily and annual volumes, for both the construction phase and ongoing/future operations, including the intended end uses of that water (e.g., cooling, power generation), potential consumptive use, and potential return flows.

Any proposed or confirmed water rights or permits currently associated with Project Jupiter, including their origin (e.g., prior agricultural use) and the legal and/or administrative processes by which any transfer or change of use was reviewed and approved—and whether any new groundwater appropriations have been sought or granted for the project, including quantities, places of use, and relevant dates of administrative action.

A list of all permits and applications filed with or issued by OSE for Project Jupiter, including dates and status of each and any protests or objections filed against them.

Any analysis performed of the project’s proposed water use or discharge on state water supplies, water quality, other users, and compliance with in-state, interstate and international laws, agreements, and management requirements on the Rio Grande.

Given the level of public concern regarding this project and its potential water impacts, and considering imminent court decisions regarding project completion, we request your responses in writing to my office no later than close of business Friday, August 28. We also request that your office make all non-privileged information available to the public.

Thank you for your attention to this request.

title: Rep. Stansbury Demands Answers on Project Jupiter’s Water Use as New Mexico Supreme Court Issues Emergency Orders

Hartford, CT - Today, members of the Connecticut Congressional delegation joined Governor Ned Lamont and Connecticut Education Commissioner Charlene M. Russell-Tucker to announce that the Connecticut State Department of Education (CSDE) has been awarded a five-year, $10 million competitive grant to expand targeted reading intervention, with integrated positive behavioral supports, for kindergarten through grade 3 students experiencing significant reading difficulties.

The Education Innovation and Research grant, awarded by the U.S. Department of Education, will support a statewide initiative led by the CSDE’s Center for Literacy Research and Reading Success in continued partnership with the University of Connecticut’s Neag School of Education, HILL for Literacy, Fordham University, and Connecticut school districts.

The initiative will expand access to small-group reading intervention across a statewide network of 75 elementary schools, along with instructional materials, professional learning, ongoing coaching, and tools to monitor student progress and guide instruction. It will also examine the impact of incorporating evidence-aligned positive behavioral interventions and supports into reading instruction to increase student engagement and maximize instructional time.

“Hundreds of thousands of kids in Connecticut rely on federal support from the Department of Education to help them succeed in the classroom, and this announcement is a significant investment in their futures,” said Congressman John B. Larson (CT-01). “As we face an administration intent on dismantling public education in Washington, the Connecticut delegation will continue to work together to defend students and teachers from these attacks, and secure new investments in our schools. I am thrilled to join my colleagues and Governor Lamont to announce this $10 million grant we secured to support educators with the tools they need to improve reading skills and student success.”

“Strong reading skills are critical to a student’s success in school and throughout their lives,” said Governor Lamont. “This investment will provide additional support to young students who are struggling to read and give our educators more tools to meet their needs. We want every child in Connecticut to have the opportunity to become a strong reader and develop a lifelong love of learning.”

“This critical $10 million grant will help more Connecticut children develop a lifelong love of reading,” said Senator Richard Blumenthal. “Reading is not only an academic skill, but helps kids develop empathy, build strong relationships, and expand their imaginations. As literacy rates and reading for pleasure decline across the nation, I am proud to see Governor Lamont and Commissioner Russell-Tucker commit to developing strong readers with this transformative program.”

“This $10 million federal investment will make a drastic difference in the lives of young people, ensuring that they have the science-backed tools needed to read proficiently,” said Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro (CT-03). “Our local schools and teachers are strengthened by federal resources and collaboration. That is why I have been a proud champion for the Education Innovation and Research program, protecting funding in my role as the top Democrat of the House Appropriations Committee, and I will continue to fight for the resources and research necessary for our students to succeed.”

“Literacy is essential for success in life,” said Congresswoman Jahana Hayes (CT-05). “I am pleased to have helped secure funds which will build on the critical steps our state is taking to foster a love of reading, create lifelong learners, and address achievement gaps.”

Since 2021, Connecticut has advanced a comprehensive literacy strategy grounded in the Right to Read legislation, investing more than $24 million in K-3 literacy assessments and instructional materials for schools and $15 million in professional learning for educators and leaders statewide, including the Science of Reading Masterclass. More recently, the state invested $2 million in a new literacy coaching program to provide job-embedded support in identified schools. The new grant complements these efforts by expanding the state’s literacy coaching work and providing intensive, small-group reading intervention for K-3 students who need additional support.

“We are pleased to have secured this competitive grant, which builds upon the significant investments Connecticut has made to strengthen literacy instruction and support our educators,” said Commissioner Russell-Tucker. “This funding will allow us to reach more students and educators with the targeted supports and resources needed to advance early literacy. As this work grows over the next five years, these efforts will position us to continue improving literacy instruction and outcomes for students across our state.”

“We are excited to continue our partnership with the Connecticut State Department of Education’s Center for Literacy Research and Reading Success to strengthen reading outcomes for students in Connecticut,” Michael Coyne and Brandi Simonsen, professors at UConn’s Neag School of Education, said. “This grant will help schools enhance targeted reading interventions and integrated positive behavioral supports. It builds on more than a decade of collaboration among CSDE, UConn, districts, schools, and partners through the Connecticut Literacy Model, while also aligning with Connecticut’s Multi-Tiered System of Support framework.”

Over the five-year grant period, the CSDE and its partners will begin this work as a pilot with a limited number of schools in the first year, with additional schools phased in over the course of the grant.
title: Connecticut Congressional Delegation, Governor Lamont and Education Commissioner Russell-Tucker Announce $10 Million Grant Award to Strengthen Early Literacy Supports

Denver — Today, U.S. Representative Brittany Pettersen joined Senator Michael Bennet and Representative Jeff Hurd and the entire Colorado Congressional delegation – Senator John Hickenlooper and U.S. Representatives Diana DeGette, Joe Neguse, Jason Crow, Lauren Boebert, Jeff Crank, and Gabe Evans – in a letter to President Trump expressing strong support for Governor Jared Polis’ request for a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration for Pueblo, Custer, and Ouray Counties in Colorado. This request comes in response to more than $18 million in Federal Emergency Management Agency validated damages from Colorado’s Aspen Acres and Gold Mountain fires.

In June, Colorado experienced two large, destructive fires within 48 hours, the Aspen Acres Fire and Gold Mountain Fire, due to prime wildfire conditions including high winds, extreme heat, and prolonged drought. These fires burned over 140,000 acres collectively across Pueblo, Custer, and Ouray Counties and destroyed hundreds of homes and structures and energy and water infrastructure. The burn scars left by these fires also contributed to significant post-fire flooding and debris flows that led to one fatality in Beulah, Colorado.

Summer is peak tourism season for Colorado, and the fires and subsequent flooding caused major disruptions to transportation, lodging, recreation, hospitality, outfitter, and guide businesses. They also damaged the operations of agricultural producers who lost livestock, fencing, and grazing lands. Several rural communities were also affected by road closures, which made accessing work, school, healthcare, or essential services extremely difficult. State and federal emergency response officials state that they expect disruptions to continue through the remainder of the summer season.

“Successful recovery is essential to restoring the counties’ economies, which depend on clean drinking water, tourism, agriculture, outdoor recreation, and hunting and fishing. Without additional support, residents could face potentially insurmountable barriers to rebuilding homes and businesses, increased drinking water and electric utility costs, and the loss of important habitat and grazing lands. In addition, these communities face ongoing hazards from the post-fire burn scars, including debris, burned trees, and threats to water quality and drinking water infrastructure,” wrote the lawmakers.

“[...] a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration unlocks federal assistance programs, including Hazard Mitigation Assistance Grants, that are indispensable to recovery, mitigation, and long-term resilience. These communities urgently need federal relief to rebuild. We thank you in advance for your expedited review and approval of the Governor’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration,” concluded the lawmakers.

The text of the letter is available HERE and below.

Dear Mr. President:

We strongly support Governor Jared Polis’ request on [TK August 24, 2026] for a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration with Public and Individual Assistance for Custer and Pueblo Counties, Colorado, in response to the Aspen Acres Fire and Public Assistance for Ouray County in response to the Gold Mountain Fire. Both fires burned during June, July, and August 2026. As part of this request, Governor Polis has also requested the Hazard Mitigation Assistance Grant Program for the affected counties.

In June 2026, extreme heat, prolonged drought, and high winds up to 100 miles per hour contributed to two mega fires in Colorado within 48 hours. The Gold Mountain Fire burned approximately 40,000 acres in Ouray County, Colorado, and the Aspen Acres Fire burned over 102,000 acres across Custer County and Pueblo County, Colorado. Together, these fires destroyed drinking water and electric utility infrastructure, and over 800 structures and 324 homes. The burn scars from both fires contributed to significant post-fire flooding and debris flows that destroyed additional homes, buildings, and electric, water, and transportation infrastructure. On August 16, a significant rain event resulted in one fatality in Beulah, Colorado.

Both fires occurred immediately before the Fourth of July during the summer’s peak tourism season, disrupting lodging, recreation, hospitality, outfitter, and guide businesses. Repeated fire, flood, and debris flow closures have limited visitation and disrupted tourism along the U.S. 550 corridor in Ouray and San Juan Counties, and in Beulah, Rye, and Westcliffe, Colorado. State and federal emergency response officials expect these disruptions to continue through the remainder of the summer season, with flood warnings and business closures continuing to cause cancellations while agricultural producers lose livestock, fencing, and grazing lands. In already isolated rural communities, the ongoing road closures are limiting access to work, schools, pharmacies, medical care, and other essential services.

Governor Polis has requested a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration for the Aspen Acres Fire and Gold Mountain Fire. With over $17 million in validated damages, and with significant gaps in private insurance coverage, the Aspen Acres Fire meets the Federal Emergency Management Administration’s threshold for both Public and Individual Assistance. Losses incurred due to the Gold Mountain Fire meet FEMA’s threshold for Public Assistance.

Successful recovery is essential to restoring the counties’ economies, which depend on clean drinking water, tourism, agriculture, outdoor recreation, and hunting and fishing. Without additional support, residents could face potentially insurmountable barriers to rebuilding homes and businesses, increased drinking water and electric utility costs, and the loss of important habitat and grazing lands. In addition, these communities face ongoing hazards from the post-fire burn scars, including debris, burned trees, and threats to water quality and drinking water infrastructure.

As you are aware, a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration unlocks federal assistance programs, including Hazard Mitigation Assistance Grants, that are indispensable to recovery, mitigation, and long-term resilience. These communities urgently need federal relief to rebuild. We thank you in advance for your expedited review and approval of the Governor’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration.

INDIANAPOLIS – Today, the Indiana congressional delegation sent a letter to President Donald Trump in support of Governor Mike Braun’s August 20, 2026, request for a major disaster declaration following severe storms, tornadoes, and flooding that began on August 11.

The delegation thanked President Trump for his swift approval of federal emergency assistance following the August storms and urged him to approve Governor Braun’s August 20 major disaster declaration request, while reiterating the delegation’s support for the governor’s pending request for the June storms.

The text of the letter is below:

Dear President Trump,

We thank you for your continued support following the severe weather that has impacted our state this summer, including your swift approval of Governor Mike Braun’s Emergency Declaration request following the storms, tornadoes, and flooding that began on August 11. That assistance has provided important federal resources as state and local officials continue responding to widespread damage.

As those efforts continue, we write in strong support of Governor Braun’s August 20 request for a Major Disaster Declaration. The damage from these storms has been widespread and, in some places, historic. At least eight Hoosiers have died, more than 1,000 families have been displaced, and power outages peaked at more than 360,000 customers, with Northwest Indiana among the hardest hit and tens of thousands still without power. More than 1,700 structures have been destroyed, damaged, or otherwise affected. Flooding forced hundreds of evacuations and water rescues, while roads and bridges were damaged or washed out. In Anderson and Noblesville, the White River exceeded flood records set in 1913, and hundreds of homes along the river in Indianapolis were evacuated.

In the days since the storms, Hoosiers have stepped up to help their neighbors with donations, supplies, and other support. State agencies, local officials, first responders, and volunteers have been working around the clock as well, but the damage has created needs on a scale that communities cannot reasonably meet on their own. Our offices are also hearing from people who are still trying to understand what assistance is available and when it may come. A Major Disaster Declaration would provide the additional federal resources needed to support that work and help families and communities through the weeks and months ahead.

We also continue to support Governor Braun’s August 6 request for a Major Disaster Declaration for the separate storms that struck from June 6–26. Many communities, particularly in Northwest Indiana, were still dealing with damage from those storms when the August disaster hit, leaving local governments to respond to another round of serious damage just weeks later.

We appreciate the assistance your administration and FEMA have provided thus far, as well as your continued consideration of the June request. The emergency assistance already approved has been important to the immediate response, and we respectfully urge swift approval of the Governor’s August 20 request to provide the additional support needed for recovery. We stand ready to work with your administration and FEMA to support affected Hoosiers and communities.

Sincerely,

U.S. Senator Todd Young (IN)

U.S. Senator Jim Banks (IN)

Congressman Frank J. Mrvan (IN-01)

Congressman Rudy Yakym (IN-02)

Congressman Marlin Stutzman (IN-03)

Congressman Jim Baird (IN-04)

Congressman Victoria Spartz (IN-05)

Congressman Jefferson Shreve (IN-06)

Congressman André Carson (IN-07)

Congressman Mark Messmer (IN-08)

Congresswoman Erin Houchin (IN-09)

(Washington, D.C.) – Today, U.S. Representative Emanuel Cleaver, II (D-MO) urged the Trump Administration to reverse course on its plan to import 300,000 metric tons of foreign beef over the next 90 days. In a Truth Social post, the President indicated that these beef products will not be subject to out-of-quota tariffs and will allegedly be sold at 25% below current market prices. In a letter to President Trump, Congressman Cleaver acknowledged that Missourians are struggling with the rising cost of groceries, but emphasized that the importation of foreign beef fails to address the primary forces which have driven up the cost of beef products.

As noted in the Congressman’s letter, the size of the American cattle herd has reached a 75-year low, and this development has contributed to a shortage of beef products made available to retailers and consumers. Moreover, according to the USDA, the number of cattle producers declined by 17% between 2017 and 2022, an alarming trend largely influenced by drought conditions in cattle-producing areas alongside higher input prices for necessities such as farm equipment and feed.

“Flooding the market with Argentinian beef isn’t how you show support for American cattle producers,” said Congressman Cleaver. “Market manipulation is also a misguided approach to bringing down grocery prices, so I struggle to see who will benefit from this plan other than foreign competitors. If anything, the President’s proposal will further discourage cattlemen here in the United States from expanding their herds, thereby perpetuating one of the very problems that led to higher beef prices in the first place. Also, I’d be remiss to not point out that the proposed lifting of out-of-quota tariffs on foreign beef extends just past the upcoming midterm elections. Selling out American cattlemen in hopes of performing better at the ballot box is a sad betrayal of the farmers who keep this country fed.”

Statements in strong opposition to the President’s plan have been issued by the National Cattlemen’s Beef Association, the Missouri Cattlemen’s Association, and the Missouri Farm Bureau.

The official letter from Rep. Cleaver available here.
title: Congressman Cleaver Calls on President Trump to Reconsider Importation of Foreign Beef Products

WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a senior member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, today renewed his call for Postmaster General David Steiner to resign after the United States Postal Service finalized a rule restricting the delivery of mail ballots under President Trump’s election mail executive order despite an active federal court order expressly prohibiting Steiner from completing that rulemaking.

In the letter, Krishnamoorthi writes:

“What makes this even more troubling is that you previously assured Congress that you would do otherwise. At a June hearing before the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, you stated that the Postal Service ‘would comply with any court orders regarding voting by mail.’ You reiterated that assurance days later. Those were not casual remarks. They were commitments made under oath before the congressional committee responsible for overseeing your agency.”

On August 11, Judge Indira Talwani barred Steiner by name from “initiating or completing rulemaking to promulgate” the rule. Ten days later, at approximately 9:00 p.m. on August 21, USPS finalized the 95-page rule and scheduled it to take effect before it could even be published in the Federal Register. The policy remains blocked by two federal injunctions, and USPS has acknowledged that it lacks the legal authority to implement it for the 2026 election absent further relief from the courts.

Krishnamoorthi continues:

“That decision has fundamentally undermined the trust required of the Postmaster General. The stakes could hardly be higher. The Postal Service is entrusted with delivering Americans’ election mail fairly, reliably, and without partisan interference. Voters should never have to wonder whether the agency responsible for delivering their ballots is being used to advance a political agenda or whether its leadership will comply with the orders of the federal courts.”

Krishnamoorthi has repeatedly warned against efforts to place USPS in a gatekeeping role over election mail and previously called for Steiner’s removal over his efforts to implement President Trump’s election mail executive order despite federal court rulings blocking key provisions.

The Trump Administration is now asking the Supreme Court to overturn the lower courts’ rulings and clear the way for the policy before the November midterm elections.

Krishnamoorthi writes:

“A Postmaster General who tells Congress under oath that he will comply with federal court orders, and then completes the very rulemaking that a federal judge ordered him not to complete, has forfeited the confidence necessary to lead the United States Postal Service.”

Krishnamoorthi reiterated his demand that Steiner resign and requested a response by August 31, 2026.
title: Krishnamoorthi Demands Postmaster General Steiner Resign After USPS Finalizes Trump-Backed Mail Ballot Restrictions Despite Court Order

WASHINGTON – Congressman Steve Cohen (TN-9) today wrote to Governor Bill Lee urging him to seek assistance from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) after Saturday’s devastating storm.

The letter reads in part:

“I strongly urge you to request assistance from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), under the provisions of Section 501 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act, 42 U.S.C. 5121-5207 (Stafford Act), and implemented by 44 CFR 206.35, for Shelby County in response to the severe storms that struck Memphis and Shelby County on Saturday, August 22.

“The powerful storm brought winds exceeding 80 miles per hour and caused extensive damage to trees, utility poles, power lines, homes, and other infrastructure throughout our community. At the height of the storm, more than 140,000 Memphis Light, Gas and Water (MLGW) customers were without power. MLGW has since determined that this was the seventh most damaging storm in its history based on outage impact and the number of circuits affected.

“While MLGW crews have made significant progress, the scope of the damage remains substantial. As of Monday morning, over 45,000 customers and constituents of mine remain without power. MLGW has deployed hundreds of its own employees and brought in dozens of additional outside crews, with approximately 700 to 800 personnel working across the service area to restore power. More than 200 tree-trimming personnel are also assisting with the recovery.

“MLGW has advised customers to prepare to be without power for multiple days because of the extensive number of downed and damaged trees, poles, and wires. The storm also affected water treatment facilities, schools, roadways, and other critical infrastructure. Memphis-Shelby County Schools were forced to close on Monday because of widespread outages affecting dozens of schools and administrative buildings.

“The severity and widespread impact of this storm have placed a significant burden on Memphis and Shelby County residents, local governments, utilities, and emergency response agencies. Given the scale of the damage and the resources required for recovery, I believe a swift request for federal disaster assistance is prudent to ensure Shelby County has access to all available resources to address the damage and support affected residents.

“I respectfully urge you to act expeditiously to seek the appropriate federal assistance for Shelby County and stand ready to assist in any way necessary to support such a request.”

See the letter here.

title: Congressman Cohen Urges Governor Lee to Seek Federal Disaster Assistance

HOUSTON, TX — Today, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) released the following statement regarding the days-long power outage at the Rose Plaza Apartment Complex in Houston’s Fifth Ward. While power has been restored to some units, approximately half of the complex remains without electricity.

“What’s happening at Rose Plaza is completely unacceptable. In the middle of a Houston summer, families have now gone days without air conditioning and other basic necessities. That is dangerous, especially for our seniors and neighbors with health conditions.

The property owner has a responsibility to keep residents safe and to get this problem fixed as quickly as possible. Families should not be left sitting in the Texas heat for days waiting for their power to come back on.

My team is on the ground working to make sure residents are getting the help and resources they need. If you live at Rose Plaza and need assistance, please reach out to my office. We’re here to help,” said Congressman Menefee.

Based on information available to the Congressman’s office, the outage does not appear to be related to CenterPoint Energy’s equipment. CenterPoint technicians visited the property last week to assess the situation, and the remaining electrical issues appear to be on the property owner’s side.

Crews are currently working to restore power to the remaining buildings. At this time, however, there is no estimated timeline for when power will be fully restored across the complex.

“These are families, seniors, and children who have been without power, and they need help now. In Fifth Ward, we look out for our neighbors. That’s what this community has always done, and that’s what we’re doing now. But Rose Plaza has a responsibility to the people who call this place home. They need to make this right, take care of these families, and do whatever it takes to help residents recover from what they’ve been put through,” said Sandra Edwards, President of the 5th Ward Civic Club.

The American Red Cross and United Way are providing relief to residents impacted by the outage. Bottled water and food are being distributed, and assistance is available to help families replace groceries lost during the prolonged power outage.

Families in need of assistance with food, housing, utilities, or other essential needs can call 2-1-1 or 1-877-541-7905, or visit 211texas.org.

Rose Plaza residents who need additional assistance are also encouraged to contact Congressman Menefee’s Houston office at (713) 655-0050 or visit menefee.house.gov.

NBC News reported last month that the Defense Department’s internal overall cost for the war so far is $80 billion to $100 billion, including the cost of repairing damaged U.S. military bases, replacing destroyed aircraft and fully replenishing American weaponry, according to three U.S. officials.

“Nearly six months ago, Donald Trump launched us into yet another war with no strategy and no endgame,” Crow said in a statement. “As Trump, his family, and his friends in the oil industry use this conflict to pad their pockets, the cost on American taxpayers has grown by the day. Gas, groceries, and everyday goods have all gotten more expensive, with no end in sight.”

The Democrats’ letter also criticizes Trump’s response to questions about the war’s economic impact on Americans.

In May, the president was asked whether Americans’ financial situation was motivating him to make a deal with Iran. “Not even a little bit,” he replied.

“This is appalling and unacceptable,” the letter states.

In addition to asking for the Pentagon price tag for the war, the letter demands specifics on the economic impact on Americans, including the effects on inflation, employment and wages.

“Americans are being asked to write a blank check for a war they never asked for — a war that has jacked up costs on everyday goods and made us less safe,” Goodlander said in a statement. “President Trump and Secretary Hegseth owe the American people a full accounting: where every taxpayer dollar has gone, how this war is affecting hardworking families, and when it will end.”

The letter, which sets a deadline of Sept. 11 for the administration to provide a detailed war accounting, ends by telling Trump and Hegseth: “Americans did not ask for this war, and they cannot afford it. They do not have the luxury of ignoring their financial situation, and you shouldn’t either.”
title: NBC News: House Democrats demand Trump administration provide full accounting of Iran war costs

MALDEN, MA — Today, Democratic Whip Katherine Clark (MA-5) appeared on MS NOW’s On the Line with Alicia Menendez to discuss House Democrats’ agenda: lowering costs, protecting healthcare, and holding the crooks accountable. Below are excerpts of the conversation.

On Trump’s Reckless War in Iran:

“It is Americans who are paying the costs for Trump’s reckless war. All it has done is endanger our troops, cost us money for defense, and driven up the cost of gas in an environment where American families are already struggling to provide the basics.

“And that’s why Democrats are fighting for a more affordable America. That’s lowering the cost of living. That’s making sure everybody can afford healthcare where and when they need it. And that’s holding corruption and the people who are perpetrating it accountable.”

On Democrats’ Fight for an Affordable America:

“We keep the American people the main character. That’s our focus. What they’re going through, what they’re experiencing.

“When 60% of families are telling us they can’t afford the basics for their kids, for their aging parents, for themselves, then that is where our focus has to be.

“That’s why, as I said, we are looking at: How can we bring down the cost of gas by ending this reckless war? How can we bring down the cost of housing and groceries? How can we make sure that we are giving families a chance to find affordable childcare? And small businesses to flourish?

“We’ve seen a Trump administration that is completely cut off from what the American people need. And Republicans in Congress that are just following the Trump administration’s every whim.

“This has become a administration that is focused on one thing: making Donald Trump and his family, the very, very wealthiest Americans, and their largest donors, wealthier at the expense of everyone else.”

On Democrats Taking Back the House in November:

“When we win the majority in November, we are still going to have a hostile White House. A White House that has turned its back on the American people and their economic needs. So, we are very clear as Democrats, we will work with anyone who’s working for the American people.

“We are going to hold the crooks accountable. And so we will work with the White House — that is going to be part of our job and priorities. But, we are going to do everything we can [and] use every tool we have to make life easier and better for the American people. If the White House will join us in that, that is a win for the American people. If they won’t, we are going to continue to push and do what’s right for working people across this country who have waited far too long for this economy to work for them.”

On Holding the Crooks Accountable:

“This is a key piece of our work, and it’s the third prong of what we are talking about in the message we’re delivering and winning on: Reducing the cost of living. Allowing access to affordable healthcare. And making sure that we hold those who have been using this system to line their own pockets accountable. And that includes everyone from Donald Trump to Jared Kushner to anyone else who may have used taxpayer money to line their own pockets.

“That’s the work we’re going to continue to do. That is why we are winning in races around the country, because the American people understand that it’s our candidates, Democratic candidates, that are fighting for them. And that’s what every single campaign comes down to: Do you see my family? Are you going to fight for me?

“The answer from Democrats is ‘absolutely.’ And we are the answer to the chaos and corruption and cruelty that has become the hallmark of the Republicans in Congress and this president.”

Watch the full interview, HERE.

New data shows tariffs, the Iran war, and the "Big Beautiful Bill" are driving up costs for families

Santa Ana, CA — U.S. Representative Lou Correa (CA-46) released a report titledThe Trump Cost-of-Living Crisis in CA-46: How the Administration Is Making Life More Unaffordable, detailing how President Trump's tariff taxes, his war with Iran, and his so-called "Big Beautiful Bill" are driving up costs and squeezing household budgets for families in CA-46 and nationwide.

"Trump promised to lower costs on day one, and instead he's made life more expensive for working families in Orange County,” said Rep. Correa. “Every day I hear from constituents who are struggling to pay for groceries, gas, and health care – and this report shows exactly why."

The report finds that CA-46 families are already feeling the economic pressure:

Families in California have faced an estimated $4,600 average increase in basic living expenses under Trump, including a $999 average increase in housing costs.

Trump's Iran war has cost CA-46 families a combined $97 million — an average of $453 per family.

Electricity costs for CA-46 families rose by an average of $296 in 2025.

The average CA-46 family now spends $1,160 a month on groceries

From April 2025 to March 2026, 52,948 California individuals and households filed for bankruptcy – a 14.9 percent increase over the previous year.

An estimated 54,370 people in CA-46 are at risk of losing health coverage because of Trump's cuts to Medicaid and the ACA, and 27,000 more are paying higher premiums after Trump allowed enhanced ACA tax credits to expire.

A family of four earning $66,000 a year, for example, faces a premium increase of $2,651 – a 213 percent jump.

Across California, 300,838 people have now lost access to SNAP food assistance.

The full report is availablehere.

Garden Grove, C.A. – Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) released the following statement in response to an announcement by GKN Aerospace that it is creating a $100 million fund for families, small businesses, and community members impacted by the hazmat incident and evacuation over Memorial Day Weekend:

“Today’s announcement from GKN Aerospace is a step in the right direction. Committing $100 million in grant funding to aid the families, workers, and small business owners impacted by the recent evacuation is part of corporate accountability. This substantial commitment is a crucial and welcome step toward helping our community recover from the severe disruption, unexpected financial burdens, and stress caused by this crisis.

Our residents and local businesses showed incredible resilience during the evacuation and they deserve to be made whole by way of direct financial relief to help cover missed wages, temporary housing, and lost business revenue. I commend GKN for stepping up to take meaningful responsibility for the hardship experienced by our neighbors.

At the same time, we must recognize that the full economic impact of an emergency involving over 50,000 displaced residents and 5,000 local businesses is complex and still unfolding. While $100 million represents significant progress, I am calling on GKN Aerospace leadership to remain open to evaluating the true long-term costs. If this initial fund proves insufficient to make every affected family and business whole, GKN must be prepared to step up with additional support.

Full accountability means ensuring no single resident or small business owner is left absorbing the financial toll of this incident. I look forward to working closely with GKN, local officials, and community leaders to ensure these grant funds are distributed swiftly, equitably, and transparently,” said Representative Tran.

On Thursday, May 21, the Orange County Fire Authority reported a leak of methyl methacrylate, a volatile and flammable chemical, from a 34,000-gallon storage tank at the GKN Aerospace plant in Garden Grove. The risk of a toxic leak or catastrophic explosion prompted over 50,000 evacuations across Garden Grove, Westminster, Buena Park, Cypress, Anaheim, and Stanton. On May 29, Representative Tran urged Administrator Kelly Loeffler to issue a disaster declaration and expedite small business loans. The Small Business Administration issued a disaster declaration on June 11, providing small businesses adversely affected by the crisis with access to low-interest federal disaster loans. On August 18, Representative Tran introduced the Hazardous Materials Transparency Act, to mandate that facilities like GKN properly and regularly notify the communities they operate in about the safety measures that are taken to avoid danger to residents and small businesses.

###
title: Representative Tran Issues Statement on GKN’s $100 Million Fund for Families Impacted by the Hazmat Incident

Washington, DC – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) led a letter with his National Security Task Force co-chairs Representatives Jason Crow (CO-06) and Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) to President Trump and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth demanding a full public accounting of the economic costs of the war with Iran as prices rise for American families nationwide.

Read the full letter HERE.

"What was billed as a two-week operation is now a full-scale war that has lasted for over 150 days, cost at least $37 billion, and claimed the lives of 18 servicemembers. At the same time, prices across the country have gone up significantly, placing the burden of this conflict on American families. By June 9, you had claimed that the war in Iran was almost over 38 times. Instead, the war has continued, leaving Americans across the country with no idea when this war will come to an end and when prices will come down. This uncertainty, and the months of higher costs have taken a toll, impacting Americans’ ability to budget, plan, and save for the future. These costs are untenable, and the American people deserve better," wrote the members.

The letter details a request for information on the cost of operations, changes in the oil and energy markets, and macroeconomic impacts. It comes following the Department of Defense’s supplemental request for tens of billions more to fund the ongoing war in Iran and concerns about the risks to American economy, personnel, and safety overtime.

An Army Veteran, Representative Tran is a member of the powerful House Armed Services Committee and serves as a member of the Readiness Subcommittee and the Intelligence and Special Operations Subcommittee. Tran has voted for or cosponsored multiple War Powers Resolutions to reassert Congressional authority over the war, includingH.Con.Res. 40,H.Con.Res. 38, andH.Con.Res. 86, and joined the Democratic Veterans Caucus in aletter to President Trump calling for the same. In May 2026, Tran joined fellow members of the Lowering Costs Caucus in aletter urging the Trump Administration to address skyrocketing energy prices.Tran serves as Co-Chair of the House Democratic Caucus National Security Task Force.

title: Representative Derek Tran Raises Alarm on the Cost of the Iran War for American Families
