WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jahana Hayes (CT-05), a member of the Congressional Head Start to Congress Caucus, was joined by Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren (CA-18) and Congressman Greg Landsman (OH-01) to introduce the Head Start Expansion and Improvement Act to triple annual funding for Head Start and Early Head Start to $36 billion for Fiscal Years 2027-2032. The bill aims to infuse federal dollars into the early education program to expand access to more children and families, recruit and retain staff, and address dire physical infrastructure needs.

Head Start is the nation’s flagship early learning program, supporting healthy child development and acts as a lifeline for the most vulnerable children and families in the United States. In Fiscal Year 2026, Head Start served nearly 700,000 children and families, including more than 4,450 in Connecticut. Despite the proven success of Head Start and Early Head Start, they remain largely under-resourced, outdated, and understaffed. Earlier this year, the National Head Start Association found that nearly twenty percent of all Head Start and Early Head Start staff positions were vacant. Additionally, the most recent Head Start Facilities Report submitted to Congress by the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) found that 61 percent of Head Start facilities surveyed were identified as needing improvement to their physical infrastructure. Without intervention, the worsening workforce and infrastructure crises could jeopardize Head Start programs in Connecticut and throughout the country.

“Head Start is one of the greatest anti-poverty programs that we have. It offers high-quality education, health, and social services to the youngest and most vulnerable among us during a critical developmental stage,” said Congresswoman Hayes. “The Head Start Expansion and Improvement Act demands immediate action in addressing the growing needs of this vital program and allows more families to access its services.”

“It's critical that America's children receive a first-class education and have opportunities that create a solid learning foundation. Under the Trump administration, critical federal education programs and agencies have been increasingly under threat,” said Congresswoman Lofgren. “For more than 60 years, Head Start has played an important role in helping children enter school ready to learn and succeed. I am proud to join Reps. Hayes and Landsman in introducing the Head Start Expansion and Improvement Act to protect and preserve the Head Start program.”

"High quality preschool makes such a difference in our children’s lives, and Head Start gives families the support they need to succeed. Our legislation will help more families give their children the best possible start," said Congressman Landsman.

Specifically, the Head Start Expansion and Improvement Act would:

Expand eligibility to include families with children 5 years old and younger who are:

At or below 138 percent of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL).

Eligible for assistance under Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), or the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP).

Triple annual funding levels to $36 billion for Fiscal Years 2027-2032.

Establish a grant program providing $1 billion in annual funding to renovate, expand, and acquire program facilities.

Provide student loan forgiveness for Head Start and Early Head Start child care workers.

Establish a grant program to increase salaries for Head Start and Early Head Start workers.
title: Hayes, Lofgren, Landsman Aim to Triple Funding to Expand And Improve Access to Head Start

(Houston, Texas) — On Monday, August 17, 2026, Congressman Al Green will join Houston Haitians United, community leaders, advocates, and concerned residents for a press conference addressing the termination of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for nationals of certain countries, including Haiti, as well as alarming concerns surrounding immigration enforcement operations across the United States. The press conference will be held on the steps of Houston City Hall, located at 901 Bagby Street, Houston, Texas 77002, at 11:00 a.m. CT.

Congressman Al Green stated, “Temporary Protected Status exists to protect human beings who cannot safely return to countries confronting extraordinary and dangerous conditions. For Haitians, those dangers are real—from devastating natural disasters to widespread crime, violence, and instability. Long before the termination of TPS, Haitians in this country were subjected to false and harmful narratives advanced by President Trump that demeaned an entire community and placed innocent people at risk. Now, hundreds of thousands of Haitians face the possibility of being returned to a country where their safety may be in danger. I am honored to stand in solidarity with Houston Haitians United and all who believe that we can enforce our laws while respecting due process and protecting human dignity.”
title: Congressman Al Green Joins Houston Haitians United for Press Conference on the Termination of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) and Immigration Enforcement

ARCADIA, CA – Today, Congresswoman Judy Chu (CA-28) hosted her annual Congressional Leadership of the Year Awards Ceremony, honoring ten remarkable individuals and organizations from across California’s 28th Congressional District for their outstanding service and contributions to their communities.

“This year’s honorees are our everyday leaders, the educators, volunteers, activists, and small business owners who have made a real difference in the San Gabriel Valley,” said Rep. Chu. “I’m proud to recognize them all, not only for their accomplishments, but for the lasting impact they make every single day. Their service reminds us of the importance of community, showing up for others, and the difference one person can make.”

This year’s honorees include:

Ringo Chiu - Building Bridges Award (Temple City): Ringo Chiu, a Pulitzer Prize-winning photojournalist, was recognized for his dedication to building bridges through his work in photojournalism. Throughout his career, Ringo has repeatedly put himself at risk to document important events and moments, including California wildfires, Black Lives Matter protests, ICE raids, and more. Through his powerful visual storytelling, Ringo has consistently connected people, inspired empathy, and helped strengthen communities during times of crisis.

Fair Oaks Burger, Christy Lee and Janet Lee - Business of the Year (Altadena): Fair Oaks Burger was recognized for serving the Altadena community in the aftermath of the Eaton Fire. Owned by Christy and Janet Lee, the business has become a cornerstone for the Altadena community, providing a place for residents to come together, support one another, and rebuild by hosting farmers' markets, food giveaways, and countless community events.

Webster’s Community Pharmacy, Meredith and Michael Miller - Business of the Year (Altadena): Webster’s Community Pharmacy, currently owned by pharmacist Michael Miller and his wife Meredith, was recognized for their 100 years serving Altadena. Through challenges including the COVID-19 pandemic and the Eaton Fire, Webster’s has remained a trusted community resource. Beyond pharmacy services, the business supports local artists and businesses, operates Altadena’s Village Post Office, and raised funds for local business recovery through its “Beautiful Altadena 91101” merchandise following the Eaton Fire.

Javier Arellano, Owner of Taco Bout Good - Community Activist of the Year (Upland): Javier Arellano has consistently demonstrated a strong commitment to serving the Upland community through both his business and charitable efforts, including numerous meal donations to first responders and essential workers. After transforming his own life, he has used his second chance to give back, advocate for men’s mental health, and create a place of connection, hope, and service for the community. His dedication has earned him widespread recognition, including being named the Upland Chamber of Commerce's Businessperson of the Year in 2020 and his restaurant receiving the BusinessRate Upland Best of 2025 award.

Ruben Karapetian - Community Activist of the Year (La Crescenta): Ruben Karapetian was recognized for his leadership as the Executive Director of the Armenian National Committee of America (ANCA) - Western Region, which is the largest and most influential Armenian American grassroots advocacy organization in the Western United States. Working on the local, state, and federal level, Karapetian advocates for Armenian American priorities, promotes recognition of Armenian American history and identity, and advocates for human rights overseas.

Altadena Meals on Wheels, Shannon Anderson and Shelley Mitchell - Nonprofit of the Year (Altadena): Altadena Meals on Wheels (AMOW) was recognized for more than 53 years of service and dedication to ensuring seniors and individuals in need have access to nutritious meals and compassionate support. Shannon and Shelley have been a vital force in rebuilding Altadena Meals on Wheels from the ground up following the Eaton Fire, restoring its meal delivery services and ensuring vulnerable residents throughout Altadena continue to receive the care and support they need.

Dean Sheldon Serwin - Volunteer of the Year (South Pasadena): Dean Sheldon Serwin was recognized for more than a decade of dedicated volunteer service to the South Pasadena community, supporting youth development, education, the arts, and civic initiatives. From Scouting and school programs to the South Pasadena Arts Council and The Oneonta Club Foundation, Dean has helped uplift the community by supporting projects that benefit residents. He has also played a key role in local funding measures supporting education, public safety, library services, and infrastructure.

Otis Triplett – Volunteer of the Year (Pasadena & Altadena): Otis Triplett was recognized for his nearly three decades of serving the Pasadena community through volunteerism, mentorship, and civic leadership. SALEM, MA — Today, the Harvard Kennedy School released a comprehensive cost-benefit economic analysis of building the North South Rail Link, finding that the Rail Link would provide an estimated $36.9 billion in total benefits for the Commonwealth at full build.

The North South Rail Link is a proposed one mile long underground tunnel that would connect North Station and South Station in Boston. The full build proposal for the project would connect the two stations with two tunnels holding two tracks each, alongside a new Central Station in Downtown Boston adjacent to the Aquarium Blue Line station.

Congressman Moulton has been working with the Kennedy School since 2017 to study the Rail Link; this study is the culmination of those efforts and details ridership growth, modeshift from cars to trains, improved job access, and development opportunities.

The study found that Rail Link would transform Greater Boston and unify the region, massively expanding access to jobs by reducing commute times, slashing wait times for each line, incentivizing transit-oriented development (including desperately-needed housing) near stations and driving massive ridership gains.

Residents would have significantly more freedom to find housing across the region and would save hours each week by avoiding Boston traffic. Commuters living on Northside rail lines—assuming a full build, regional rail, and electrification—would be able to access 147% (136,600) more jobs within one hour on average, while Southside line commuters would be able to access 26% (40,000) more jobs within one hour on average. The average station wait time would be slashed from 34 minutes to less than 10.

“For decades, we've talked about the North South Rail Link as a nice idea for the future, but this study proves it's an economic necessity for the present,” said Congressman Moulton. “This project would bring nearly $40 billion in benefits for Massachusetts, and would bring more jobs, shorter commutes, and less time stuck in traffic for families across Massachusetts. This is how we grow our economy, create good-paying jobs, and make Massachusetts a place where people can afford to live, work, and build a future. The case for the North South Rail Link has never been stronger. It’s time to build it.”

“This is the first major study to examine the economic benefits of the NSRL—not just the costs,” said Linda Bilmes, Daniel Patrick Moynihan Chair in Public Policy and Public Finance, Harvard Kennedy School. “Our research shows that the benefits outweigh the costs by a large margin that grows over time. Great public projects begin with people imagining bold ideas. Governors Michael Dukakis and William Weld, along with countless other leaders in Massachusetts, have long shared the vision of a fully connected regional rail system. Congressman Seth Moulton is inspiring a new generation to carry that vision forward.

“Our research found that a North-South Rail Link would create jobs, open up housing, connect people to opportunity and reinvigorate Greater Boston for future generations. After decades of asking whether we can do this, perhaps the better question is: why not?"

“Instead of your train reaching the end of the line at South Station, just imagine it continuing through Boston and connecting you to the entire northern half of the system. Our study puts numbers around those benefits—and finds a compelling economic case for what is really a pretty simple idea.” said Brian Iammartino, Adjunct Lecturer in Public Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School.

Congressman Moulton will continue to advocate for the construction of the North South Rail Link to bring massive transit-oriented development to Massachusetts and to reduce commute times for many.

The full report can be found here.

###
title: Moulton Applauds Harvard Kennedy School Study on North South Rail Link, Highlights Nearly $40 Billion in Total Benefits for Massachusetts

Washington, D.C. – Today, on the solemn fifth anniversary of the Taliban overtaking Kabul—the capital and largest city in Afghanistan—Congressman Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34) is sharing his firsthand experience working with Lieutenant Colonel (LTC) Marvin “Lee” Chase and a CIA operative to save the lives of six Afghan pilot allies and their families. Since 2018, the Congressman has served as the co-chair and founder of the Congressional Uzbekistan Caucus, which played a pivotal role in securing the safe passage for our allies into the neighboring country of Uzbekistan.

Congressman Gonzalez’s testimony can be viewed here.

An edited transcript of Congressman Gonzalez’s account is as follows:

“The story we're about to tell you is something that happened five years ago on the anniversary of the withdrawal from Afghanistan. I'm on vacation. It was my August break, so I took a break to Spain with my wife. We're actually in the hotel in Madrid, and I get a call from a constituent of mine from my district in Texas telling me, ‘Hey, there's this situation. There's this lady from your district that married this colonel that lives in Virginia, that was in Afghanistan.’

“And he [LTC Chase] tells me a story about these Afghan pilots, our allies, who trained and worked with us [the United States military] and trained some of our pilots for over a decade...And as we were evacuating, they're not evacuated, and they haven't made it through the gate—and neither have their families. And the Taliban knows who they are and where they are and was visiting their homes. They wanted to kill them and their families because they were our allies. And he said, ‘We're just seeing what you can do.’

“Well, penetrating the State Department during that period was impossible, even for a member of Congress. Their lines were just booked. They weren't answering calls. I mean, just the evacuation of 172,000 people in that short amount of time was an extraordinary achievement even though I didn’t agree with it…

“…I happened to be the Chair of the Congressional Uzbekistan Caucus, the neighboring country…I had had a meeting with the Uzbek government...not that long ago. And the foreign minister, Minister Kamilov...we traded numbers. Never thought I was going to have to call him or him call me. But that night, I called him…and he recognized my number…

“It was late in the evening. And I said, ‘Well, I'm calling because we have a peculiar situation, and I need your help…we have some allied Afghan pilots who are friends of ours who are flying our planes…And the Taliban is chasing them down, trying to kill them, and we’re trying to find a way for them out. Is there a way you can help me get them into Uzbekistan?’

“It went silent…and then he [Minister Kamilov] tells me, ‘You know what, let me see what I can do'…about two hours later, an hour or two later, he calls me. He says, ‘I have a place where they can land safely, and we’ll give you the coordinates of the airport and the location.’

“…I call the Colonel. I said, ‘I think we can help. I’ve got a place for them to go and a way for them out.’ And he contacts the pilots…they tell him, ‘We’re out of fuel.’ They were out of fuel because they had already tried to fly to Uzbekistan, and they had been turned back.

“…We worked on this case all night long. A few hours later…I get a call back that said they were able to get fuel, by force, but they fueled up all these planes…and were ready to go…They took off, and I called the foreign minister and said ‘Hey, they’re in the air. They’re on their way.’ And they made it to Uzbekistan…at the time, they were also being turned back. They said, ‘Well, Congressman Gonzalez and Minister Kamilov have given us clearance to land…’

“Ultimately, they were there for six weeks, longer than we were hoping for and longer than the Government of Uzbekistan was hoping to have them…the minister was calling me, telling me, ‘You need to get these guys out of here because the Taliban has intel. They know they’re here. They know we have them…’

“It took us six weeks…to get them out of Uzbekistan, and then they went to Tajikistan and Qatar and eventually made it all back to the United States. The Colonel was able to—through the CIA operative, who was also working in conjunction with us through this whole process—get the families…and they were actually able to come into Virginia, I think, before the pilots actually got here…

“I never thought I would ever be in the middle of one of these situations, but those were personal relationships that I made traveling the world, traveling the world with colleagues on the other side of the aisle, making myself available to join caucuses and learn about a country I never thought I was going to learn about and build relationships in places that we never expected we would…

“We saved six of our pilot allied friends’ lives and their family. They’re all living here in the United States safely and started a new life.”

Background:

During the United States’ chaotic withdrawal of American troops and U.S. allies out of Afghanistan, which Congressman Gonzalez strongly condemned, the Taliban forcefully captured the city of Kabul and overtook its government on August 15, 2021. Eleven days later, on August 26, 2021, an ISIS-K terrorist freed by the Taliban committed a heinous attack outside Kabul’s airport at Abbey Gate, killing 170 Afghan civilians and 13 American service members, including a 20-year-old from Texas. On August 30, 2021, the final U.S. military aircraft departed Kabul and officially ended the 20-year war.
title: Five Years Later: Congressman Gonzalez Recollects on Saving Six U.S. Allies During Withdrawal from Afghanistan

Today, Congresswoman Maxine Waters (D-CA), the top Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, issued the following statement after U.S. District Judge David O. Carter temporarily blocked the Trump Administration from suspending the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA) from federal homelessness grant programs, protecting approximately $241 million in dedicated federal funding as well as immediate future funds supporting programs that serve more than 11,000 people.
“In the face of the Trump Administration’s continued attacks toward people experiencing homelessness, I am glad to see Judge Carter demonstrate some humanity. Los Angeles is on the front lines of America’s homelessness crisis and continues to confront it head on, with nearly 73,000 people experiencing homelessness on any night across Los Angeles County. Instead of working side by side to address this crisis, the Trump Administration’s response was to jeopardize hundreds of millions of dollars and cut off critical services for more than 11,000 people in dire need of assistance, with no real plan for what would happen to them next.
Of course, none of this should surprise us. Time and time again, Donald Trump has made it painfully clear that he doesn’t give a damn about solving America’s affordable housing and homelessness crisis. Since returning to office, he wasted no time attacking the Department of Housing and Urban Development and the programs millions of Americans depend on. And more recently, when Democrats and Republicans in Congress handed him the most significant housing legislation in decades—and frankly an easy win—he threw a tantrum and refused to sign it. Thankfully, we did not need him. The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act became law anyway.
While I commend this decision, a judge should never have to stop the President of the United States from making our nation’s homelessness crisis worse. This ruling is a reprieve, not a solution. Americans need affordable homes, stable housing, and a federal government that actually cares whether they have a roof over their heads.
Unlike Donald Trump, Democrats are not sitting around waiting for this crisis to get worse nor are we actively fueling it. While he told us himself that “no one gives a shit about housing,” I introduced the Ending Homelessness Act to make the investments necessary to move people off the streets and into safe, stable, affordable homes. And just as I worked across the aisle to get the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act across the finish line, I will continue fighting for real solutions. Trump can keep trying to tear down the programs Americans depend on. Democrats will keep building them back stronger.”
###
title: Ranking Member Maxine Waters Applauds Federal Court for Blocking Trump’s Cruel Attack on Los Angeles Homelessness Funding

Washington, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) today celebrated the U.S. Department of Justice’s (DOJ) award of thousands of dollars in federal funding to communities across Virginia’s Seventh Congressional District to strengthen local law enforcement operations and improve public safety.

“As a former prosecutor, I care deeply about ensuring our communities remain safe. That’s why I work with local law enforcement to ensure they get the tools and resources they need to do their jobs effectively,” said Vindman. “I’m proud to see Virginia’s Seventh Congressional District receive this federal funding to strengthen public safety. I’ll keep fighting to bring federal resources back home, supporting the dedicated public servants who work every day to respond to emergencies and keep families safe.”

All three grants were awarded through the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) Program. Administered by the DOJ’s Bureau of Justice Assistance (BJA), the program provides non-competitive formula grants to support personnel, equipment, training, and technology across the criminal justice system.

Spotsylvania County was awarded $29,500 in funding that will enable the Spotsylvania County Commonwealth’s Attorney’s Office to purchase up to nine portable, high-performance forensic laptops for the secure and efficient review of large volumes of digital evidence, including social media content, body-worn camera footage, cellphone extractions, and data from other electronic devices.

These specialized laptops are designed to support forensic software and applications, allowing prosecutors to review evidence more effectively and prepare cases more efficiently. The laptops will be assigned to prosecutors to enhance case preparation and litigation.

The City of Fredericksburg was awarded $16,552 in funding, which will allow the city to replace an all-terrain vehicle (ATV) used to patrol the City’s watershed, which spans thousands of acres.

The ATV enables officers to efficiently patrol rugged, hard-to-reach areas, including hills, muddy trails, and undeveloped land that are inaccessible to standard patrol vehicles. Replacing the ATV will help improve patrol coverage and support faster response times in remote areas.

Stafford County was awarded $37,657 in funding to enhance public safety, emergency response, and officer safety by purchasing critical equipment for its ATV Team, Traffic Safety and Volunteer Unit, and SWAT Team. It will also support the acquisition of a new all-terrain vehicle to improve search and rescue operations and response in difficult terrain, portable jump starter packs to reduce response times for disabled motorists, and advanced night vision equipment to strengthen tactical operations during low-light incidents.

###

WASHINGTON – Today, House Committee on Education and Workforce Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03) sent a letter to Acting Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling and Assistant Secretary Daniel Aronowitz demanding answers about reported settlement negotiations with companies selling junk health plans that use sham employment or partnership relationships to circumvent federal consumer protections and state oversight.

The reported negotiations come amid growing concerns about so-called health plans tied to fictious jobs or downloading an app, which can evade many Affordable Care Act protections and state insurance oversight by misclassifying consumers as employees or business partners. According to Bloomberg, more than 100,000 U.S. households have purchased plans tied to purported employment relationships, with some consumers left facing significant medical bills due to barebones health plans that fail to offer adequate coverage. Patient and consumer groups have also sounded the alarm.

In his letter, Ranking Member Scott urged the Department to ensure that any action it takes is consistent with federal law and does not leave consumers without meaningful protections or state oversight.

“Any settlement or other action that is inconsistent with the Department’s obligations under these laws would be an inappropriate exercise of power at the expense of consumers and state authority to regulate health insurance,”wrote Ranking Member Scott. “I remind you of your obligation to ensure that any action taken must be consistent with federal law, including the requirements of ERISA and the Administrative Procedure Act.”

Ranking Member Scott is also seeking an update on the status of the settlement, whether the Department has changed its legal position, and whether the Department is preserving all records of meetings and communications between political appointees and Data Marketing Partnership, in compliance with federal law and regulations.

Further, Ranking Member Scott requested information about complaints from consumers and state regulators regarding the plans sold by Data Marketing Partnership or similar entities.

U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), and U.S. Representatives Mike Quigley (D-IL-05) and Danny Davis (D-IL-07) today announced that the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) has awarded $696,250,000 in federal funding to Amtrak projects based in Chicago. One of the three projects receiving funding—the South Bridge Rehabilitation—is part of the Chicago Hub Improvement project (CHIP), a multi-phased project to revitalize Chicago Union Station and its surrounding infrastructure, as well as revolutionize Midwest passenger rail.

The funding was awarded through the Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail (Fed-State) grant program, which supports capital projects that repair, improve, or expand intercity passenger rail service.

“Our state’s top-notch rail system keeps our economy moving while allowing Illinoisans to travel from Chicago to Carbondale. This latest federal investment into Chicago’s Amtrak facilities and infrastructure reflects the city’s status as a thriving transportation hub,” Durbin said. “I look forward to seeing this funding turn into concrete improvements to our rail infrastructure, and in turn, delivering an even better experience to Amtrak riders.”

“Investments in our rail infrastructure are investments in our economy, making sure our rail network is safer, faster and more efficient for people and goods to get where they need to go,” said Duckworth. “This funding will help support critical upgrades to our rail infrastructure and strengthen our city’s role as a national hub for Amtrak. I will continue working alongside Senator Durbin, Congressman Quigley, Amtrak leadership and our local leaders to ensure our communities have the support they need to modernize our rail network, improve reliability and keep trains moving safely and efficiently for generations to come.”

“Safe, affordable, and accessible rail travel is critical to the success of Chicago and the Illinois region. This grant will make improvements and repairs that will modernize passenger rail service in our area for the millions of people who utilize these services. I have talked about the dangers of disrepair in our rail system for many years, and I have particularly called out the damaged bridges in the region that are long past the need for repair. I am pleased that this grant will help address these issues and improve access to safe and efficient rail services for Chicagoland residents for many years to come. I will continue working with my colleagues in the House and Senate to bring home more funding to achieve these goals,” said Quigley.

“The 7th District has long felt the impact of aging infrastructure, and our residents deserve a rail system that is safe, reliable, and built to last. This funding is not just an investment in steel and concrete — it is an investment in the working families who depend on Amtrak to get to their jobs, their schools, and their loved ones every day. I am proud to have fought alongside my colleagues to secure these resources, and I will keep pushing to ensure Chicago's West Side and communities across our region benefit from the good-paying jobs and safer travel this project will bring,” said Davis.

The three Amtrak projects receiving a portion of the announced $696,250,000 are:

Midwest Maintenance Facilities Modernization P3 ($572,000,000). The proposed project was selected for Right of Way Acquisition and includes activities to improve efficiency and safety at Amtrak’s Chicago-area Midwest Maintenance Facilities by relocating certain maintenance facilities from Amtrak’s 14th St. Yard to the to-be-acquired Canal St. Yard to support ongoing operations. The project will improve service and system performance because it will provide a modern, efficient maintenance and inspection facility and increase the ability to meet anticipated demand. The project will benefit Blue Water, Borealis, Hiawatha, Illini/Saluki, Illinois Zephyr, Lincoln, Pere Marquette, Wolverine routes.

Chicago Rail Bridge Renewal P3 ($87,000,000). The proposed project was selected for Project Development, Final Design, and Construction to rehabilitate or replace approximately 17 aging viaducts, bridges, and ancillary structures at Chicago’s Canal Street Yard as part of Amtrak’s Chicago Rail Bridge Renewal P3 Project. The project will enhance safety and improve system and service performance because it will correct critical structural deficiencies and eliminate hazards for rail operations, drivers, and pedestrians. The project will benefit Blue Water, Borealis, Hiawatha, Illini/Saluki, Illinois Zephyr, Lincoln, Pere Marquette, Wolverine routes.

South Branch Bridge Rehabilitation ($37,250,000). The proposed project will rehabilitate the existing South Branch Bridge and Project Development activities for a future bridge replacement. Activities will support the immediate state of good repair including the replacement of missing fasteners, defective hardware, and replacement parts to balance, support machinery and plan for a future replacement. The project will enhance safety and increase reliability by bringing the over-110-year-old South Branch Bridge into a state of good repair. The project will benefit Amtrak’s Blue Water, Lincoln, Pere Marquette, River Runner, and Wolverine routes.

In 2023, Durbin and Duckworth announced $93.6 million in secured federal funding for CHIP through the U.S. Department of Transportation’s (DOT) Federal-State Partnerships for Intercity Passenger Rail grant program, which received funding through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.

Durbin worked to bring parties together—local officials, the State, Amtrak, and other stakeholders including labor, environmental groups, and businesses—to ensure there was a unified push for the project. In September 2023, Durbin, Duckworth, and Quigley (D-IL-05) led 29 Midwest colleagues in a bipartisan, bicameral letter to Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and Federal Railroad Administration Administrator Amit Bose expressing their support for Amtrak’s Fed-State grant application for CHIP.

In May 2025, Durbin raised the issue of CHIP funding with Transportation Secretary Duffy, urging the DOT to obligate the remaining funds for the $93.6 million grant awarded in 2023. The Members also sent a letter of support to Secretary Duffy for this round of Fed-State grant applications.

Durbin, Duckworth, Quigley, and Davis will continue to build upon previous investments in the CHIP and lead stakeholders in advocating to advance the improvement of Chicago Union Station, cementing its critical importance to both Illinois and the Midwest.
title: Quigley, Durbin, Duckworth, Davis Announce More than $696 Million for Amtrak Upgrades in Chicago

Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, announced that two Northwest Ohio airports will receive United States Department of Transportation Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) awards for critical upgrades and improvements. The Defiance County Regional Airport Authority will receive $192,887 for pavement reconstruction, while the Put-in-Bay Township Port Authority will receive $96,710 for an airport-wide obstruction survey.

“Ohio’s strong aviation history shines bright across our Great Lakes region, and it is a privilege to build upon it by investing in local airport innovation and expansion,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). “Creating partnerships between Federal agencies and our local communities is vital to Northwest Ohio’ continued success. Working together to deliver these awards makes our airports safer and more efficient for all aviation staff, customers, and the businesses that rely on them. Together we are creating a standard of excellence that will help our region thrive for all the generations to come.”

Called Northwest Ohio’s “gateway to business and community,” Defiance County Memorial Airport has been undergoing many improvements over recent years to enhance its infrastructure. Today’s $192,887 investment will help the airport complete the final phase of reconstructing 1,091 square yards of East Apron pavement that has reached the end of its useful life. The Put-in-Bay Airport is located on South Bass Island and services both small commercial carriers and private aviators carrying freight or vacationers to the area. Its $96,710 award will help the airport conduct an airport-wide obstruction survey for the purpose of collecting detailed aeronautical and environmental data. Comprehensive data will make landing and takeoff safer and can help with future airport planning.

U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) is demanding answers from the United States Postal Service (USPS) following delays of time-sensitive mail deliveries across Southeast Michigan. In a letter to Postmaster General David Steiner, Congresswoman Dingell highlighted the responsibilities of the USPS to ensure deliveries are received in a timely fashion and the recent failures of the department to deliver voting materials during the Michigan primary elections. The mail was not returned, they sat in mailboxes, and they were not picked up.

USPS has a responsibility to deliver the mail reliably and on time, especially when those delays can directly affect Americans’ ability to participate in our democracy," said Congresswoman Dingell.

Dear Postmaster General Steiner:

This letter is regarding mail service disruptions in my district, particularly the delay of absentee ballots and political mail. The United States Postal Service (USPS) has a responsibility to remain accessible to all communities and ensure the delivery of essential mail, including bills, medications, legal documents, and urgent communications. The reliable delivery of time-sensitive mail is of the utmost importance.

I was alarmed to hear that on August 1, 2026, five carrier routes in Ann Arbor, Michigan, were left without assigned letter carriers, resulting in mail going undelivered. Just as concerning, USPS management failed to contact available employees to seek additional assistance in covering these routes, allowing the mail to remain untouched. Although employees are not required to work based solely on management’s outreach, failing to make any effort to find volunteers is unacceptable, particularly given that the state’s primary election was held on Tuesday, August 4, 2026. These delayed deliveries left many Ann Arbor residents without their scheduled absentee ballots and political mail, limiting their time to vote before the statutory deadline and possibly preventing them from casting their ballots and receiving important candidate information. USPS has a responsibility to deliver the mail reliably and on time, especially when those delays can directly affect Americans’ ability to participate in our democracy.

This incident is increasingly troubling, as I had raised concerns about persistent mail delays in Southeast Michigan in April of this year. One would expect the Postal Service to take these concerns seriously and to ensure that sufficient staffing and management procedures are in place to prevent similar failures. USPS plays a critical role in facilitating participation in our democratic processes, and I will continue to work to ensure my constituents have the reliable service they deserve.

I request clarity regarding this issue in my district and would like written responses to the following questions:

Was USPS aware of the five carrier routes in Ann Arbor, Michigan not receiving mail on August 1, 2026?

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Andrea Salinas (OR-06) introduced the Data Center Community Reinvestment Act, a bill that would tax the electricity data centers use and send that money to programs that build affordable housing, protect public lands and waterways, clean up hazardous waste sites, fund clean energy projects, and repair roads and bridges.

“As AI use expands and the demand for data centers grows, we need to ensure our communities aren’t left footing the bill,” said Rep. Salinas. “This bill taxes the energy used by data centers and reinvests that money in the programs our communities rely on, from affordable housing to conservation to cleaning up hazardous waste sites. Every community deserves to drive a hard bargain with data center developers, and at the end of the day, every community deserves to share in the benefits from data center growth.”

As data center demand grows, so will the strain on local infrastructure. Rep. Salinas’ bill would place a 1-cent-per-kilowatt-hour excise tax on electricity used by any data center with more than 1 megawatt of power capacity, whether that power comes from the grid or is generated on-site. Based on current data center electricity use nationwide, the tax is projected to raise about $1.76 billion a year.

The bill would split that revenue equally five ways among the following federal programs and funds:

The Land and Water Conservation Fund, which protects public lands and waterways. It would receive about $352 million more a year, an increase of nearly 40 percent.

The Housing Trust Fund, which builds and preserves affordable housing for the lowest-income households. It would receive about $352 million more a year, more than doubling its current funding.

The Hazardous Substance Superfund, which pays for the cleanup of hazardous waste sites when no responsible party can be identified.

The Highway Trust Fund, which funds road, bridge, and transit projects nationwide.

The Energy Technology Trust Fund, which would fund federal loan guarantees for clean energy, advanced nuclear, and grid infrastructure projects. Last year, Republicans rescinded funding for this loan guarantee program. Rep. Salinas' bill would restore a dedicated funding source for it.

Click here to view the full text of the legislation.

title: Rep. Salinas Introduces Bill to Tax Data Centers, Reinvest in Housing, Conservation, and Infrastructure

The letter follows reports of an intensifying mental health crisis aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln

The aircraft carrier’s crew is in its 9th month at sea and has spent a record 250 consecutive days without making land

Congressman Bell serves on the House Armed Services Committee

Washington, D.C. — Today, Representatives Wesley Bell (D-MO-01), Maggie Goodlander (D-NH-02), and Joe Courtney (D-CT-02) led a group of 34 lawmakers in demanding immediate answers from the Department of Defense on the conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln.

The letter addresses mounting reports of poor living conditions, food shortages, and a mental health crisis among the crew. The ship and its crew have been deployed at sea for more than 8 months — including a record-breaking 208 days without a single port call — and multiple sailors have reportedly attempted to jump overboard in recent weeks.

“Like the USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78) before it, CVN-72’s extended deployment is accompanied by deeply troubling reports about sailors’ mental health and living conditions. These reports are not political conjecture; they come from sailors’ worried family members,” the lawmakers wrote. “Navy leadership took the appropriate step in meeting to address families’ concerns, but there remains more to be done to ensure that the families and the public have faith that these sailors are being taken care of and that the Department is appropriately managing the fleet and its readiness for Operation Epic Fury.”

On Tuesday, the Navy Times reported on the mental health strain, exhaustion, and safety concerns of sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has been deployed for over eight months supporting President Trump’s war with Iran, which included a span of 208 continuous days without porting, a carrier record.

“The Ford and Lincoln's successive overextended deployments and subsequent challenges have become a pattern in the Administration's handling of its war against Iran. As of August 13, the USS George Washington (CVN-73) is reported to replace the Lincoln at some point in the future. The reported conditions on the Lincoln, following so soon after the reported conditions on the Ford, leave both Congress and the public concerned that the Department is not adapting quickly enough to the conditions in the CENTCOM area of responsibility, nor taking the appropriate steps to mitigate the continued challenges in our fleet,” the representatives concluded.

As a member of the House Armed Services, Foreign Affairs, and Oversight Committees, and representing a state with a large military community, Congressman Bell has focused much of his work in Congress on defending the men and women who serve our country. St. Louis, Bell recently hosted a roundtable with women veterans from across the region to hear directly about the unique challenges they face, and he continues to fight for the healthcare, benefits, and resources our service members and veterans have earned.

The full letter text can be found HERE and below:

“Dear Secretary Cao:

We write to express deep concern for the personnel and material readiness of the USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) and request information on the ship's deployment and future. The Lincoln and her crew have been deployed for more than 8 months, twice extended and still performing at a high level under constant combat conditions. The carrier deployed from San Diego on November 21, 2025, and was originally scheduled to return from deployment in May. Carrier crews are always prepared for extended deployments at sea due to potential operational requirements.

However, this crew has been extended multiple times and is still deployed in a combat zone 3 months after their originally scheduled return date – with no anticipated redeployment date in sight. Furthermore, the Lincoln has reportedly only pulled into port twice since deploying, once in December 2025 and a second time for a one-day port call in July 2026. This 208-day period without pulling into port was a modern-day record and uncharted territory for a Navy aircraft carrier and her crew. We recognize the severe logistical challenges that come with operating in a warzone. We also note that these challenges, including the inability to make port calls as frequently and the increased mental strain on sailors in a war environment, should be foreseeable and actions should be taken to mitigate the effects to the extent possible.

Like the USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78) before it, the Lincoln's extended deployment is accompanied by deeply troubling reports about sailors' mental health and living conditions. These reports are not political conjecture; they come from sailors' worried family members. Numerous sailors have reportedly attempted to jump overboard, in an escalation of challenges the Ford faced. In one instance, the wife of one of these sailors initially received a call from the carrier's ombudsman but has not received more information from the Navy in the last few weeks. Other family members have sounded the alarm on food shortages or quality issues since April.

These concerns reached fever pitch at an August 6 townhall in San Diego, where they were raised by family members of the Lincoln's crew to Acting Secretary Cao and other Navy leadership. Navy leadership took the appropriate step in meeting to address families' concerns, but there remains more to be done to ensure that the families and the public have faith that these sailors are being taken care of and that the Department is appropriately managing the fleet and its readiness for Operation Epic Fury.

The Ford and Lincoln's successive overextended deployments and subsequent challenges have become a pattern in the Administration's handling of its war against Iran. As of August 13, the USS George Washington (CVN-73) is reported to replace the Lincoln at some point in the future. The reported conditions on the Lincoln, following so soon after the reported conditions on the Ford, leave both Congress and the public concerned that the Department is not adapting quickly enough to the conditions in the CENTCOM area of responsibility, nor taking the appropriate steps to mitigate the continued challenges in our fleet. As such, we urge the Department to continue communicating with these sailors' families and the appropriate congressional committees, and we respectfully request the following information:

What additional resources is the Department providing for sailors who are serving under more difficult conditions on extended deployments?

What additional measures are being taken to ensure the safety of sailors who may be struggling with their mental health while on extended deployment?

What measures did the Department take to mitigate the effects caused by foreseeable strain on standard replenishment procedures in a contested or combat environment?

What specific measures did the Department take to overcome unanticipated resource strains caused by adversaries in the CENTCOM AOR?

What methods of communication can family members and the public anticipate the Department will use to share information about conditions or other developments on board? Does the Department plan to use the same methods for future extended deployments for Operation Epic Fury, if applicable?

At time of writing, does the Department consider there to be a food shortage or chronic hygiene issues on the Lincoln during this stage of deployment?

What lessons learned, related to either personnel or material readiness from the extended deployment of the Ford, were put into practice to mitigate strain on the Lincoln personnel?

What new procedures, both for personnel and material readiness, can be informed by the extended deployments of the Ford and the Lincoln and how may they be implemented for a potential deployment of the George Washington or other carriers facing lengthy deployments?

What lessons learned, related to the Ford's post-deployment, can be put into practice when the Lincoln returns for its maintenance availability?

If the George Washington shifts to CENTCOM to relieve the Lincoln, what are the Navy's plans to maintain its current force posture in INDOPACOM?

Sincerely,
title: Representatives Bell, Courtney, and Goodlander Lead Colleagues in Urging Clarity from Pentagon on USS Lincoln’s Overextended Deployment & Sailors’ Safety

WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representatives Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), Ranking Member of the Military and Foreign Affairs Oversight Subcommittee, and Robert Garcia (CA-42), Ranking Member of the House Oversight Committee, are demanding answers from the Department of Defense (DOD) about conditions on the USS Lincoln.

“Secretary Hegseth has claimed the rumors of overboard attempts and food rationing are overblown. If conditions are what he says they are and he has nothing to hide, then we will see if the information matches his claims. Our servicemembers are being asked to be away from family for months on end with inadequate conditions. That is unacceptable,” said Ranking Member Subramanyam.

"Sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln are going without food, dealing with contaminated water, and attempting suicide after hundreds of days at sea due to President Trump’s incompetent and disastrous war with Iran. Secretary Hegseth must answer for and improve these unacceptable conditions immediately," said Ranking Member Robert Garcia.

There have been reports for months about food rationing and insufficient food on the USS Lincoln. There have also been more recent reports of several servicemembers attempting to jump off the ship. The USS Lincoln has been deployed for more than 250 days, setting modern records for deployments without port calls.

The letter can be found HERE and below.

###

Dear Secretary Hegseth:

We write regarding the conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, specifically, the living conditions and access to mental health resources for the sailors. Recent reports have revealed disturbing sanitation conditions, food shortages, and deteriorating mental health among those deployed on the aircraft carrier, including multiple suicide attempts, with one sailor jumping overboard. Our sailors deserve better while they serve our country, and these deplorable conditions negatively impact morale and readiness. As Members of Congress, we have a duty to support our troops, and it is clear that additional oversight is needed aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln.

The USS Abraham Lincoln holds more than 5,000 sailors and Marines and departed San Diego last November. Now redirected to the Middle East to support the Iran War in Operation Epic Fury, the carrier has been deployed for over 250 days and has spent a record-setting 200 consecutive days at sea. At a town hall with Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, families of those aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln voiced their concerns directly. Among them were food shortages, water contamination, and disruptions in mail.

As the Ranking Members of the Oversight Committee and the Oversight Committee’s Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs, we request a classified briefing on the USS Abraham Lincoln’s conditions and answers to the following questions by August 28, 2026:

What is the current inventory of food aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln?

Please detail the food supply and delivery schedule over the course of the carrier’s deployment.

What sanitation issues have been identified aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, including broken bathroom facilities?

What health care, including mental health care, are available to the sailors aboard?

What behavioral health care professionals are on board and accessible to those seeking help?

How quickly can someone on board the ship meet with a behavioral health care professional after seeking help?

What steps can be taken to mitigate the disruptions to the mail system that sailors have experienced?

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao reportedly told family members that the USS Theodore Roosevelt is preparing to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln. Without jeopardizing national security, what details can be shared about the timeline for the ship’s relief?

The Committee on Oversight and Government Reform is the principal oversight committee of the House of Representatives and has broad authority to investigate “any matter” at “any time” under House Rule X. If you have any questions about this request, please contact Committee Democratic staff at (202) 225-5051. Thank you for your prompt attention to this request.
title: Ranking Members Subramanyam and Garcia Demand Answers About Conditions on USS Lincoln

WASHINGTON, DC — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández lideró una carta junto a 25 congresistas urgiendo a la gobernadora Jenniffer González-Colón a solicitar sin más demora al presidente Donald Trump una declaración de desastre mayor ante la crisis de agua que afecta a Puerto Rico. Bajo la ley federal Stafford, corresponde a la Gobernadora solicitar formalmente al Presidente una declaración de desastre mayor.

Una declaración de desastre mayor podría permitir el acceso a asistencia de FEMA para municipios y entidades públicas, ayuda para individuos y familias afectadas, y préstamos por desastre de la Administración de Pequeños Negocios (SBA) para hogares y negocios elegibles. También podría proveer fondos para cubrir costos de respuesta a la emergencia, reparar infraestructura pública afectada, movilizar asistencia federal directa y financiar medidas para fortalecer la infraestructura y reducir el impacto de futuras emergencias.

“Puerto Rico enfrenta una crisis de agua que ya no puede atenderse con medidas temporales. Más de 180,000 hogares están bajo racionamientos de hasta 48 horas, y durante demasiado tiempo cientos de miles de personas han sufrido interrupciones en el servicio,” escribieron el Comisionado Residente y los congresistas. “La Gobernadora es quien debe solicitar esta declaración al Presidente, y debe hacerlo sin más demora para que podamos movilizar toda la asistencia federal disponible. El pueblo de Puerto Rico no puede seguir esperando.”

La carta, liderada por el Comisionado Residente, contó con el respaldo de 25 miembros del Congreso, reflejando un creciente apoyo en Washington al reclamo para movilizar recursos federales adicionales ante la crisis de agua en Puerto Rico. Esta semana, la Asociación de Alcaldes también apoyó el reclamo del comisionado residente.

La carta fue firmada por el demócrata de mayor rango del Comité de Recursos Naturales, Jared Huffman (CA-02), el demócrata de mayor rango del Comité de Seguridad Nacional, Bennie Thompson (MS-02), y el senador Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), junto a los congresistas Sam Liccardo (CA-16), Jim Costa (CA-21), Luz Rivas (CA-29), Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), Norma Torres (CA-35), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Darren Soto (FL-09), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Rob Menendez (NJ-08), Nellie Pou (NJ-09), Gabe Vasquez (NM-02), Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Daniel Goldman (NY-10), Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Ritchie Torres (NY-15), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Seth Magaziner (RI-02), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34) y Emily Randall (WA-06).

“Seguiré trabajando con los congresistas y alcaldes para obtener más recursos para ayudar a la gente a superar esta emergencia y para que la AAA rinda cuentas por su mala administración.” dijo el Comisionado Residente.

Como parte de esos esfuerzos, la semana pasada presentó un plan de cinco pasos para atender la emergencia, que incluye una declaración federal, asistencia inmediata para las comunidades afectadas y medidas para fortalecer la infraestructura de agua de Puerto Rico. Además, esta semana el Comisionado Residente y líderes congresionales con jurisdicción sobre Puerto Rico, solicitaron a la Oficina de Rendición de Cuentas del Gobierno federal (GAO) una investigación sobre el estado del sistema, el uso de fondos federales y la respuesta de las agencias federales.

###

Hernández Leads 25 Members of Congress in Calling on Governor to Request Major Disaster Declaration Over Water Crisis

WASHINGTON, DC — Congressman Pablo José Hernández of Puerto Rico led 25 members of Congress in a letter urging Governor Jenniffer González-Colón to request, without further delay, that President Donald Trump issue a major disaster declaration in response to Puerto Rico’s ongoing water crisis. Under the federal Stafford Act, the Governor is responsible for formally requesting a major disaster declaration from the President.

A major disaster declaration could provide access to FEMA assistance for municipalities and public entities, assistance for affected individuals and families, and Small Business Administration (SBA) disaster loans for eligible households and businesses. It could also provide funding to cover emergency response costs, repair affected public infrastructure, mobilize direct federal assistance, and support measures to strengthen infrastructure and reduce the impact of future emergencies.

“Puerto Rico is facing a water crisis that can no longer be addressed through temporary measures. More than 180,000 households are under water rationing of up to 48 hours, and for far too long hundreds of thousands of people have experienced service interruptions,” wrote the lawmakers. “The Governor is the one who must request this declaration from the President, and she must do so without further delay so that we can mobilize all available federal assistance. The people of Puerto Rico cannot afford to wait any longer.”

This letter, spearheaded by Congressman Hernández and signed by 25 members of Congress, underscores growing support in Washington for efforts to mobilize additional federal resources in response to Puerto Rico’s water crisis. This week, the Asociación de Alcaldes de Puerto Rico (Puerto Rico Mayor's Association) also announced its support for the Resident Commissioner’s effort.

The letter was signed by the House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (CA-02), House Homeland Security Committee Ranking Member Bennie Thompson (MS-02), and Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), along with Sam Liccardo (CA-16), Jim Costa (CA-21), Luz Rivas (CA-29), Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), Norma Torres (CA-35), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Darren Soto (FL-09), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Rob Menendez (NJ-08), Nellie Pou (NJ-09), Gabe Vasquez (NM-02), Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Daniel Goldman (NY-10), Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Ritchie Torres (NY-15), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Seth Magaziner (RI-02), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34), and Emily Randall (WA-06).

“I will continue working with members of Congress and mayors to secure additional resources to help people through this emergency and to hold the Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority (AAA) accountable for its mismanagement,” said Hernández.

As part of those efforts, last week he introduced a five-step plan to address the emergency, including a federal disaster declaration, immediate assistance for affected communities, and measures to strengthen Puerto Rico’s water infrastructure. In addition, this week Hernández and congressional leaders with jurisdiction over Puerto Rico issues requested that the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) investigate the condition of the island’s water system, the use of federal funds, and the federal government’s response to the crisis.

DURHAM, NC (August 14, 2026) — Yesterday, Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04) introduced the Sustainable Hospitals Act, legislation directing the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to study whether certain medical devices currently designated for single use could be safely reprocessed and reused.

“Every year, our health care system throws away enormous amounts of material, and we should be looking for smart, safe ways to reduce that waste,” said Congresswoman Valerie Foushee. “If we can safely reprocess and reuse certain devices, we can cut medical waste, lower costs, and make our health care system more sustainable. I’m proud to introduce the Sustainable Hospitals Act to take a closer look at this opportunity while keeping patient safety at the center.”

Hospitals and health care systems generate significant amounts of medical waste, while also facing pressure to control costs and make the most effective use of limited resources. Reprocessing certain medical devices may offer an opportunity to reduce waste and expenses, but any expansion of reuse must be grounded in rigorous safety standards, quality controls, and infection prevention practices.

“Duke Health is committed to delivering expert care in a way that is also fiscally and environmentally responsible. We support efforts to identify opportunities to reduce waste without compromising patient safety, and we believe this legislation establishes the right framework, grounding any expansion of single-use device reprocessing in rigorous FDA evaluation before it reaches the bedside." — Duke University Health System.

The Sustainable Hospitals Act would specifically direct HHS to examine:

Existing FDA pathways for reprocessing single-use devices, including where current regulations are sufficient and where barriers may exist;

The role of FDA-cleared third-party reprocessors compared with in-house hospital reprocessing;

The operational feasibility, including sterile processing capacity, staffing, equipment, chain of custody, tracking, and quality assurance;

Potential financial and environmental benefits, including waste reduction and cost savings, as well as additional labor, capital, and compliance costs; and

Liability and accountability issues if a reprocessed device fails or contributes to patient harm.

The study would also require consultation with hospitals, supply-chain leaders, infection prevention organizations, sterile processing professionals, clinicians, industry representatives, the FDA, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.

Within one year of enactment, HHS would be required to report its findings to Congress, including a list of the single-use devices that may have potential for safe reuse and recommendations for programs and activities to facilitate such reuse. Those recommendations could include the use of FDA-cleared reprocessors, appropriate cleaning and sterilization technologies, quality-assurance and tracking systems, and infection-prevention controls.

Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03) joined Governor Maura Healey in announcing a $139.6 million investment from the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) to the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (MBTA) to make major improvements to the Haverhill Commuter Rail line, helping deliver faster, safer and more reliable service for thousands of riders every day.

The funding will support the final design and construction of the Haverhill Double-Track Project, a major upgrade project that will add approximately 6.8 miles of new track between Reading and Andover to allow trains traveling in opposite directions to keep moving instead of waiting for one another. The project will also upgrade four stations in Reading, North Wilmington, Ballardvale and Andover with high-level platforms, to make those stations more accessible, and will modernize signals to improve safety at 15 rail crossings.

The federal funding will be matched by $34.9 million from the MBTA, bringing the total investment in the Haverhill Line project to $174.5 million.

“This is a significant federal investment in the future of commuter rail across the Merrimack Valley. This funding will deliver faster, more reliable service for riders in Haverhill, Lawrence, and communities throughout the region, along with safer crossings and modernized stations that are fully accessible to seniors and riders with disabilities,” said Congresswoman Lori Trahan. “I've been proud to fight alongside Governor Healey for federal funding like this because Massachusetts families deserve a transit system they can count on.”

“Since taking office, we’ve made historic investments to turn the T around, and riders are seeing the difference with fewer slow zones and more reliable service,” said Governor Maura Healey. “Now we’re keeping that momentum going. This $140 million award will help us make major improvements to the Haverhill Line that mean fewer delays, safer and more accessible stations, and better service for riders. We’re grateful to our federal delegation for helping us bring this funding home to Massachusetts.”

“This $140 million investment is not only going to make major safety, reliability, and accessibility impact along the Haverhill Commuter Rail Line, but it will also directly support Amtrak Downeaster operations and freight rail,” said Interim Secretary and MBTA General Manager Phillip Eng. “New double track gives us more operational flexibility and the ability to decrease commute time along the line. Upgrading four stations with high-level platforms is another step closer to a fully accessible MBTA system, and modernizing our signals will help to move trains more safely and reliably through the intercity area. Improving freight allows for more efficient movement of goods and helps to control costs for the public. I’m grateful for the leadership of Governor Healey to make these continued improvements possible and for our Congressional Delegation, MassDOT, and the MBTA for advocating for this funding with the foresight that it will have benefits for decades to come. I also want to thank the Federal Railroad Administration for their partnership and ability to move this project forward and through construction.”

What This Means for Riders

Today, parts of the Haverhill Line have only one track, which means a train sometimes has to wait for another train traveling in the opposite direction to pass. If there is a problem with a train or the track, that single-track section can also cause delays to ripple across the line.

This project will add nearly seven miles of second track between Reading and Andover, allowing trains to move in both directions at the same time and giving the MBTA more options to keep service moving when problems arise. It will also make it easier for crews to perform maintenance without disrupting service or requiring shuttle buses.

Approximately 10 miles of new fencing will also be installed along the corridor between Andover and Reading to help prevent unauthorized access to the tracks.

The project will also make Reading, North Wilmington, Ballardvale and Andover stations more accessible by adding high-level platforms that allow riders to step directly between the platform and train. The MBTA will improve signals at 15 rail crossings, eliminate the Tewksbury Street crossing in Andover and install approximately 10 miles of new fencing to improve safety along the tracks.

The improvements will benefit not only MBTA Commuter Rail riders but also Amtrak’s Downeaster service, which operates between Boston and Brunswick, Maine, and CSX freight service. By removing delays and increasing capacity, the project will strengthen passenger and freight rail connections throughout the region and support future improvements to rail service.

This funding is the latest championed by Congresswoman Trahan to support transportation-related projects throughout the district. Just this year, Trahan secured $1.2 million in federal funding for bridge improvements in Lawrence. Last year, she celebrated alongside Governor Maura Healey $251 million in federal funding secured through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law for the Rourke Bridge Replacement Project in Lowell. Trahan also secured $7,158,564 for the Lowell Regional Transit Authority and $7,194,360 for the Merrimack Valley Regional Transit Authority to purchase new buses and improve service, helping better connect communities across the district.

##
title: Trahan Celebrates $140 Million in Federal Funding for Haverhill Line Improvements

Ranking Member Scott Demands Answers from Labor Department on “Fake Job” Health Plans
WASHINGTON – Today, House Committee on Education and Workforce Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03) sent a letter to Acting Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling and Assistant Secretary Daniel Aronowitz demanding answers about reported settlement negotiations with companies selling junk health plans that use sham employment or partnership relationships to circumvent federal consumer protections and state oversight.
The reported negotiations come amid growing concerns about so-called health plans tied to fictious jobs or downloading an app, which can evade many Affordable Care Act protections and state insurance oversight by misclassifying consumers as employees or business partners. According to Bloomberg, more than 100,000 U.S. households have purchased plans tied to purported employment relationships, with some consumers left facing significant medical bills due to barebones health plans that fail to offer adequate coverage. Patient and consumer groups have also sounded the alarm.
In his letter, Ranking Member Scott urged the Department to ensure that any action it takes is consistent with federal law and does not leave consumers without meaningful protections or state oversight.
“Any settlement or other action that is inconsistent with the Department’s obligations under these laws would be an inappropriate exercise of power at the expense of consumers and state authority to regulate health insurance,” wrote Ranking Member Scott. “I remind you of your obligation to ensure that any action taken must be consistent with federal law, including the requirements of ERISA and the Administrative Procedure Act.”
Ranking Member Scott is also seeking an update on the status of the settlement, whether the Department has changed its legal position, and whether the Department is preserving all records of meetings and communications between political appointees and Data Marketing Partnership, in compliance with federal law and regulations.
Further, Ranking Member Scott requested information about complaints from consumers and state regulators regarding the plans sold by Data Marketing Partnership or similar entities.
To read the full letter, click here.

After passing the largest health care cuts in our nation’s history, Speaker Johnson now says he has a ‘plan’ to cut Social Security.
I will always defend Americans’ hard-earned benefits against Republican cuts. My Medicare and Social Security Fair Share Act proves that we can protect and strengthen these programs by making millionaires and billionaires pay their fair share. It’s time to pass my bill and keep the promise of Social Security for all generations.”

The independent actuaries at the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services and the Social Security Administration have confirmed Boyle’s legislation will extend solvency indefinitely.

Congresswoman Dina Titus, Regional Transportation Commission of Southern Nevada (RTC) and Boulder City officials held a news conference today to provide details about the upcoming Phase II Nevada Way Reconstruction Project to upgrade this key roadway in Boulder City, including safety improvements for vulnerable roadway users.

The project is being made possible by an $850,000 federal grant secured by Congresswoman Titus.

“Nevada Way is a main thoroughfare through Boulder City, providing a gateway to Lake Mead National Recreation Area and other tourist destinations around Boulder City,” Congresswoman Titus said. “This project will contribute to Boulder City’s economic vitality while providing additional pedestrian safety measures for its residents.”

“RTC is proud to partner with Boulder City and Congresswoman Titus to advance improvements that make Nevada Way safer and more welcoming for residents, businesses, and the customers they serve,” said Andrew Kjellman, RTC Deputy CEO. “We are grateful for Congresswoman Titus’ leadership and commitment to bringing resources back to Southern Nevada.”

The project will rehabilitate Nevada Way from Colorado Street to Park Street through the historic downtown area of Boulder City and reconstruct Colorado Street from Nevada Way to Utah Street, and Park Street from Nevada Way to Utah Street. The project will repave, restripe, and replace deteriorating asphalt on the roadway. The improvements include raised crosswalks with pedestrian-activated flashing beacons. The project also includes upgrades to ADA and pedestrian access, especially where sidewalks and ramps are currently limited.

The news conference was held at The Coffee Cup Café on Nevada Way and featured speakers were Andrew Kjellman, Deputy CEO, RTC, Boulder City Mayor Joe Hardy, Gary Poindexter, Public Works Director, Boulder City, and Congresswoman Titus.
title: U.S. Rep. Dina Titus, RTC and Boulder City officials highlight Nevada Way improvements

NORWICH, CT – Today, Reps. Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee, Wesley Bell (MO-01), and Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) led 15 of their colleagues on the House Armed Services Committee and 34 more Members of Congress in sending a letter to Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao expressing concern for the personnel and material readiness of the USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) and requesting information on the ship’s deployment and future.

“Like the USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78) before it, CVN-72’s extended deployment is accompanied by deeply troubling reports about sailors’ mental health and living conditions. These reports are not political conjecture; they come from sailors’ worried family members,” the lawmakers wrote. “Navy leadership took the appropriate step in meeting to address families’ concerns, but there remains more to be done to ensure that the families and the public have faith that these sailors are being taken care of and that the Department is appropriately managing the fleet and its readiness for Operation Epic Fury.”

Read the full letter here.

On Tuesday, the Navy Times reported on the mental health strain, exhaustion, and safety concerns of sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72), which has been deployed for over eight months supporting President Trump’s war with Iran, which included a span of 208 continuous days without porting, a carrier record.

Last month, Courtney led four of his colleagues on the Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee in sending a letter to Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao requesting information on the future of the USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78) and its scheduled maintenance following its return earlier this year after a 326-day deployment, the longest carrier deployment since the Vietnam War. Read the letter here.

U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and Jack Bergman (R-MI-01), alongside nine of their Michigan colleagues in the U.S. House, co-led a letter to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the Center for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) highlighting the essential role of Gift of Life Michigan. Gift of Life Michigan is the federally designated non-profit Organ Procurement Organization (OPO) serving Michigan. As CMS undertakes this year’s OPO recertification process, the lawmakers are urging the administration to consider the essential role Gift of Life Michigan and its nearly 400 staff statewide play in serving their communities and sustaining the systems that make life-saving organ, eye, and tissue donation and transplantation possible.

A copy of the letter can be found HERE and below:

Dear Secretary Kennedy and Administrator Oz:

We write as the congressional delegation representing Michigan to express our strong support for the recertification of Gift of Life Michigan, the federally designated non-profit Organ Procurement Organization (OPO) serving our state. As CMS undertakes this year’s OPO recertification process, we urge you to thoughtfully consider the essential role Gift of Life Michigan—and its nearly 400 staff statewide—play in serving our communities and sustaining the systems that make life-saving organ, eye, and tissue donation and transplantation possible.

Since its founding in 1971, Gift of Life Michigan has built deep and enduring relationships with hospitals, health systems, medical examiners, transplant centers, and local community leaders across the state. They have also developed a profound understanding of Michigan’s population, the regional healthcare and governmental landscape, and the unique cultural contexts that shape effective donation work—expertise that cannot be quickly recreated or replaced without significant disruption and added taxpayer expense.

During the current certification cycle, Gift of Life Michigan has increased the number of organs available for transplant by 29% and expanded the Michigan Organ Donor Registry by 1.2 million people through sustained public education and community outreach12. The organization has also grown youth education efforts from 3,700 to more than 38,000 students, per internal data. Additionally, according to data from the Michigan Department of Treasury and Michigan Department of State, Gift of Life Michigan worked with state legislators and the Secretary of State to make Michigan the first state in the nation to include a Donor Registry question on state income tax forms—an initiative that has already produced 38,000 new donor registrations since 2024.

Given Gift of Life Michigan’s decades of experience, strong performance, deep community partnerships, and critical role in ensuring access to donation and transplantation services, we urge CMS to provide full and fair consideration of the organization’s longstanding service and effectiveness.

Maintaining continuity with a well-established, community-rooted OPO is essential to preserving public trust, supporting donor families, and ensuring patients across Michigan and the nation continue to receive timely, high-quality, life-saving donation and transplant services.
title: Dingell, Bergman Co-Lead Letter Highlighting the Essential Role of Gift of Life Michigan
