Today, Congresswoman Suzan DelBene (WA-01) delivered a $500,000 ceremonial check to the City of Bellevue to replace old pipes and upgrade the wastewater management system along Lake Washington. DelBene secured the investment in the FY26 federal funding law.

This federal investment will be dedicated to the Lake Washington Sanitary Sewer Lines Program. First installed in the 1950s and 1960s, the wastewater management system’s pipes are aging and need to be updated. They currently serve approximately 1,900 residents in the Hunts Point, Yarrow Point, Evergreen Point, Medina South, Meydenbauer Bay, Killarney and Newport South areas. Without repairs and modernization, the “Lake Lines” will begin to fail and could release raw sewage into Lake Washington. This federal funding will aid the City of Bellevue in developing a plan to manage and update the system, which will protect public health and the local ecosystem.

“Lake Lines serve 1,900 members of our community, but the aging pipes’ location along the shoreline and in Lake Washington create challenges for upgrades,” said DelBene. “Bellevue has worked tirelessly to come up with a strategy to update these pipes to preserve access, protect public health, and avoid harm to Lake Washington. This funding will make a difference in the development and eventual implementation of this critical project.”

“Most people never think about the sewer lines running along Lake Washington - and that’s a good thing. But some of this infrastructure has been serving Bellevue since the 1950s and 60s, and now it is our responsibility to plan for what comes next,” said Bellevue Mayor Mo Malakoutian. “We are grateful to Congresswoman DelBene for helping secure this federal investment and for recognizing that a $1.2 billion challenge will require continued partnership. This funding helps us start that work now, protect Lake Washington and plan responsibly for the generations that will depend on it.”

DelBene secured over $22.2 million for 15 community projects across Washington’s 1st Congressional District in the FY26 federal funding package. Only non-profit, city, county, and Tribal entities are permitted to receive funding.
title: DelBene Delivers $500,000 for Bellevue Wastewater Improvement Project

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández presentó un plan de cinco puntos dirigido al gobierno federal para atender la crisis de agua que afecta a cientos de miles de puertorriqueños, que incluiría préstamos federales para pequeños negocios y agricultores.

En un video publicado en redes sociales, el Comisionado Residente hizo un llamado a la gobernadora para que solicite al presidente de los Estados Unidos una declaración federal de emergencia ante la crisis de agua en Puerto Rico.

Bajo la Ley Stafford, la gobernadora tiene la facultad de presentar formalmente esa solicitud. Hernández reiteró su disposición a buscar respaldo congresional para fortalecer la petición y aumentar sus probabilidades de éxito, tal como hizo con la declaración de emergencia energética en 2025.

De lograrse, dicha declaración aumentaría la disponibilidad de recursos de FEMA para atender la escasez de agua, incluyendo la distribución de agua almacenada y el reembolso de gastos de emergencia para los municipios y la AAA.

El Comisionado Residente además pidió que la solicitud incluya asistencia individual, lo cual habilitaría préstamos de la SBA para los negocios afectados por la sequía.

Por separado, el Comisionado Residente recomendará al Departamento de Agricultura federal que emita la designación de emergencia por sequía que las condiciones actuales incluyendo la sequía extrema ya registrada en el sur de la isla — ameritan bajo sus propios criterios, lo cual proveería ayuda para nuestros agricultores.

Finalmente, el Comisionado Residente indicó que deben iniciarse las gestiones necesarias para el regreso de los cientos de puertorriqueños de la Guardia Nacional actualmente desplegados en Washington, D.C., de manera que puedan apoyar la respuesta a esta crisis en la isla.

“Como reflejan estas cinco medidas, el gobierno estatal y federal pueden hacer más, y estoy en la mejor disposición de ayudar para que así sea”, concluyó el Comisionado Residente.

In an op-ed published by The Hill on August 10, 2026, Congressman James Walkinshaw (VA-11) touted that modernizing government technology is starting to pay off and that we must keep going.

Read the op-ed below or online at The Hill.

A veteran should not have to stare at a frozen screen, hitting refresh again and again, because an aging benefits portal struggles to keep up. A federal employee applying for retirement should not have to piece together records across a maze of disconnected legacy systems just to complete the final steps of their career in public service. And cybersecurity teams should not have to spend their days patching antiquated infrastructure.

But that is the price of letting federal technology fall behind: Americans wait longer to receive essential services, cybersecurity risks grow, and taxpayers pay to keep obsolete platforms on life support.

Congress created the Technology Modernization Fund to break that cycle, helping agencies replace legacy systems with secure, modern technology. A new Government Accountability Office report shows that work is beginning to pay off.

As of June 2025, the Technology Modernization Fund had invested roughly $1.03 billion in 68 modernization projects. The Government Accountability Office found that 11 projects have already saved $13.5 million, while 24 are expected to generate $1.06 billion in lifecycle savings, more than the fund has invested across all projects to date.

Those returns will take time. Most are expected in fiscal 2027 or later, reflecting the scale and complexity of the work underway. The largest projected savings are concentrated in three major efforts: modernizing the Department of Agriculture’s network, improving veteran identity systems at the Department of Veterans Affairs, and updating federal retirement systems at the Office of Personnel Management.

But direct savings tell only part of the story. The Government Accountability Office found that 37 Technology Modernization Fund projects are intended to strengthen cybersecurity, improve operations, or deliver better services without generating direct savings. In comments on the report, General Services Administration Administrator Ed Forst noted that direct-savings calculations do not capture the full value of costs avoided through more secure and reliable systems.

Congress now has three jobs: reauthorize the Technology Modernization Fund, keep it funded while its largest projects mature, and hold agencies accountable for results.

The Technology Modernization Fund is designed as a revolving fund, but agencies are still years away from realizing many of the anticipated savings, and not every worthwhile investment will produce a direct financial return. Congress must provide the funding needed to keep modernization efforts moving.

Congress must also make the fund workable for agencies taking on difficult, high-impact projects. That is why, during the House Oversight Committee’s markup of legislation to reauthorize the Technology Modernization Fund, I offered an amendment extending the standard repayment period from five to seven years. I also offered an amendment, adopted by the committee, requiring the Government Accountability Office to assess whether Technology Modernization Fund investments are reaching the government’s highest-priority legacy systems.

Most importantly, Congress must reauthorize the Technology Modernization Fund before it expires this September. Letting the fund lapse would leave agencies with fewer tools to replace systems that waste taxpayer dollars, expose Americans’ data, and hold back services people depend on.

The House Oversight Committee has already advanced bipartisan reauthorization legislation. Now the House and Senate must finish the job before the deadline. Congress cannot continue spending taxpayer dollars to keep obsolete systems on life support while pulling the plug on the fund designed to replace them.

###
title: ICYMI: Op-Ed by Rep. James Walkinshaw: Modernizing government technology is starting to pay off — let’s keep going

Energy Fuels CEO bought 74,000 shares days before the monument was cut by 90 percent, the largest insider purchase in company history

Washington, D.C. – Today, House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) and Oversight & Investigations Subcommittee Ranking Member Maxine Dexter (D-Ore.) opened an investigation into potential insider trading at Energy Fuels Inc., after the company's CEO and Chairman of the Board bought company stock days before President Trump announced he was shrinking Bears Ears National Monument by more than 90 percent.

On July 7, 2026, CEO Ross Bhappu purchased 74,000 shares, the largest insider purchase of stock in the company's history, increasing his ownership by 41 percent. Chairman Bruce Hansen purchased 4,000 shares the next day. On July 13, Trump opened nearly 3 million acres of federal land to mining, including uranium-rich areas of the San Juan Basin that had previously been protected.

“The timing of these stock purchases indicate that nonpublic information was potentially available to both you and Mr. Hansen,” the lawmakers wrote to Bhappu.

The lawmakers argue Energy Fuels' relationships with the administration put its executives in position to learn of the decision early and potentially profit from it. The company hired outside lobbyists that included a former Trump Interior official, identified strong government support as a selling point to investors in its expansion plans, and cited ongoing discussions with government sources as a way to close its financing gap.

The lawmakers write that this “demonstrates close coordination and communication with the Trump administration, which may have enabled you to receive privileged information about when the Bears Ears announcement would occur.”

The new boundaries opened uranium and vanadium districts the company had been eyeing for years. In a 2017 letter to the Trump administration, Energy Fuels wrote that the monument “could affect existing and future mill operations” and pointed to “many other known uranium and vanadium deposits located within the [original boundaries] that could provide valuable energy and mineral resources in the future.”

The reduction opened districts including White Canyon and Elk Ridge, areas holding multiple ore deposits west of Blanding, Utah. Ore mined there would be trucked to White Mesa, the only conventional uranium mill operating in the country.

Two Utah laws took effect in May that fast-track permits and fund critical mineral processing where the company's mill already operates. On June 18, Energy Fuels secured a $725 million loan from the Defense Department's Office of Strategic Capital, the largest that office had issued at the time. Two weeks after the monument shrank, the company broke ground on a mill expansion.

“After the recent passage of favorable state laws and securing funding from DOD, the final leg in Energy Fuels' quest to gain strategic position in domestic uranium extraction and processing was to attack protections for the land and the sovereign Tribal Nations that steward it,” the lawmakers wrote.

The letter argues the company standing to profit from the monument reduction has spent decades harming the community next door. White Mesa sits a mile from the former boundary and the lawmakers describe a facility that “has become a radioactive dumping ground, taking in waste from Superfund sites, the Manhattan Project, and even foreign countries, all while storing more than 700 million pounds of toxic material in outdated, single-liner pits that threaten nearby tribal communities and groundwater.”

“Energy Fuels cannot credibly claim to be a responsible operator while the nation's last uranium mill functions like an unregulated, bargain-bin waste dump on the doorstep of an Indigenous community,” the lawmakers wrote. “Instead of respecting the Tribes for whom Bears Ears is sacred, you appear to be enriching yourself from their devastation.”

Huffman and Dexter are demanding communications between Energy Fuels and Interior, Agriculture, and Defense officials, both executives' calendars, the company's lobbying contract with Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck LLP, and internal revenue projections tied to redrawing the boundaries.

Read the full letter to Energy Fuels CEO Ross Bhappu here.

title: Huffman, Dexter Open Investigation into Insider Trading at Energy Fuels After Trump Guts Bears Ears

Above: Gottheimer announces funding to help stop violence in North Jersey.

HACKENSACK, NJ — Today, August 10, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) hosted a roundtable at Bergen’s Promise in Hackensack with leaders from Hackensack Meridian Health (HMH), law enforcement, local elected officials, and community stakeholders to discuss domestic violence, shootings, stabbings, and other forms of community violence, and the expansion of hospital-based violence intervention services in Bergen County. Gottheimer clawed back more than $1 million in federal resources to expand HUMC’s Community Health Worker Violence Intervention Program (HVIP). The roundtable discussion focused on the expansion of the program, how the federal funding will expand services for victims and their families, and how it will help reduce community violence in North Jersey.

Watch Gottheimer’s announcement here.

“Keeping Jersey families safe is about as common sense and bipartisan as it gets — and it starts with making sure our hospitals and communities have the tools they need to break the cycle of violence,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “This is exactly the kind of partnership between the federal government, our hospitals, and our community organizations that actually gets things done for people. I’m proud to have fought for this funding. I’m proud it’s coming back to Bergen County where it belongs, and I’m ready to work with all of you to make sure this program succeeds.”

“Community violence isn’t just a public safety issue – it is a public health crisis. At Hackensack Meridian Health, we see the real-world impact of this every day, which is why we are building out our community health worker violence intervention program. By reaching people where they are and providing trauma-informed support, our goal is to break the cycle of violence before it repeats. I want to thank Congressman Gottheimer for pulling this group together. Real, lasting safety happens when healthcare systems, law enforcement, and local advocates sit at the same table and tackle this together,” said Dr. Nicole Harris-Hollingsworth, SVP, Social Impact and Population Health at Hackensack Meridian Health.

Hospital-based violence intervention programs (HVIPs) are multidisciplinary programs that identify patients at risk of repeat violent injury and connect them with hospital and community-based services to support recovery, address underlying risk factors, and work to reduce future victimization. HVIPs begin working with patients while they are still in the emergency department or hospital, then provide intensive community-based case management and support in the months following an injury.

From 2021 through 2026, Hackensack University Medical Center in Bergen County treated almost 3,000 victims of shootings, stabbings, beatings, and domestic violence — accounting for roughly 25 percent of the more than 11,400 violence victims treated across the entire Hackensack Meridian Health network in New Jersey. And these violence intervention programs work: just 5 percent of victims who participate are rehospitalized for another violent injury, compared with 36 percent of those who do not.

The federal funding clawed back by Gottheimer will support trained professionals, technology and supplies, and transportation costs needed to serve victims and families across North Jersey.

Gottheimer was joined by Bergen County Sheriff Anthony Cureton; Bergen County Prosecutor Mark Musella; Bergen County Commissioner Steven A. Tanelli; Dr. Nicole Harris-Hollingsworth, SVP Social Impact and Population Health, HMH; Ms. Sarah Lechner, SVP Chief of External Affairs, HMH; Ms. Leslie Eaddy, Manager, Social Impact and Population Health, HMH; Ms. Angelica Santomauro, Community Health Worker, Social Impact and Population Health, HMH; Ms. Katelyn Segilia, Supervisor, Social Impact and Population Health, HMH; Ms. Omna Syed, Manager, Government Relations, HMH; Dr. Abby Lowe, Assistant Director of Quality, Department of Emergency Medicine, HMH; Dr. Aakash Shah, Program Director, Violence Intervention Programs, HMH; Melissa DeBartolo, Director, Bergen County Department of Human Services; Mr. Dean Paskas, CEO, Bergen’s Promise; Shelisa Foster, Chief Operating Officer, Bergen’s Promise; Ms. Kathryn Werheim, Director of Community Resources, Bergen’s Promise; Ms. Shekinah Williams, Youth Justice Operations Manager, Bergen’s Promise; Ms. Jacqueline Yeboah, Behavioral Health Home Nurse Manager, Bergen’s Promise; Ms. Kelly Kopec, Health Promotion Manager, Bergen’s Promise; Mr. Jacques Hryshko, CEO, Family Connections; Dr. Amanda Santana, COO, Family Connections; Ms. Latisha Miller, Program Coordinator, Family Connections; Ms. Lil Corcoran, CEO, Women’s Rights Information Center; Ms. Lisa Maurer, Associate Executive Director, Women’s Rights Information Center; Ms. Dania Hochberg, Licensed Associate Counselor, Women’s Rights Information Center; Mr. William Salcedo, CEO, Big Brothers Big Sisters of Coastal and Northern New Jersey; Ms. Shannon Orefice, Director of Programs, Big Brothers Big Sisters of Coastal and Northern New Jersey; Ms. Helen Archontou, CEO, YWCA Northern New Jersey; Ms. Monique Joseph, Health Equity Specialist, YWCA Northern New Jersey; Ms. Simaza Sadek, Program Director of healingSPACE, YWCA Northern New Jersey; Ms. Kristine Pendy, CEO, Center for Hope and Safety; Beth Ostuni, Deputy Director of the Division of Alternatives to Domestic Violence; and Kate Gerathy, Advocacy Coordinator, Division of Alternatives to Domestic Violence.

Below: Gottheimer hosts roundtable to help stop violence in North Jersey.

Gottheimer’s remarks as prepared for delivery:

Thank you so much, everybody, for being here today. And a special thank you to the whole team at Hackensack Meridian Health for helping organize today’s discussion, and to Bergen’s Promise for opening up your doors and hosting us. For those of you who don’t know, Bergen’s Promise is a nonprofit that connects children and families with critical mental health, behavioral health, and other support services. We are all very grateful for them.

I want to start by saying how thankful I am to sit down with the people doing this work every single day. The best ideas often don’t come from Washington — they come from the people on the front lines. The doctors, the community health workers, the folks who see community violence up close. You understand these challenges better than most around the country because you’re helping patients and families during some of the most difficult moments of their lives. Let’s talk about why we’re here.

Hackensack University Medical Center is one of the busiest and best hospitals in the state of New Jersey and the country.

In fact, it was just recognized once again by U.S. News & World Report as the number one hospital in New Jersey — a testament to the outstanding care and leadership right here in Bergen County. You provide that top-notch care at your facilities across our great state.

But even one of the nation’s top hospitals, in the ninth safest county in the country, sees the devastating impact of community violence every day. Between 2021 and 2024, Hackensack in Bergen County alone treated more than 2,100 victims of violence — people who came through your doors after shootings, stabbings, and beatings.

In other words, nearly one-quarter of all violence victims treated at HUMC hospitals statewide were treated right here in Bergen County. The bottom line: we are not immune from violence.

Now, the good news: violent crime is down nationally, and it’s down in Jersey. Across the country, violent crime dropped by 5.6 percent this year, and here in New Jersey, violent crime is down more than 16 percent. Two Bergen County communities — Emerson and Allendale — were named among the top ten safest in the entire country.

That’s real progress, and law enforcement and community organizations across Bergen County deserve a lot of credit for helping make our communities safer. As a side note, I also proudly represent most of Sussex County, which is also one of the safest counties in America, with Vernon Township, which has been ranked the safest municipality in our state for three years running. Some of the towns I represent in Passaic County — Ringwood and Wanaque — are always recognized as among the safest, too.

But here’s the thing. Even with crime on the decline, we still have thousands of people walking through the doors of HUMC every year who are victims of violent crime, whether that’s a gunshot wound, a stabbing, or domestic violence. Across the country, more than 44,000 Americans are killed by gun violence every year, and nearly 97,000 more are shot and wounded. In New Jersey, in 2024, 778 people were shot — that’s more than two people every day. Nationally, unintentional and violence-related injuries still cause more than 300,000 deaths a year.

So, the question isn’t whether we’ve made progress. The question is what we do for the people who are still walking through that emergency room door today, and how we stop them from walking back through it again.

That’s what this program is about.

We know that if you were treated for a violent injury once, you are at a much higher risk of being injured again. It’s called repeat victimization, and it’s one of the most frustrating cycles in public health. Hospitals see the same patients come back, again and again. Intervention works — if there is intervention, we see only 5% of victims rehospitalized versus 36% who do not receive these services.

So, the question is: what can you do about it? How do you help break the cycle of violence? Well, that’s why we are here today.

Working closely with Hackensack University Medical Center, I helped claw back more than a million dollars from Washington to Jersey for a new, federally-funded hospital-based violence intervention program, or an HVIP, here in Hackensack. This is a big deal.

HVIPs aren’t new to other hospitals in our state or to Hackensack’s hospitals — but they’ll be new to Hackensack Medical in Bergen County.

With an HVIP, instead of just stitching someone up and sending them back out the door, doctors, nurses, and trained community health workers will meet them right in the emergency department, at their bedside, in the moments immediately after an act of violence, when they’re most vulnerable and most open to accepting help and changing the course of their lives. Hospitals are uniquely positioned to do this work because they’re often the first place victims receive care after experiencing violence.

By connecting patients with support at these critical moments, hospital-based violence intervention programs play a key role in breaking the cycle of repeat victimization before it starts again.

HVIPs work. Since 2021, Project HEAL at Jersey Shore University Medical Center has used this approach in Monmouth and Ocean Counties, and it’s made a real difference. It has helped hundreds of victims of violence access counseling, emergency assistance, transportation, legal services, and other resources that reduce the likelihood of future violence.

What we’re talking about today is bringing that same proven model here to North Jersey, where it’s needed just as much.

Here’s how it works. This funding adds twelve community health workers through the hospital across Bergen County, plus a team leader to coordinate the whole effort. These aren’t bureaucrats. These are trusted, competent, trained professionals — many of them from the very same communities they’re serving — who go to a patient’s bedside, build trust, and then stay with that family long after they leave the hospital.

They assist with housing assistance, food assistance, job training, and mental health support — whatever it takes to help a victim of violence actually recover, not just physically, but mentally, emotionally, and economically, too.

Just to reiterate, of the $1,028,000 we clawed back from Washington to Jersey, $988,000 goes directly to the community health workers, $30,000 will help cover the costs of technology and equipment, and $10,000 to transportation. Every dollar has a purpose, and every dollar makes a difference.

This money isn’t coming out of your state, county, or property taxes. These are your federal tax dollars coming back to Jersey to cover our costs — instead of hitting our local property taxes. And it’s coming back here — not to some Moocher State like Mississippi or Alabama, that often gets back far more than it puts into the federal kitty.

As many of you know, when I first got to Congress, I made it a mission of mine to get more federal dollars back to Jersey. Historically, Moocher States like Mississippi would get about $4.38 back for every dollar they sent to Washington. West Virginia got about $4.23 back.

But New Jersey? We got about 67 cents on the dollar. Now, here in the Fifth Congressional District, we are up more than 357 percent. In the end, that helps lower your taxes and get more bang for the buck. Why should Moocher States get our money instead of it coming back home to you?

My job, and something I take really seriously, is making sure that when your tax dollars go to Washington, as much as possible comes back to North Jersey instead of disappearing into some other state’s budget or some other member’s pet project.

So, when HMH needed additional funding to take on violence and expand this program, I didn’t ask Trenton to raise a tax or ask the county to find room in its budget. I went and got this money back from Washington — dollars that were already yours to begin with.

And I’ll say this, too. HMH isn’t just relying on the federal government to fund this critical work. They’re already investing about $2.2 million a year into violence intervention, with more than 30 team members working on this across the network. That tells you everything you need to know about their commitment.

This federal funding isn’t replacing that. It’s building on top of it, giving them the extra capacity they need to reach the hardest-hit communities.

So, what does success look like a year from now? It looks like fewer repeat victims walking back through that emergency room. It looks like victims and their families getting connected to housing, to jobs, to counseling, instead of falling through the cracks. It looks like Bergen County becoming a model — the same way Project HEAL became one in Monmouth and Ocean Counties — that HMH can expand to other hospitals across its entire network.

To everyone at Hackensack Meridian Health, to everyone at Bergen’s Promise, and to everyone at this table today doing the hard work on the ground — thank you. This is exactly the kind of partnership between the federal government, our hospitals, and our community organizations that actually gets things done for people. I’m proud to have fought for this funding. I’m proud it’s coming back to Bergen County where it belongs, and I’m ready to work with all of you to make sure this program succeeds. There is nothing partisan about it.

If we keep working together to improve our community and keep people safe, in the greatest country in the world, I know that our best days will always be ahead of us.

Thank you.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) co-sponsored the bipartisan, commonsense SCAM Act, a bill that would require social media companies to take action to prevent fraudulent and deceptive ads on their platforms. The bill would also strengthen accountability for those who perpetrate scams , giving the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and state law enforcement agencies more support to enforce consumer protection laws and stop scams from happening.

“Too many Americans are falling for scam advertising on social media, getting ripped off by fraudsters and fake companies,” said Vasquez. “Social media companies should follow the same standards as every other advertiser and verify the authenticity of what they’re promoting. That’s why I strongly support this bill to regulate tech companies and give law enforcement the tools they need to go after scammers.”

Rep. Vasquez has worked to hold social media companies accountable for dangerous behavior on their sites that impacts our communities:

Sent a letter to Big Tech CEOs at Meta, SnapChat, and Telegram demanding that they take action to curb illegal gun sales and cyber bullying on their platforms. This letter was sent after local law enforcement officers flagged illegal gun sales and bullying on these platforms as a driver of youth violence in New Mexico communities.

Cosponsor of the Combating Cartels on Social Media Act to require DHS to develop and implement a national strategy to combat illicit recruitment of American citizens through social media and introduced the No More Narcos Actto create a coordinated educational campaign led by the Department of Justice to teach middle and high school students within 100 miles of the U.S.-Mexico border about the dangers of working with cartels

SupportsSammy’s Law, a bipartisan, commonsense bill to bolster youth online safety by giving parents tools to help ensure their children are not using social media platforms to engage in drug deals and other dangerous behaviors.

The National Law Enforcement Remembrance, Support, and Community Outreach Act, introduced byCongressman Chris Pappas (NH-01), Congressman Troy E. Nehls (TX-22), and Congressman Jimmy Panetta (D-CA-19), passed out of the House Committee on Natural Resources.

This bipartisan legislation would establish a formal program within the U.S. Department of Interior (DOI) to support and enhance the community outreach, public education and officer safety and wellness programs of the National Law Enforcement Museum through grants to the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Fund (NLEOMF). These programs would memorialize and honor law enforcement, compile data on law enforcement fatalities and injuries, increase public understanding of and support for law enforcement, enhance and improve law enforcement officer safety and wellness, and bring law enforcement closer to the communities they serve.

“Every day our law enforcement answers the call to serve and keep our communities safe, putting their lives on the line to do so. We must always support their critical work and honor those that give the ultimate sacrifice,” said Congressman Pappas. “This bipartisan legislation would support efforts to honor law enforcement officers killed in the line of duty, commemorate their legacies of service and sacrifice, and strengthen officer safety and wellbeing. I remain committed to supporting our law enforcement and the important work they do for Granite Staters.”

The National Law Enforcement Remembrance, Support and Community Outreach Act is supported by NLEMOF’s board member organizations, including the Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association, Fraternal Order of Police, Fraternal Order of Police Auxiliary, International Brotherhood of Police Officers, International Union of Police Associations/AFL-CIO, Motorola Solutions, Verizon, National Association of Police Organizations, National Sheriffs’ Associations, COPS, DuPont, National Black Police Association, National Organization of Black Law Enforcement Executives, National Policing Institute, National Troopers Coalition, Police Executive Research Forum, Police Unity Tour, and the United Federation of Police Officers.

Created by an Act of Congress in 1984, NLEOMF operates the National Law Enforcement Museum and the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial. NLEOMF’s mission is to honor fallen law enforcement officers, tell the story of our nation’s law enforcement officers, and make it safer for law enforcement.
title: PASSED OUT OF COMMITTEE: Pappas’s Bipartisan Bill to Honor Fallen Law Enforcement, Strengthen Officer Safety

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Representative Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA), with Senators Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), and Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and Representatives Maggie Goodlander (D-NH), Delia Ramirez (D-IL), and Lizzie Fletcher (D-TX) led a bicameral letter pressing the Department of Defense (DoD), the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Veterans Affairs (VA), U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) on their efforts to coordinate to arrest, and detain, and deport hundreds of veterans and military families. In April 2025, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) rescinded its long-standing policy that treated military service a “significant mitigating factor” when deciding whether to pursue immigration enforcement, and replaced it with a new policy stating that military service alone “does not automatically exempt” non-citizens from enforcement actions.

In September 2025, Rep. Houlahan, Sen. Warren, and other lawmakers opened an investigation into the impacts of these policy changes on military families. The investigation revealed that ICE has attempted to deport 282 veterans and their relatives. But DHS refused to disclose the number of active-duty troops and their families who have been threatened by the administration’s policy.

But new reports indicate that DoD and DHS appear to be coordinating to convert military bases into “traps” for individuals this administration deems deportable and has detained non-citizens during routine check-ins, visits, and drop-offs at or near military installations. At the same time, DoD has continued to recruit new service members with the promise of immigration protections.

Recent reporting by the Associated Press reveals that, since January 2025, more than 50 parents and spouses of active-duty service members have been detained, and at least six have been deported. ICE’s statistics show that the agency has arrested 16 non-citizen armed forces members since the beginning of Fiscal Year 2026. Some service members have reportedly needed to take leave or delay deployment because ICE detained their families.

“These efforts imperil military readiness, weaken service members’ morale, and betray America’s promises to the people who put their lives on the line for our nation,” wrote the lawmakers. Alarmingly, DoD has been reportedly targeting individuals at military installations, detaining them on military property, and turning them over to ICE — effectively converting military bases into “traps” for noncitizens. For example, a 22-year-old military wife was recently detained while attempting to obtain a military spouse I.D. Military officials allegedly called DHS and held her in a room until ICE agents arrived to take her to a detention center.

“DoD’s participation in civil immigration enforcement activities raises both ethical and legal concerns, including potential violations of the Posse Comitatus Act, which prohibits using the armed forces of the military for civilian law enforcement,” wrote the lawmakers.

The coalition warned that if service members were to be swept up in any of these enforcement actions, it could separately constitute a violation of the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, which provides protections to all members of the United States military on active duty, including non-citizens, from civil actions—such as immigration proceedings—that interfere with their military duties.

“Service members must have confidence that their sacrifices will be honored, not used against them or to target their loved ones,” wrote the lawmakers. “DoD’s new anti-immigrant practices risk deterring future recruits and damaging the credibility of military recruitment efforts—which promised to care for service members even after their time in uniform.”

The lawmakers requested that the agencies explain the enhanced coordination between DoD and DHS, restore long-standing immigration protections for family members of service members, and explain what steps they are taking to protect troops, veterans, and their families from unjust immigration enforcement by August 23, 2026.

The letter was signed by Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.).

Representatives Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.), Nanette Barragán (D-Calif.), André Carson (D-Ind.), Greg Casar (D-Texas), Sean Casten (D-Ill.), Joaquin Castro (D-Texas), Gil Cisneros (D-Calif.), Bonnie Watson Coleman (D-N.J.), Daniel Davis (D-Ill.), Madeleine Dean (D-Pa.), Diana DeGette (D-Colo.), Mark DeSaulnier (D-Calif.), Maxine Dexter (D-Ore.), Veronica Escobar (D-Texas), Bill Foster (D-Ill.), Maxwell Frost (D-Fla.), Chuy García (D-Ill.), Sylvia Garcia (D-Texas), Adelita Grijalva (D-Ariz.), Jonathan Jackson (D-Ill.), Hank Johnson (D-Ga.), Ro Khanna (D-Calif.), John Larson (D-Conn.), Stephen Lynch (D-Mass.), Seth Magaziner (D-R.I.), Seth Moulton (D-Mass.), Kevin Mullin (D-Calif.), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.), Mike Quigley (D-Ill.), Jan Schakowsky (D-Ill.), Lateefah Simon (D-Calif.), Marilyn Strickland (D-Wash.), Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.), Mark Takano (D-Calif.), Dina Titus (D-Nev.), Marc Veasey (D-Texas), Maxine Waters (D-Calif.), and Gabe Vasquez (D-N.M.), joined in signing the letter.

The letter was endorsed by the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), Immigration Defenders Law Center, the Seattle Clemency Project, Common Defense, Repatriate Our Patriots, and League of United Latin American Citizens.

"It is hard to imagine a more profound betrayal than targeting service members, veterans, and military families for deportation,” said Jennie Pasquarella, interim executive director of the Seattle Clemency Project. "This administration is abandoning decades of bipartisan policies that recognized a simple truth: protecting those who serve makes our military stronger and our nation safer. Targeting the very communities that have sacrificed for this country is not just morally indefensible, it is a direct attack on military readiness, recruitment, and trust."

"This administration has made a conscious decision to abandon its promises to military families and fail those who put their lives on the line for our nation,” said Amanda Schuft, director of legal services at Immigrant Defenders Law Center. “We have seen the devastating human cost firsthand. Our client, the father of an active-duty Army service member, was detained by ICE despite suffering from terminal renal failure, forcing his son to take leave from military service to plead for his release and provide evidence of his grave medical condition. The government ignored those pleas. After his health deteriorated in detention, our client was eventually released, only to die within weeks.”

“Family readiness directly impacts mission readiness. Behind every military spouse or parent in detention is a servicemember who could deploy at any moment. Without a strong homefront, we cannot have a ready force. Our government must honor its commitments to those who serve,” said Danitza G. James, MSW, President, Repatriate Our Patriots.

--end--
title: Rep. Houlahan, Sen. Warren, Lawmakers Slam Trump Admin for Efforts to Tear Apart Military Families, Convert Military Bases Into “Traps” for Non-Citizens

Washington, D.C. – Today, Representatives Jared Huffman (D-CA) and Vern Buchanan (R-FL) re-introduced the Critically Endangered Animals Conservation Act, a bipartisan bill to support conservation efforts for highly endangered species around the world.

“The alarming acceleration in species extinction has serious consequences not only for ecosystems and wildlife, butfor our economies, communities, and the future generations that will be robbed of the rich biodiversity and species we depend on today,” said Rep. Huffman. “Our bill will bring the U.S. back as a partner on the global stage to reverse the extinction crisis and support conservation projects for the world’s most vulnerable species. This is a moral and economic imperative that we cannot ignore.”

“Allowing a species to become extinct is a tragedy we should do everything in our power to prevent. This important bill will support vital conservation projects around the world and help save some of the world’s most threatened animals. The competitive grant program created by this bill will ensure that every dollar goes towards worthwhile projects that protect endangered wildlife,” said Rep. Buchanan.

This legislation would establish funding for the Critically Endangered Animals Conservation Fund, to be administered by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service as part of the successful Multinational Species Conservation Funds. This bill will re-inject U.S. support into the global fight to conserve thousands of the world’s most vulnerable species, such as snow leopards, Andean cats, African penguins, the white-backed vulture, and countless others that need active help to prevent further loss in the wild.

AGUADA, Puerto Rico – El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, destacó que su oficina ha anunciado más de $1.7 billones en fondos federales para municipios de la Isla, durante su participación hoy en un encuentro de la Asociación de Alcaldes de Puerto Rico celebrado en Aguada.

Durante el encuentro, el Comisionado Residente dialogó con los alcaldes sobre las necesidades prioritarias de sus comunidades y las oportunidades disponibles para financiar proyectos de infraestructura, desarrollo económico, turismo y servicios municipales mediante programas federales.

“Los municipios conocen de primera mano las necesidades de sus comunidades. Nuestro trabajo es ayudarlos a convertir esas prioridades en proyectos competitivos y conectarlos con los recursos federales necesarios para hacerlos realidad”, expresó el Comisionado Residente.

La agenda reunió a representantes del Cuerpo de Ingenieros del Ejército de los Estados Unidos (USACE), Rural Development del Departamento de Agricultura federal (USDA), Estudios Técnicos Inc, Invest Puerto Rico y Discover Puerto Rico, entre otras entidades.

Las conversaciones se concentraron en identificar oportunidades de financiamiento, fortalecer la coordinación entre los municipios y las agencias, y adelantar iniciativas relacionadas con infraestructura, turismo, innovación tecnológica y crecimiento económico.

"Hasta la fecha, hemos anunciado más de $1.7 billones en fondos federales para municipios de Puerto Rico. Mi compromiso es seguir trabajando para que esos recursos continúen llegando a las comunidades y se traduzcan en más oportunidades para nuestra gente", expresó el Comisionado Residente.

La cifra incluye subvenciones y otras asignaciones provenientes de la Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias (FEMA), destinadas a proyectos y servicios municipales.

Como parte de su gestión en Washington, la oficina del Comisionado Residente continuará ofreciendo apoyo a los municipios para identificar programas federales, atender obstáculos en los procesos de solicitud y promover proyectos que mejoren la infraestructura y los servicios que reciben los ciudadanos.

Toledo, OH – Today, Co-Founder and Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Emeritus Congressman Michael McCaul (TX-10), Former Majority Leader of the House of Representatives Congressman Steny Hoyer (MD-05), and Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus Congressman Joe Wilson (SC-02) introduced the bipartisanLindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 alongside 12 of their colleagues. This legislation — which honors the late Senator Lindsey Graham, who worked on the bill for more than a year and secured the White House’s support — will hold major purchasers of Russian oil and gas accountable for supporting Russia’s war against Ukraine and extend sanctions that restrict funding for Iran’s energy and weapons sectors.

“Dictator Vladimir Putin’s illegal invasion of Ukraine is failing—Ukraine is battering Russian war infrastructure and the Kremlin is losing tens of thousands of troops each month. Now is the time to intensify pressure on Putin through crippling sanctions while surging support for our Ukrainian allies,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). “Putin will not make peace until he is forced to. I have been a supporter of every bipartisan sanctions bill on the table to pressure Russia to end its illegal full-scale invasion, and I am confident that the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 will accomplish that mission. Designed to protect our allies who aid Ukraine while squeezing Putin and the countries that enable his invasion, the sweeping sanctions and targeted tariffs in this bill are the best chance we have to get bipartisan legislation signed into law to hold Russia accountable and achieve peace.”

“Senator Graham was a national security giant, a statesman of unmatched conviction, and a personal friend and mentor. We shared a fundamental worldview: America is strongest at home when it projects strength abroad. That’s why he fought so hard for this bill, which I promised him months ago I would introduce in the House,” said Congressman Michael McCaul (TX-10). “As President Zelensky told me last month when I visited Ukraine, he is ready for a ceasefire — ready to negotiate, as he has been for years. Putin, on the other hand, consistently defies President Trump and the international community by refusing to come to the table. I can think of no better way to honor Senator Graham’s life and legacy than by passing these tough sanctions, which will help force Putin into negotiations and bring us closer to securing Lindsey’s vision of enduring peace in two critical regions of the world.”

“Democracy is presently under threat from despotism, and Congress must act to defend democracy and help Ukraine defeat Vladimir Putin’s effort to extinguish its liberty and sovereignty. Our legislation goes after multiple sources of Russian war funding, including its oil and gas sectors, shadow fleet, and financial institutions. I’m encouraged that the Senate passed the companion legislation last week with overwhelming support, and I thank former Chairman McCaul for partnering with me to facilitate action by the House. This action has been delayed too long and will, hopefully, accelerate Ukraine’s success and the ending of this war, one that was initiated illegally by Putin and that has resulted in tens of thousands of deaths of Russians and Ukrainians. I hope that we can secure bipartisan consensus in the House and enact a sanctions package that will stem the flow of money to Russia’s war machine and contribute to a Ukrainian victory," said Congressman Steny Hoyer (MD-05).

"Senator Lindsey Graham and I shared the belief that opposing dictators in defense of freedom and liberty is always the right thing to do. War criminal Putin is losing his invasion of sovereign Ukraine and the threat to humanity posed by the Iranian regime is dire. It is time for Congress to give President Trump the strongest tools available to choke off Russia's war machine for the good of mankind and cripple the ability of Tehran to continue sowing chaos in the region and beyond. My friend and colleague worked tirelessly in championing these critical initiatives, and I am grateful to help advance them across the finish line in the House,” said Congressman Joe Wilson (SC-02).

Earlier this month, an overwhelming bipartisan majority in the Senate voted to pass companion legislation, by a vote of 86-11, led by Sens. Darline Graham (R-SC), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Katie Britt (R-AL), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Chair of the Senate Armed Services Committee Roger Wicker (R-MS), and Chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee Jim Risch (R-ID). The text of the House bill is identical to the text that passed the Senate.

“This legislation was deeply important to my brother, Lindsey, and I’m grateful that it has achieved such a wide coalition of support. Lindsey was committed to achieving a peaceful resolution to this war, and I’m confident that these sanctions will pave the way,” said Senator Darline Graham (R-SC). “I’m grateful to Rep. McCaul for leading this effort in the House. The Senate came together in a strong, bipartisan fashion to pass the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, and I hope the House of Representatives will do the same. Russia has waged war against Ukraine for far too long, and this bill assists President Trump in his noble efforts to bring it to a close.”

“Representatives McCaul, Hoyer, Wilson, Kaptur, and Fitzpatrick are longtime champions of Ukraine’s cause and I am glad to have them leading our legislation in the House of Representatives. After a massive bipartisan vote in the Senate, we are eager to turn to the House as we fight to get this legislation across the finish line. There is immense urgency in getting this done – July set a record for Russia’s use of ballistic missiles, killing and wounding dozens of Ukrainians, including many children. Cutting off the source of funding – profits from oil and gas – for these deadly weapons and Russia’s war machine is essential to ending the bloodshed,” said Senator Blumenthal (D-CT).

Joining Kaptur, McCaul, Hoyer, and Wilson as original cosponsors are Co-Chair of the House Baltic Caucus Congressman Don Bacon (NE-02), Congressman Jake Auchincloss (MA-04), House Armed Services Committee Chairman Congressman Mike Rogers (AL-03), Congresswoman Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Congressman Mike Turner (OH-10), Congressman Gabe Vasquez (NM-02), Congresswoman Ann Wagner (MO-02), Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), Congressman Andy Barr (KY-06), Congressman Ed Case (HI-01); Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Congressman Eugene Vindman (VA-07), Congressman Nathaniel Moran (TX-01), and Congresswoman Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06).

“Putin’s illegal war is failing, but he will not choose peace until the cost becomes too high for Russia and those helping fund his brutality,” said Congressman Don Bacon (NE-02). “Senator Lindsey Graham was one of Congress’s clearest voices for Ukraine, understood that Putin only responds to strength, and worked until his final days to advance the toughest sanctions package yet against Russia’s war machine. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act would impose crippling pressure on Russia and those enabling Putin’s aggression, honor Sen. Graham’s commitment to Ukraine’s fight for freedom, and make clear that America stands with Ukraine.”

“Since 2022, I have called on both Biden and Trump to empower Ukraine to win this war through both strikes and sanctions on Russian oil infrastructure. The strikes are finally happening, and with this bill the sanctions are coming,” said Congressman Jake Auchincloss (MA-04).

"I am proud to join in introducing this legislation to sanction Vladimir Putin and his thugs as well as the Iran and its terrorist regime,” said Congressman Mike Rogers (AL-03). “Every dollar denied to Vladimir Putin weakens his war machine. By choking off the oil and gas revenue fueling Russia's aggression, this legislation gives President Trump powerful leverage to force Putin into serious negotiations that deliver a truly lasting peace. Including additional sanctions on Iran is equally critical given the terrorist regime’s continued threats to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and its role in enabling Russia’s war against Ukraine. This legislation strengthens America’s hand against adversaries who threaten American security, our allies, and global stability.”

"It is long past time for Congress to impose tougher consequences on Russia and those financing its illegal war against Ukraine. I'm proud to support this updated legislation, which targets major purchasers of Russian oil and gas that continue to fund the Kremlin's aggression. This war has resulted in an estimated 2 million casualties, including more than half a million deaths. The United States must continue standing with the Ukrainian people and keep the pressure on Russia to agree to a just and lasting peace that preserves a free, sovereign, and independent Ukraine,” said Congresswoman Jill Tokuda (HI-02).

“For more than four years, the Ukrainian people have fought courageously to defend their sovereignty, and their resolve is paying off. Lindsey Graham understood that standing with nations fighting for freedom strengthens America’s own security, and until his final days, he was pressing for stronger sanctions against Russia,” said Congressman Mike Turner (OH-10). “This legislation honors that legacy, sends a clear message to Vladimir Putin that he cannot outlast Ukraine or the free world, and gives President Trump another powerful tool to pressure Russia, bring Putin to the negotiating table, and help restore peace to the region.”

“To end Russia’s unprovoked and deadly invasion of Ukraine, we must enact maximum financial pain on Vladimir Putin and his cronies. I will not stand idly by while countless people are killed due to Putin’s doomed quest to reconstitute the Soviet Union. I am beyond proud to join my colleagues in introducing this sweeping sanctions legislation that will enact severe financial penalties against Putin, his allies, and those who choose to do business with him. The largest war in Europe since World War II must come to an end, and I am confident these measures will accelerate that process. I am also pleased this bill extends the Iran Sanctions Act to ensure all available measures are available to cripple the terrorist Iranian regime. These necessary sanctions are a fitting legacy to honor the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a friend and colleague who continually fought for freedom, democracy, and against tyrannical regimes like Russia and Iran,” said Congresswoman Ann Wagner (MO-02).

"Vladimir Putin and the regime in Tehran are two of the gravest threats to America and our allies. For far too long, they've bankrolled their aggression by selling oil and gas to whoever will buy it,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05). "This bipartisan legislation cuts off those funding streams: holding accountable anyone who fills Putin's war chest as he wages his brutal, illegal war against Ukraine, and choking off the money that fuels Iran's weapons programs and its terror proxies. I was proud to see the Senate pass this bill with an overwhelming, bipartisan majority, and now it's on the House to finish the job. I can think of no better tribute to Senator Lindsey Graham — a national security champion — than enacting the tough sanctions he fought so hard for. Standing up to tyrants isn't a Democratic or Republican issue; it's an American one."

“By targeting the energy revenues and financial networks that fuel Putin’s war machine and enable the Iranian regime’s terrorist activities, this bipartisan legislation strengthens America’s ability to impose real economic consequences on our adversaries,” said Congressman Andy Barr (KY-06). “Senator Graham understood that harnessing America’s full strength from our financial system to our military is essential to deterring aggression, defending our allies, and advancing peace. I’m proud to join my colleagues to help carry forward that legacy.”

“Senator Graham believed, as I do, that American strength remains the surest guardian of peace,” said Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01). “That conviction guided our work together on this legislation. Putin’s war machine runs on oil, money, and the willingness of others to look the other way—and the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 attacks all three. It isolates Russia’s banks, shuts down the networks financing its aggression, and forces every government and company enabling this war to make a choice. By increasing the cost of Putin’s war and reducing his ability to sustain it, this legislation strengthens the path to a just and lasting peace—one determined by Ukraine, not imposed by Moscow. The most fitting tribute Congress can offer Lindsey is to finish the work he began, carry forward the cause of freedom he championed, and make clear that America’s resolve will endure until that peace is secured.”

“Supporting a strong, free Ukraine is imperative for the national security of our communities here at home. Sanctioning Russia and Putin sends a direct message to the world: the United States will not sit by while brutal regimes bankroll aggression against democratic nations,” said Congressman Eugene Vindman (VA-07). “I am proud to be a co-sponsor of this essential legislation. We must continue to escalate the economic pressure on the Kremlin and strengthen our resolve for the Ukrainian people as they fight for their freedom, sovereignty, and security.”

"Russia is perpetrating a war of aggression, and we must keep the pressure on Vladimir Putin. This action is long overdue, but we are finally moving forward with the resolve this moment demands. These sanctions will erode Russia's war machine by cutting off the revenue that funds it. We must hold those who are fueling this war accountable. These sanctions focus on Russia but will also target dangerous Chinese entities which support the Russian defense industrial base. Peace is the goal, and these mechanisms give the President the tools to achieve that goal,” said Congressman Nathaniel Moran (TX-07).

“For more than four years, Ukrainians have courageously defended their freedom against Putin’s brutal invasion. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act would increase pressure on the Kremlin, hold those supporting its war accountable, and strengthen Ukraine’s position in pursuit of a just peace," said Congresswoman Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06). “The bill also extends longstanding sanctions against Iran. Sanctions cannot replace a clear strategy or the President’s obligation to seek congressional authorization for war, but they remain an important diplomatic tool. I am proud to cosponsor this legislation.”

Click here to read full text of the legislation.
title: Kaptur, McCaul, Hoyer, Wilson, Colleagues Introduce the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026

WASHINGTON – Today, Rep. Greg Casar (D-TX) led 21 members of Congress demanding OpenAI disclose additional information about the company’s disclosure that Anthropic models have, in three separate incidents, hacked unsuspecting companies without Anthropic’s knowledge.

In a letter to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, the members write: “While Anthropic has disclosed some information about these incidents, you have yet to release the relevant logs, and significant questions remain unanswered. Given the serious risk that frontier AI models can pose, it is imperative we have a detailed understanding of how this security incident unfolded, including any potential negligence on the part of Anthropic.”

The members demand that Amodei release the logs regarding the incident and answer a series of detailed oversight questions including: whether or internal or external actors wanted the company about the risk of such an incident; why Anthropic’s evaluation partner failed to detect the incident; at what point the company could have halted the incident; what steps Anthropic is taking to ensure another incident like this does not happen again; what is known about the objective of each model that hacked another company; and details about Anthropic’s disclosure that Claude “tried and failed” to get real money.

A full copy of the letter is available here.

The letter to Anthropic is co-led by Rep. Doris Matsui (D-CA) and signed by U.S. Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Becca Balint (VT-AL), Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), April McClain Delaney (MD-06), Bill Foster (IL-11), Valerie P. Foushee (NC-04), Jesús G. "Chuy" García (IL-04), Sylvia R. Garcia (TX-29), Adelita S. Grijalva (AZ-07), Jonathan L. Jackson (IL-01), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Summer L. Lee (PA-12), Stephen F. Lynch (MA-08), Jennifer L. McClellan (VA-04), James P. McGovern (MA-02), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Patrick Ryan (NY-18), and Nydia M. Velázquez (NY-07).

###

Congressman Greg Casar represents Texas’s 35th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, which runs down I-35 from East Austin to Hays County to the West Side of San Antonio. A labor organizer and son of Mexican immigrants, Casar serves as the Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus for the 119th Congress. He also serves on the Committee on Education and Labor and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability.
title: Casar Leads Demand for Information from Anthropic About Security Incidents

AKRON, OHIO — Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) announced that the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has awarded $400,000 in continuation funding for Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services to Ohio's 13th Congressional District. The funding, awarded to Oriana House, supports the Akron Municipal Recovery Court and the Summit County Turning Point Collaborative Drug Court Program, which serve individuals with mental illnesses or substance abuse disorders who come into contact with the justice system.

"Programs that support individuals with mental illness in the criminal justice system are essential for breaking the cycle of incarceration and promoting recovery. Investing $400,000 to expand programs like Summit County's Valor Court to support veterans and the PIVOT Drug Court to support individuals with substance abuse issues creates a more just and humane system that prioritizes rehabilitation and reintegration into society," said Rep. Sykes.

“Thank you to Congresswoman Emilia Sykes for the continuation of this important funding, used in part to support Summit County’s only adult felony drug court program, Turning Point,” said Judge Joy Malek Oldfield. “This funding strengthens access to treatment and recovery support, and assists our participants working towards stability and sobriety. Judge Oldfield and the Summit County Turning Point Program are grateful to work alongside Congresswoman Sykes, the Oriana House, Judge Jon Oldham and Akron Recovery Court towards a stronger, safer and healthier community.”

For more information about grant opportunities and assistance, visit sykes.house.gov/services/grants-and-federal-funding.
title: Rep. Sykes Announces $400,000 for Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services in Ohio’s 13th District

text:
Huffman, Dexter Open Investigation into Insider Trading at Energy Fuels After Trump Guts Bears Ears
Energy Fuels CEO bought 74,000 shares days before the monument was cut by 90 percent, the largest insider purchase in company history
Washington, D.C. – Today, House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) and Oversight & Investigations Subcommittee Ranking Member Maxine Dexter (D-Ore.) opened an investigation into potential insider trading at Energy Fuels Inc., after the company's CEO and Chairman of the Board bought company stock days before President Trump announced he was shrinking Bears Ears National Monument by more than 90 percent.
On July 7, 2026, CEO Ross Bhappu purchased 74,000 shares, the largest insider purchase of stock in the company's history, increasing his ownership by 41 percent. Chairman Bruce Hansen purchased 4,000 shares the next day. On July 13, Trump opened nearly 3 million acres of federal land to mining, including uranium-rich areas of the San Juan Basin that had previously been protected.
“The timing of these stock purchases indicate that nonpublic information was potentially available to both you and Mr. Hansen,” the lawmakers wrote to Bhappu.
The lawmakers argue Energy Fuels' relationships with the administration put its executives in position to learn of the decision early and potentially profit from it. The company hired outside lobbyists that included a former Trump Interior official, identified strong government support as a selling point to investors in its expansion plans, and cited ongoing discussions with government sources as a way to close its financing gap. 
The lawmakers write that this “demonstrates close coordination and communication with the Trump administration, which may have enabled you to receive privileged information about when the Bears Ears announcement would occur.”
The new boundaries opened uranium and vanadium districts the company had been eyeing for years. In a 2017 letter to the Trump administration, Energy Fuels wrote that the monument “could affect existing and future mill operations” and pointed to “many other known uranium and vanadium deposits located within the [original boundaries] that could provide valuable energy and mineral resources in the future.”
The reduction opened districts including White Canyon and Elk Ridge, areas holding multiple ore deposits west of Blanding, Utah. Ore mined there would be trucked to White Mesa, the only conventional uranium mill operating in the country.
Two Utah laws took effect in May that fast-track permits and fund critical mineral processing where the company's mill already operates. On June 18, Energy Fuels secured a $725 million loan from the Defense Department's Office of Strategic Capital, the largest that office had issued at the time. Two weeks after the monument shrank, the company broke ground on a mill expansion.
“After the recent passage of favorable state laws and securing funding from DOD, the final leg in Energy Fuels' quest to gain strategic position in domestic uranium extraction and processing was to attack protections for the land and the sovereign Tribal Nations that steward it,” the lawmakers wrote.
The letter argues the company standing to profit from the monument reduction has spent decades harming the community next door. White Mesa sits a mile from the former boundary and the lawmakers describe a facility that “has become a radioactive dumping ground, taking in waste from Superfund sites, the Manhattan Project, and even foreign countries, all while storing more than 700 million pounds of toxic material in outdated, single-liner pits that threaten nearby tribal communities and groundwater.”
“Energy Fuels cannot credibly claim to be a responsible operator while the nation's last uranium mill functions like an unregulated, bargain-bin waste dump on the doorstep of an Indigenous community,” the lawmakers wrote. “Instead of respecting the Tribes for whom Bears Ears is sacred, you appear to be enriching yourself from their devastation.”
Huffman and Dexter are demanding communications between Energy Fuels and Interior, Agriculture, and Defense officials, both executives' calendars, the company's lobbying contract with Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck LLP, and internal revenue projections tied to redrawing the boundaries.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Frank Pallone, Jr. (NJ-06) joined members of the New Jersey congressional delegation in urging President Donald J. Trump to approve Governor Mikie Sherrill’s appeal of FEMA’s denial of the State’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration following the devastating February 22–23, 2026, winter storm. New Jersey submitted its original request for federal disaster assistance on April 7, 2026, and FEMA denied that request on July 2, 2026.

“According to data from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, approximately 24 inches of snow fell in less than 24 hours across eastern and central New Jersey, and eight of the State’s 21 counties recorded record or near-record snowfall totals and qualify as ‘core counties’ as laid out by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) in the Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG). Another four counties met the ‘contiguous county’ requirements for snow assistance outlined in the PAPPG,” wrote the lawmakers.

The lawmakers’ latest appeal follows a bipartisan April 21 letter from the delegation pressing the Administration to approve the State’s initial request, citing the storm’s deadly impacts, widespread outages affecting more than 127,000 customers, hundreds of accidents, and nearly $100 million in statewide damages. The February storm claimed 12 lives across nine counties, caused extensive power outages, and inflicted significant damage to homes, businesses, and critical infrastructure—costs that New Jerseyans should not be forced to shoulder alone.

Preliminary damage assessments for Public Assistance teams documented significant emergency work and damage to public facilities and infrastructure across 19 counties. The storm further strained New Jersey’s emergency response capacity, which was already stretched after the State responded to a major snow and ice storm just weeks earlier and managed six active federal disaster declarations.

“A careful review of the State of New Jersey’s appeal demonstrates that this request far exceeds all Stafford Act statutory and regulatory thresholds. The extent of the damage, the operational burden throughout the State, and the cumulative impacts of recent and related extreme weather all provide overwhelming evidence that New Jersey’s request must be granted,” wrote the lawmakers.

In addition to Pallone, the letter was signed by Senators Booker and Kim, New Jersey U.S. Representatives Donald Norcross (D-NJ-1), Herb Conaway Jr. (D-NJ-3), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5), Robert Menendez (D-NJ-8), Nellie Pou (D-NJ-9), LaMonica McIver (D-NJ-10), Analilia Mejia (D-NJ-11), and Bonnie Watson Coleman (D-NJ-12).

(Rochester, N.Y.)—Today, Congressman Joe Morelle reintroduced the Summer Meals and Learning Act, legislation he authored to help children continue learning while ensuring they have access to nutritious meals during the summer months. The bill would establish a new federal grant program supporting reading programs at schools that serve as summer meal sites, helping students stay engaged academically even after the school year ends.

"Summer break should never mean a child falls behind in school or goes without a healthy meal," said Congressman Joe Morelle. "For too many families, that's exactly what's happening. This bill is a simple idea with a real impact: keep kids connected to books, keep school libraries open, and make sure they have healthy meals while they're there. I'm proud to partner with Senator Merkley once again to give more children the support they need to learn, grow, and succeed."

For many children, school provides far more than classroom instruction. It's where they can find books to read, adults who encourage them to keep learning, and dependable access to healthy meals. When summer arrives, too many of those supports disappear—especially in communities where families have fewer opportunities to fill the gap.

Research has shown the consequences can last well beyond the summer months. By fifth grade, students without access to summer learning opportunities can be as much as two years behind their peers.

The Summer Meals and Learning Act would establish a grant program through the U.S. Department of Education to help State libraries partner with schools on summer reading programs. Schools would qualify if they:

Operate a summer meal program; and

Serve student populations where at least 50 percent of children are reading below grade level or are at risk of reading below grade level.

By bringing books and meals together in one place, the legislation would help more children return to school in the fall healthy, engaged, and ready to learn.

To learn more about the Summer Meals and Learning Act, read the full text of the legislation here.
